name.en: Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan
name.zh: 特奥蒂瓦坎太阳金字塔

summary.en: Around 200 CE Teotihuacan completed the Pyramid of the Sun, about 65 m high and set over a man-made cave, on its great north–south axis, the Street of the Dead. It is among the largest structures ever built in the pre-Columbian Americas.
summary.zh: 约公元200年，特奥蒂瓦坎在其南北大轴线“亡者大道”旁建成太阳金字塔。塔高约65米，建于一处人工洞穴之上，是前哥伦布时代美洲最大的建筑之一。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Pyramid of the Sun
UNESCO World Heritage: Pre-Hispanic City of Teotihuacan
George L. Cowgill, Ancient Teotihuacan: Early Urbanism in Central Mexico (2015)

note: Construction is dated by ceramics and radiocarbon to roughly 100–250 CE; 200 is a conventional midpoint.

story.en:
Teotihuacan grew in the first two centuries CE from a cluster of villages into a planned city laid out on a grid oriented about 15.5° east of north. The Pyramid of the Sun was its first giant monument: a core of rubble and earth faced with stone, raised over a tunnel that leads to a chamber beneath the centre. Excavators have suggested that the cave, perhaps seen as a place of origin, was the reason the pyramid stands where it does.

At its height around 400–550 the city held perhaps 100,000 people, many living in walled apartment compounds, some of them inhabited by migrants from Oaxaca and the Gulf Coast. Its own name is unknown. Centuries after it fell, the Aztecs visited the ruins as a holy place and called it Teotihuacan, "where the gods were born", and named its avenue and pyramids.
story.zh:
公元1至2世纪，特奥蒂瓦坎由若干村落发展为一座按网格规划的城市，轴线偏北约15.5度向东。太阳金字塔是它的第一座巨型建筑：以碎石和泥土为核心，外砌石块，建在一条通向中心下方石室的隧道之上。发掘者认为，这个或许被视为起源之地的洞穴，正是金字塔选址于此的原因。

约400至550年鼎盛时，城中人口或达10万，许多人住在有围墙的公寓式院落里，其中一些院落居住着来自瓦哈卡和墨西哥湾沿岸的移民。这座城市原本的名字已无从得知。它衰落数百年后，阿兹特克人把废墟当作圣地朝拜，称之为“特奥蒂瓦坎”，意为“众神诞生之地”，并为大道和金字塔命名。

name.en: Temple of the Feathered Serpent dedicated

summary.en: In the Ciudadela at Teotihuacan builders raised a stepped temple carved with feathered serpents and headdress masks. More than 130 sacrificed people, many dressed as warriors, were buried under and around it at its dedication.
summary.zh: 特奥蒂瓦坎在“城堡”广场建起一座阶梯神庙，饰有羽蛇与头饰面具浮雕。落成时有130多名献祭者被埋在神庙之下和四周，其中许多人身着武士装束。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Temple of the Feathered Serpent, Teotihuacan
Saburo Sugiyama, Human Sacrifice, Militarism, and Rulership: Materialization of State Ideology at the Feathered Serpent Pyramid, Teotihuacan (2005)
Michael D. Coe & Rex Koontz, Mexico: From the Olmecs to the Aztecs (7th ed., 2013)

note: Dated to c. 200–250 CE. A tunnel beneath the temple, explored from 2003 by Sergio Gómez, contained tens of thousands of offerings.

name.en: Abandonment of El Mirador (Preclassic Maya collapse)
name.zh: 埃尔米拉多尔被弃（前古典期玛雅崩溃）

summary.en: El Mirador in northern Petén, whose La Danta complex is one of the largest pyramid platforms in the world, was largely abandoned around 150 CE, along with other giant Preclassic Maya centres. Environmental degradation and shifting trade are among the proposed causes.
summary.zh: 位于佩滕北部的埃尔米拉多尔，其拉丹塔建筑群是世界上体量最大的金字塔平台之一。约公元150年，它与其他大型前古典期玛雅中心一同基本被弃，原因可能包括环境退化与贸易格局变化。

sources.title: Wikipedia: El Mirador
Robert J. Sharer & Loa P. Traxler, The Ancient Maya (6th ed., 2006)
Richard D. Hansen, "The Beginning of the End: Conspicuous Consumption and Environmental Impact of the Preclassic Lowland Maya" (2012)

note: The decline is dated broadly to the 1st–2nd centuries CE; a smaller Late Classic reoccupation followed.

name.zh: “陌生人到来”：特奥蒂瓦坎势力入主蒂卡尔

summary.en: In January 378 a war leader named Siyaj K'ahk', linked to Teotihuacan, reached Tikal; its king Chak Tok Ich'aak I died the same day. A year later a new king, son of a foreign lord called "Spearthrower Owl", was installed, and Teotihuacan symbols spread through the Maya lowlands.
summary.zh: 378年1月，与特奥蒂瓦坎有关的军事首领西亚赫·卡克抵达蒂卡尔，国王查克·托克·伊查克一世同日死去。一年后，一位名为“掷矛器猫头鹰”的外族君主之子被立为新王，特奥蒂瓦坎的符号随之传遍玛雅低地。

sources.title: David Stuart, "The Arrival of Strangers: Teotihuacan and Tollan in Classic Maya History", in Mesoamerica's Classic Heritage (2000)
Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)
Wikipedia: Siyaj K'ak'

note: Recorded on Tikal Stela 31 and Uaxactun and El Perú monuments (Long Count 8.17.1.4.12). Conversions put the arrival in mid- to late January 378, depending on the correlation used. Whether this was a conquest or an alliance is still debated.

story.en:
Stela 31 at Tikal, carved two generations later, tells the story in a few terse phrases. On 8.17.1.4.12 in the Maya Long Count, mid-January 378, Siyaj K'ahk' ("Fire Is Born") "arrived" at Tikal. Inscriptions at El Perú show him passing through that city eight days earlier, on a route that came from the west. On the day he reached Tikal the reigning king, Chak Tok Ich'aak I, "entered the water", a Maya phrase for death.

In 379 a boy named Yax Nuun Ahiin was enthroned under Siyaj K'ahk's supervision. His father was a ruler called Jatz'om Kuy, "Spearthrower Owl", whom many scholars think was a king of Teotihuacan itself. Yax Nuun Ahiin appears on Stela 31 dressed as a central Mexican warrior, with a Teotihuacan-style shield.

David Stuart, who first read the "arrival" glyph, calls it the "entrada". Within a few years new dynasties with Teotihuacan connections appeared at Uaxactun, Río Azul and, in 426, Copán, and Tikal became the leading Maya kingdom for nearly two centuries.
story.zh:
蒂卡尔31号石碑刻于两代人之后，用寥寥数语记述了此事。玛雅长纪历8.17.1.4.12，即378年1月中旬，西亚赫·卡克（意为“火焰诞生”）“抵达”蒂卡尔。埃尔佩鲁的铭文显示，他在8天前途经该城，路线自西而来。就在他抵达蒂卡尔的当天，在位国王查克·托克·伊查克一世“入水”，这是玛雅人对死亡的说法。

379年，一个名叫亚什·努恩·阿因的少年在西亚赫·卡克的监护下登基。他的父亲是一位名为“掷矛器猫头鹰”的统治者，许多学者认为此人就是特奥蒂瓦坎的君主。31号石碑上的亚什·努恩·阿因身着墨西哥中部武士装束，手持特奥蒂瓦坎式盾牌。

最早释读出“抵达”字符的大卫·斯图尔特称此事为“进入”。此后数年间，与特奥蒂瓦坎有关的新王朝相继出现在瓦哈克通、里奥阿苏尔，并于426年出现在科潘；蒂卡尔则成为此后近两个世纪里最强大的玛雅王国。

name.en: K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' founds the Copán dynasty
name.zh: 基尼奇·亚什·库克·莫建立科潘王朝

summary.en: In 426 a lord named K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' took power at Copán in western Honduras, founding a dynasty of 16 kings. Isotope analysis of his skeleton suggests he grew up in the central Petén, and later monuments show him in Teotihuacan-style goggles.
summary.zh: 426年，一位名为基尼奇·亚什·库克·莫的君主在洪都拉斯西部的科潘掌权，开创了一个历经16位国王的王朝。对其遗骸的同位素分析表明他在佩滕中部长大，后世石刻则把他描绘成戴特奥蒂瓦坎式护目镜的形象。

sources.title: Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)
Ellen E. Bell, Marcello A. Canuto & Robert J. Sharer (eds.), Understanding Early Classic Copan (2004)
UNESCO World Heritage: Maya Site of Copan

story.en:
Copán's kings never forgot their founder. Three and a half centuries after him, the 16th king, Yax Pasaj Chan Yopaat, dedicated Altar Q in 776: a square stone whose four sides show all sixteen rulers seated in order, with K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' handing the staff of office to Yax Pasaj himself.

Tunnelling inside the Acropolis in the 1990s, archaeologists of the University of Pennsylvania found the founder's own buildings buried under later temples, among them the brightly painted Rosalila temple, preserved almost intact. In a tomb at the base they found an older man with healed battle injuries, very probably the founder. Strontium isotopes in his teeth pointed to a childhood far from Copán, most likely in the central Petén near Tikal. The texts call him a "lord of the west", tying him to the Teotihuacan-backed order created after 378.
story.zh:
科潘的国王们始终铭记开国之君。三个半世纪后，第16位国王亚什·帕萨赫·陈·约帕特于776年立起“Q号祭坛”。这块方石四面刻着按次序端坐的全部16位君主，其中基尼奇·亚什·库克·莫正把王权权杖交给亚什·帕萨赫本人。

20世纪90年代，宾夕法尼亚大学的考古学家在卫城内部开掘隧道，在后期神庙下面找到了开国者时代的建筑，其中包括几乎完好保存、色彩鲜艳的“罗萨利拉”神庙。他们在底部一座墓中发现一名带有愈合战伤的年长男子，很可能就是开国者本人。其牙齿中的锶同位素显示他童年远离科潘，最可能在蒂卡尔附近的佩滕中部度过。铭文称他为“西方之主”，把他与378年后特奥蒂瓦坎扶植的秩序联系在一起。

name.en: Tierra Blanca Joven eruption of Ilopango
name.zh: 伊洛潘戈火山“年轻白土”大喷发

summary.en: The Ilopango caldera in El Salvador produced one of the largest eruptions of the last 10,000 years in Central America, burying the surrounding valleys under thick ash and pyroclastic flows. Ice-core work dates it to 431 ± 2 CE, though a date of 539/540 has also been argued.
summary.zh: 萨尔瓦多的伊洛潘戈破火山口发生中美洲近一万年来规模最大的喷发之一，周边河谷被厚厚的火山灰和火山碎屑流掩埋。冰芯研究将其定年为公元431±2年，但也有学者主张539/540年。

sources.title: Victoria C. Smith et al., "The magnitude and impact of the 431 CE Tierra Blanca Joven eruption of Ilopango, El Salvador", PNAS 117 (2020)
Robert A. Dull et al., "Radiocarbon and geologic evidence reveal Ilopango volcano as source of the colossal 'mystery' eruption of 539/40 CE", Quaternary Science Reviews 222 (2019)
Wikipedia: Tierra Blanca Joven eruption

note: Date disputed: 431 ± 2 CE (Smith et al. 2020, Greenland ice-core tephra) versus 539/540 CE (Dull et al. 2019, radiocarbon on buried trees). We follow 431.

story.en:
Lake Ilopango, just east of San Salvador, fills the crater of a volcano that tore itself apart. The eruption threw out tens of cubic kilometres of ash, the "young white earth" (tierra blanca joven) that geologists find over much of western El Salvador. Pyroclastic flows swept across an area that had been densely farmed by Maya-speaking villagers, and ash fell as far as Guatemala and Honduras.

Scientists disagree on when it happened. Robert Dull's team dated trees killed by the flows and linked the blast to the cold "mystery" years of 536–540 that chroniclers in Europe and China recorded. Victoria Smith and colleagues then found glass shards with Ilopango's chemistry in a Greenland ice layer dated 431, and argued the eruption had only a modest global effect. Either way, the zone nearest the volcano was emptied for generations and people moved toward the highlands and the Pacific coast.
story.zh:
伊洛潘戈湖位于圣萨尔瓦多以东，湖水注满一座自我撕裂的火山的火山口。这次喷发喷出数十立方公里的火山灰，即地质学家在萨尔瓦多西部大部分地区发现的“年轻白土”。火山碎屑流横扫了讲玛雅语的村民密集耕作的土地，火山灰远落至危地马拉和洪都拉斯。

科学家们对喷发时间看法不一。罗伯特·达尔的团队测定了被碎屑流杀死的树木的年代，把这次喷发与欧洲和中国史家所记536至540年间神秘的寒冷年份联系起来。维多利亚·史密斯等人随后在格陵兰一层定年为431年的冰层中发现了与伊洛潘戈化学成分相符的玻璃碎屑，认为这次喷发对全球的影响有限。无论哪种说法，火山附近地区都荒废了好几代人，居民迁往高地和太平洋沿岸。

name.zh: 特奥蒂瓦坎被焚与衰落

summary.en: Around 550 the palaces and temples along Teotihuacan's Street of the Dead were burned and its sculptures smashed, apparently in an internal revolt against the ruling elite. The city shrank rapidly, and power in central Mexico fragmented among rival centres such as Cholula, Xochicalco and Cacaxtla.
summary.zh: 约550年，特奥蒂瓦坎亡者大道两旁的宫殿和神庙被焚毁，雕像被砸碎，似乎是一场针对统治精英的内部暴动。城市迅速萎缩，墨西哥中部的权力分散到乔卢拉、霍奇卡尔科、卡卡斯特拉等相互竞争的中心。

sources.title: George L. Cowgill, Ancient Teotihuacan: Early Urbanism in Central Mexico (2015)
Linda R. Manzanilla, "Cooperation and tensions in multiethnic corporate societies using Teotihuacan, Central Mexico, as a case study", PNAS 112 (2015)
Britannica: Teotihuacán

note: Older literature dates the fire to c. 650–750; recalibrated radiocarbon now places it around 550 ± 25.

story.en:
For four centuries Teotihuacan had dominated central Mexico. Then, around the middle of the sixth century, someone set fire to the buildings along its main avenue. Excavations show the burning was selective: temples, palaces and elite residences on the Street of the Dead were torched, statues of deities were broken and thrown down, and the fire was not a battle damage pattern of the whole city. Linda Manzanilla and others read it as a revolt from within, perhaps by intermediate elites who ran the multi-ethnic neighbourhoods and resented the rulers.

The city did not vanish overnight; tens of thousands of people still lived there for a while. But the great state that had sent Siyaj K'ahk' to Tikal in 378 was gone. Its fall opened the "Epiclassic" period, when fortified hilltop cities such as Xochicalco and Cacaxtla rose, and when Maya kingdoms freed of Teotihuacan's shadow entered their own most brilliant age.
story.zh:
特奥蒂瓦坎主宰墨西哥中部长达四个世纪。约6世纪中叶，有人放火焚烧了它主干道两旁的建筑。发掘显示焚烧是有选择的：亡者大道上的神庙、宫殿和精英宅邸被点燃，神像被砸碎推倒，并非整座城市遭受战火的样子。琳达·曼萨尼利亚等学者认为这是一场内部暴动，发起者或许是管理多民族街区、对统治者心怀不满的中层精英。

城市并未一夜消失，此后一段时间仍有数万人居住。但那个曾于378年派西亚赫·卡克前往蒂卡尔的强大国家已不复存在。它的衰落开启了“后古典早期”（Epiclassic），霍奇卡尔科、卡卡斯特拉等设防的山顶城市兴起，摆脱了特奥蒂瓦坎阴影的玛雅王国也迎来了各自最辉煌的时代。

name.en: Tikal defeated by Caracol and Calakmul
name.zh: 蒂卡尔败于卡拉科尔与卡拉克穆尔

summary.en: In 562 Tikal suffered a "star war" defeat at the hands of Caracol, led by Yajaw Te' K'inich II and backed by the Kaanul (Snake) kingdom. Tikal's king Wak Chan K'awiil was probably sacrificed, and the city erected no dated monuments for over a century.
summary.zh: 562年，蒂卡尔在一场“星辰战争”中败于亚哈夫·特·基尼奇二世统率、得到卡努尔（蛇）王国支持的卡拉科尔。蒂卡尔国王瓦克·陈·卡维尔很可能被献祭，此后一百多年该城未再竖立有纪年的石碑。

sources.title: Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)
Arlen F. Chase & Diane Z. Chase, "Investigations at the Classic Maya City of Caracol, Belize: 1985–1987" (1987)
Wikipedia: Caracol

note: Caracol Altar 21 records the war; the reading of the victor (Caracol or the Kaanul king Sky Witness) is debated.

story.en:
Caracol, in the hills of western Belize, had been a client of Tikal: in 553 its king Yajaw Te' K'inich II was installed "under the supervision" of Tikal's ruler. Three years later relations broke down, and in 562 Caracol's Altar 21 records a "star war", the glyph the Maya used for a decisive war that overthrew a kingdom, against Tikal.

The text is damaged, and scholars argue whether the real victor was Caracol or its powerful ally Sky Witness, king of the Kaanul dynasty, which was then building an alliance network to encircle Tikal. Whoever won, Tikal's king Wak Chan K'awiil disappears from the record, probably sacrificed. Tikal entered a "hiatus" of about 130 years without dated monuments, while Caracol grew into a city of perhaps 100,000 people with causeways radiating across the hills.
story.zh:
卡拉科尔位于伯利兹西部山区，原是蒂卡尔的附庸：553年，其国王亚哈夫·特·基尼奇二世是在蒂卡尔君主“监督下”即位的。三年后双方关系破裂，卡拉科尔21号祭坛记载，562年对蒂卡尔发动了一场“星辰战争”，这是玛雅人用来表示推翻一个王国的决定性战争的字符。

铭文残损，学者们争论真正的胜者是卡拉科尔，还是其强大盟友、卡努尔王朝国王“天空见证者”，后者当时正在构建包围蒂卡尔的联盟网络。无论谁取胜，蒂卡尔国王瓦克·陈·卡维尔从此从记载中消失，很可能被献祭。蒂卡尔进入长约130年没有纪年碑刻的“空白期”，卡拉科尔则发展为人口或达10万的城市，堤道从中心向群山辐射。

name.en: Joya de Cerén buried by the Loma Caldera eruption
name.zh: 霍亚德塞伦被洛马卡尔德拉火山喷发掩埋

summary.en: Around 600 a small eruption of Loma Caldera buried the Maya farming village of Joya de Cerén in El Salvador under several metres of ash. The villagers escaped, but their houses, tools, food and gardens were preserved, giving a unique view of everyday Classic Maya life.
summary.zh: 约600年，洛马卡尔德拉火山的一次小规模喷发将萨尔瓦多的玛雅农村霍亚德塞伦埋在数米厚的火山灰下。村民得以逃生，但他们的房屋、工具、食物和菜园被完整保存下来，为了解古典期玛雅人的日常生活提供了独一无二的窗口。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Joya de Cerén Archaeological Site
Payson Sheets, The Ceren Site: An Ancient Village Buried by Volcanic Ash in Central America (2nd ed., 2006)
Wikipedia: Joya de Cerén

note: Radiocarbon dates the eruption to the late 6th or early 7th century; an August evening is inferred from the crops and the state of the houses.

story.en:
In 1976 a bulldozer levelling ground for grain silos cut into a clay wall buried deep under volcanic ash. Payson Sheets of the University of Colorado, who began excavating two years later, realised he had found a whole village frozen at one moment.

The eruption seems to have come on an August evening, after dinner: dishes had been used but not washed, and sleeping mats were not yet unrolled. The people fled, apparently in time, since no bodies have been found. Left behind were adobe houses, storehouses, a sweat bath, a community building, pots still holding beans and chilli, a duck tied up, and fields of maize ridges and manioc, the first manioc cultivation ever documented archaeologically in the Maya world.

Often called the "Pompeii of the Americas", Cerén shows farmers who were far from poor: each household owned dozens of vessels and traded for obsidian and jade.
story.zh:
1976年，一台推土机在平整修建粮仓的地基时，挖到了深埋在火山灰下的一堵黏土墙。两年后开始发掘的科罗拉多大学学者佩森·希茨意识到，他发现的是一整座被定格在某一刻的村庄。

喷发似乎发生在8月的一个傍晚、晚饭之后：碗碟用过尚未清洗，睡席还没铺开。村民们看来及时逃走了，因为至今没有发现遗体。留下的有土坯房、仓库、蒸汽浴室、公共建筑、仍盛着豆子和辣椒的陶罐、一只被拴住的鸭子，以及玉米垄和木薯田；这是玛雅地区第一次在考古中证实木薯种植。

塞伦常被称为“美洲的庞贝”，它显示这里的农民远非贫困：每户都拥有数十件器皿，并通过交易获得黑曜石和玉石。

summary.en: In 629 a branch of Tikal's royal family founded Dos Pilas in the Petexbatún region. Its king B'alaj Chan K'awiil switched to the side of Calakmul and fought his own brother at Tikal; the kingdom collapsed in 761 amid endemic warfare, its last people walling themselves inside palisades.
summary.zh: 629年，蒂卡尔王族的一支在佩特斯巴通地区建立多斯皮拉斯。其国王巴拉赫·陈·卡维尔倒向卡拉克穆尔，与身为蒂卡尔国王的兄长兵戎相见。761年，王国在连绵战乱中崩溃，最后的居民在木栅围墙中自守。

sources.title: Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)
Arthur A. Demarest, The Petexbatun Regional Archaeological Project (2006)
Wikipedia: Dos Pilas

story.en:
Dos Pilas tells the Classic Maya world's family quarrel in stone. Its first king, B'alaj Chan K'awiil, was a prince of Tikal, probably sent as a boy to rule a new outpost near the Pasión River. Captured or pressured by the Kaanul kingdom of Calakmul in about 648, he became Calakmul's vassal and turned against his half-brother Nuun Ujol Chaak of Tikal. A hieroglyphic stairway at Dos Pilas boasts of his victory over Tikal in 679.

His daughter, Lady Six Sky, was sent to Naranjo in 682 to restart its dynasty. Later kings expanded the Petexbatún state, but in 761 its ruler was defeated and fled. Archaeologists of Vanderbilt University found that the last inhabitants had torn stones from temples and palaces to build double palisade walls across the royal plaza, a vivid sign of the warfare that preceded the Classic Maya collapse.
story.zh:
多斯皮拉斯用石刻讲述了古典期玛雅世界的一场家族纷争。第一位国王巴拉赫·陈·卡维尔是蒂卡尔王子，可能幼年时被派往帕西翁河附近的新据点为王。约648年，他被卡拉克穆尔的卡努尔王国俘获或胁迫，成为其附庸，转而与同父异母的兄长、蒂卡尔国王努恩·乌霍尔·查克为敌。多斯皮拉斯的象形文字阶梯夸耀他在679年战胜了蒂卡尔。

他的女儿“六天夫人”于682年被派往纳兰霍重建王统。后来的国王扩张了佩特斯巴通王国，但761年其统治者战败出逃。范德堡大学的考古学家发现，最后的居民从神庙和宫殿拆下石块，在王室广场上筑起双重木栅围墙，生动地反映了古典期玛雅崩溃前的战乱。

name.en: Burial of K'inich Janaab Pakal in the Temple of the Inscriptions

summary.en: Pakal the Great of Palenque died in 683 after a reign of 68 years and was buried in a vaulted crypt deep inside the Temple of the Inscriptions, under a carved sarcophagus lid. Alberto Ruz Lhuillier found the sealed tomb in 1952, the first royal burial discovered inside a Maya pyramid.
summary.zh: 帕伦克的巴加尔大帝在位68年后于683年去世，葬于铭文神庙深处的拱顶墓室，覆以雕花石棺盖。1952年，阿尔韦托·鲁斯·吕利耶发现了这座密封的墓室，这是首次在玛雅金字塔内部发现王陵。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Pre-Hispanic City and National Park of Palenque
Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)
Britannica: Palenque
Wikipedia: Temple of the Inscriptions

story.en:
Pakal began his own funerary pyramid late in life; his son K'inich Kan Bahlam II finished it. Its three great tablets carry one of the longest Maya inscriptions, listing Palenque's kings and the rituals of the calendar.

In 1948 the Mexican archaeologist Alberto Ruz Lhuillier noticed that one floor slab in the temple on top had holes with stone plugs. Lifting it, he found a staircase packed solid with rubble. Four field seasons later, on 15 June 1952, his team reached a triangular stone door at the bottom, guarded by the bones of five or six sacrificed people. Behind it lay a vaulted chamber with stucco figures on the walls and a stone sarcophagus covered by a five-tonne lid showing Pakal falling into, or rising from, the jaws of the underworld.

Inside lay Pakal, wearing a mosaic jade mask. A narrow stone tube, the "psychoduct", ran from the coffin up the stairway to the temple floor, a path by which the king's spirit could speak to the living.
story.zh:
巴加尔晚年开始修建自己的陵墓金字塔，由其子基尼奇·坎·巴拉姆二世完成。神庙的三块大石板上刻有最长的玛雅铭文之一，列举了帕伦克诸王和历法仪式。

1948年，墨西哥考古学家阿尔韦托·鲁斯·吕利耶注意到顶部神庙地面的一块石板上有用石塞堵住的孔洞。掀开后，他发现一段被碎石填实的阶梯。经过四个发掘季，1952年6月15日，团队到达底部一扇三角形石门，门前有五六名献祭者的遗骨。门后是一间拱顶墓室，墙上饰有灰泥人像，石棺上覆盖着一块重约5吨的石盖，刻画巴加尔坠入（或升出）冥界巨口的情景。

棺内的巴加尔戴着镶嵌玉石面具。一条细长的石管，即“灵魂通道”，从石棺沿阶梯通到神庙地面，国王的灵魂可借此与生者对话。

name.zh: 蒂卡尔击败卡拉克穆尔

summary.en: On 5 August 695 Tikal's king Jasaw Chan K'awiil I defeated Yuknoom Yich'aak K'ahk' of the Kaanul kingdom, capturing a palanquin effigy of Calakmul's patron god. The victory ended Tikal's long eclipse and broke the Snake kingdom's hegemony over the lowlands.
summary.zh: 695年8月5日，蒂卡尔国王哈萨夫·陈·卡维尔一世击败卡努尔王国的尤克努姆·伊查克·卡克，缴获了卡拉克穆尔守护神的神轿像。这场胜利结束了蒂卡尔长期的低迷，打破了蛇王国对低地的霸权。

sources.title: Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)
Simon Martin, Ancient Maya Politics: A Political Anthropology of the Classic Period 150–900 CE (2020)
Wikipedia: Jasaw Chan K'awiil I

note: Date from Tikal Temple I, Lintel 3 (9.13.3.7.18); the battle site is unknown, so the marker is at Tikal.

story.en:
By the 690s the Kaanul kings, ruling from Calakmul, had spent a century hemming Tikal in with allies such as Caracol, Naranjo and Dos Pilas. Jasaw Chan K'awiil I, who took Tikal's throne in 682, broke the ring. A carved wooden lintel from Temple I records that on 5 August 695 he "brought down the flint and shield" of Yich'aak K'ahk', Calakmul's king, and seized a giant effigy of the enemy's patron deity, carried on a litter.

Thirteen days later, exactly 260 days (one ritual calendar cycle) after the anniversary of Siyaj K'ahk's arrival in 378, Jasaw held victory rites in Tikal, deliberately reviving the city's Teotihuacan heritage. Calakmul never fully recovered. Jasaw was later buried under Temple I, the Temple of the Great Jaguar, facing the temple of his wife across Tikal's Great Plaza.
story.zh:
到690年代，以卡拉克穆尔为都的卡努尔诸王已用一个世纪时间，联合卡拉科尔、纳兰霍、多斯皮拉斯等盟友围困蒂卡尔。682年即位的哈萨夫·陈·卡维尔一世打破了这个包围圈。一号神庙的木雕门楣记载，695年8月5日，他“击倒了”卡拉克穆尔国王伊查克·卡克的“燧石与盾牌”，并夺得敌方守护神置于轿舆上的巨大神像。

13天后，正好是378年西亚赫·卡克到来纪念日之后的260天（一个仪式历周期），哈萨夫在蒂卡尔举行凯旋仪式，有意复兴该城的特奥蒂瓦坎传统。卡拉克穆尔从此一蹶不振。哈萨夫后来葬于一号神庙（大美洲豹神庙）之下，隔着蒂卡尔大广场与其王后的神庙相望。

name.en: Yaxchilan Lintels 24–26 carved for Lady K'abal Xook
name.zh: 亚斯奇兰为卡巴尔·肖克夫人雕刻24至26号门楣

summary.en: King Itzamnaaj Bahlam III (Shield Jaguar) of Yaxchilan dedicated a temple to his principal wife, Lady K'abal Xook, with carved lintels showing her drawing a thorned rope through her tongue and conjuring a serpent vision. Lintel 24 is now in the British Museum and is a masterpiece of Maya relief.
summary.zh: 亚斯奇兰国王伊察姆纳赫·巴拉姆三世（盾豹）为正妻卡巴尔·肖克夫人献建一座神庙，门楣浮雕描绘她用带刺绳索穿过舌头放血、召唤蛇形幻象的场景。24号门楣现藏大英博物馆，是玛雅浮雕的杰作。

sources.title: British Museum: Lintel 24, Yaxchilan (Am1923,Maud.4)
Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)
Wikipedia: Yaxchilan Lintel 24

story.en:
Structure 23 at Yaxchilan, on a bend of the Usumacinta River, is the first Maya building known to have been dedicated to a woman. Its three doorways were spanned by limestone lintels carved in deep relief. On Lintel 24 the king, Shield Jaguar, holds a blazing torch over Lady K'abal Xook, who kneels in a richly woven huipil and pulls a rope studded with thorns through her pierced tongue; the blood drips onto paper in a basket. On Lintel 25 a giant serpent rises from the smoke of the burnt paper, with a warrior emerging from its jaws.

The British explorer Alfred Maudslay cut the lintels from the building in 1882 and shipped Lintels 24 and 25 to London. Their quality and the prominence they give to a royal woman have made them among the best-known images of the Classic Maya. After Shield Jaguar died in 742, a ten-year gap preceded the accession of his son by another wife, Bird Jaguar IV.
story.zh:
亚斯奇兰坐落在乌苏马辛塔河的一处河湾上，其23号建筑是已知第一座献给女性的玛雅建筑。三个门道上横架着深浮雕石灰岩门楣。24号门楣上，国王盾豹高举燃烧的火炬，卡巴尔·肖克夫人身着精织的惠皮尔长衫跪在他面前，将一根缀满尖刺的绳索穿过被刺穿的舌头，鲜血滴在篮中的纸上。25号门楣上，巨蛇从焚纸的烟中升起，一名武士从蛇口中现身。

1882年，英国探险家阿尔弗雷德·莫兹利把门楣从建筑上切下，将24号和25号运往伦敦。其精湛的工艺以及对王室女性的突出表现，使它们成为古典期玛雅最著名的图像之一。盾豹于742年去世后，经过十年空位，他与另一位妻子所生的儿子“鸟豹四世”才继位。

name.en: Quiriguá captures and beheads 18 Rabbit of Copán
name.zh: 基里瓜俘获并斩首科潘国王“十八兔”

summary.en: On 3 May 738 K'ak' Tiliw Chan Yopaat of Quiriguá, a small vassal city, captured Copán's great king Uaxaclajuun Ub'aah K'awiil ("18 Rabbit") and beheaded him. Quiriguá became independent and raised the tallest stelae in the Maya world to celebrate.
summary.zh: 738年5月3日，小附庸城邦基里瓜的国王卡克·蒂利夫·陈·约帕特俘获科潘的伟大国王瓦沙克拉胡恩·乌巴·卡维尔（“十八兔”），并将其斩首。基里瓜由此独立，并竖起玛雅世界最高的石碑以示庆贺。

sources.title: Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)
UNESCO World Heritage: Archaeological Park and Ruins of Quirigua
Wikipedia: Uaxaclajuun Ub'aah K'awiil

story.en:
Quiriguá, 50 km north of Copán in the Motagua valley, controlled the jade route to the Caribbean. In 724 Copán's 13th king, 18 Rabbit, had installed K'ak' Tiliw Chan Yopaat as its ruler. Fourteen years later the vassal turned on his lord. Quiriguá's monuments say that on 3 May 738 its king "chopped" 18 Rabbit's "wooden and flint" gods, captured him, and decapitated him the same day.

How a minor town overcame the patron of Copán's splendid Great Plaza is unclear; many scholars suspect the hand of Calakmul, which may have backed the rebel. At Copán the shock was brief, but no inscriptions mention the disaster except a laconic note that 18 Rabbit died "in battle". At Quiriguá, K'ak' Tiliw spent the next decades raising colossal sandstone stelae, Stela E reaching about 10.6 m, to proclaim his triumph.
story.zh:
基里瓜位于科潘以北50公里的莫塔瓜河谷，控制着通往加勒比海的玉石之路。724年，科潘第13位国王“十八兔”立卡克·蒂利夫·陈·约帕特为基里瓜统治者。14年后，这位附庸背叛了宗主。基里瓜的碑铭称，738年5月3日，其国王“砍倒”十八兔的“木质与燧石”神像，俘获并于当天将他斩首。

一个小城邦如何击败修建科潘壮丽大广场的君主，至今不明；许多学者怀疑卡拉克穆尔在背后支持叛乱者。在科潘，这场震荡为时不长，铭文中除了简短记载十八兔“死于战斗”外别无提及。在基里瓜，卡克·蒂利夫在此后数十年里竖起巨大的砂岩石碑宣扬胜利，其中E号石碑高约10.6米。

name.zh: 科潘象形文字阶梯落成

summary.en: King K'ak' Yipyaj Chan K'awiil completed Temple 26 at Copán with a stairway of 62 steps carved with about 2,200 glyphs, the longest known Maya text. It retold the dynasty's history to restore royal prestige after the humiliation of 738.
summary.zh: 国王卡克·伊普亚赫·陈·卡维尔在科潘完成了26号神庙，其62级台阶上刻有约2200个字符，是已知最长的玛雅文献。它重述王朝历史，以挽回738年受辱后的王室威望。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Maya Site of Copan
Barbara W. Fash, The Copan Sculpture Museum (2011)
Wikipedia: Hieroglyphic Stairway

note: Dedicated in 755; most of the steps were found collapsed in the 1890s, so the text order is only partly restored.

summary.en: Under King Yajaw Chan Muwaan, three rooms of Structure 1 at Bonampak were covered with murals of a royal heir's presentation, a battle, the torture of captives and a victory dance. Shown to outsiders in 1946, they are the most complete Classic Maya paintings known.
summary.zh: 在国王亚哈夫·陈·穆万统治下，博南帕克1号建筑的三个房间绘满壁画，描绘王储亮相、战斗、折磨俘虏和凯旋舞蹈。1946年首次向外界展示，它们是已知最完整的古典期玛雅绘画。

sources.title: Mary Ellen Miller & Claudia Brittenham, The Spectacle of the Late Maya Court: Reflections on the Murals of Bonampak (2013)
Wikipedia: Bonampak
Robert J. Sharer & Loa P. Traxler, The Ancient Maya (6th ed., 2006)

note: An inscription dates the dedication to 791; the paintings may have been left unfinished as the kingdom collapsed.

story.en:
In 1946 Lacandon Maya guides led the American photographer Giles Healey to a small temple in the Chiapas rainforest. Inside, under a crust of calcite, the walls were alive with colour. The three rooms read like a story: in the first, nobles in white capes and musicians with trumpets and turtle-shell drums attend the presentation of a royal child; in the second, a chaotic battle in the forest gives way to a scene where naked captives, their fingernails torn out and bleeding, plead before the king on a stairway; in the third, lords in towering feathered headdresses dance in triumph.

The king was Yajaw Chan Muwaan, a vassal of nearby Yaxchilan. The murals were painted around 791, only a few decades before the region was abandoned. The vivid "Maya blue" pigment and the unflinching scenes of violence overturned an older belief that the Classic Maya were peaceful astronomer-priests.
story.zh:
1946年，拉坎东玛雅向导带领美国摄影师贾尔斯·希利来到恰帕斯雨林中的一座小神庙。在一层方解石外壳之下，墙壁上色彩鲜活。三个房间如同一则连环故事：第一间里，身披白斗篷的贵族和吹号角、敲龟甲鼓的乐师出席王子的亮相仪式；第二间里，林中一场混战之后，赤身的俘虏指甲被拔、鲜血淋漓，在阶梯上向国王求饶；第三间里，戴着高耸羽冠的贵族跳起凯旋之舞。

这位国王是附近亚斯奇兰的附庸亚哈夫·陈·穆万。壁画约绘于791年，距离这一地区被弃仅数十年。鲜艳的“玛雅蓝”颜料和毫不避讳的暴力场面，推翻了古典期玛雅人是和平的天文学家兼祭司这一旧观念。

summary.en: Between about 800 and 950 the great kingdoms of the southern Maya lowlands stopped erecting dated monuments, their dynasties ended and their cities emptied; millions of people left the region. Endemic warfare, overpopulation, deforestation and a series of severe droughts are all implicated.
summary.zh: 约800至950年间，玛雅南部低地的大王国不再竖立纪年碑，王朝相继终结，城市人去楼空，数以百万计的人口离开了这一地区。连绵的战争、人口过剩、森林砍伐以及一系列严重干旱都被认为是原因。

sources.title: David A. Hodell, Jason H. Curtis & Mark Brenner, "Possible role of climate in the collapse of Classic Maya civilization", Nature 375 (1995)
Arthur A. Demarest, Prudence M. Rice & Don S. Rice (eds.), The Terminal Classic in the Maya Lowlands (2004)
Simon Martin & Nikolai Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens (2nd ed., 2008)
Wikipedia: Classic Maya collapse

note: The collapse was a process, not a single event: some cities failed by 760 and others lasted past 900. The last Long Count date (Toniná, 909) is often used as its end point.

story.en:
The last dated monuments read like a countdown. Dos Pilas fell in 761; Palenque's last known king acceded in 799; Copán's final ruler, Ukit Took', began an altar in 822 that was never finished; Tikal's last stela dates from 869; and a monument at Toniná in 909 bears the final Long Count date ever carved. Around them, populations that may have totalled several million in the southern lowlands dwindled to scattered villages.

No single cause explains it. Inscriptions show warfare intensifying in the eighth century, with more kings capturing kings. Pollen cores show forests cleared for farms and fuel. In 1995 David Hodell's team showed from sediment layers in Lake Chichancanab that the ninth century was the driest period in the region for thousands of years, and later studies found repeated multi-year droughts. Kings whose authority rested on securing rain from the gods lost legitimacy when the rains failed.

The Maya themselves did not vanish. Life shifted north to Chichen Itza and the Puuc cities, and to the highlands, where millions of Maya people live today.
story.zh:
最后的纪年碑读来如同倒计时：多斯皮拉斯于761年陷落；帕伦克已知最后一位国王于799年即位；科潘末代君主乌基特·托克于822年开凿的祭坛未能完工；蒂卡尔最后一块石碑立于869年；909年托尼纳的一座石碑刻下了最后一个长纪历日期。在这些城市周围，南部低地原本或达数百万的人口缩减为零星村落。

没有单一原因可以解释这一切。铭文显示，8世纪战争愈演愈烈，国王俘获国王的事件越来越多。花粉岩芯显示森林被砍伐用于耕作和燃料。1995年，戴维·霍德尔团队根据奇昌卡纳布湖的沉积层证明，9世纪是该地区数千年来最干旱的时期，后来的研究又发现了反复出现的多年干旱。国王的权威建立在向神祈雨之上，雨水不来，他们便失去了合法性。

玛雅人自身并未消失。生活重心北移到奇琴伊察和普克地区诸城，也转向高地，今天仍有数百万玛雅人生活在那里。

summary.en: Monte Albán, the Zapotec capital on a levelled mountaintop above the Valley of Oaxaca since about 500 BCE, lost its political primacy between about 750 and 850. The valley broke into rival Zapotec lordships such as Zaachila, Mitla and Lambityeco.
summary.zh: 阿尔班山自约公元前500年起就是萨波特克人的都城，建在俯瞰瓦哈卡谷地的削平山顶上。约750至850年间，它失去了政治上的首要地位，谷地分裂为萨奇拉、米特拉、兰比蒂耶科等相互竞争的萨波特克领地。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Historic Centre of Oaxaca and Archaeological Site of Monte Albán
Joyce Marcus & Kent V. Flannery, Zapotec Civilization: How Urban Society Evolved in Mexico's Oaxaca Valley (1996)
Wikipedia: Monte Albán

note: Dates for the end of Period IIIB–IV vary between about 700 and 900.

story.en:
Monte Albán was founded around 500 BCE on a ridge 400 m above the valley floor, a defensible meeting point for the valley's three arms. Over a thousand years its people levelled the summit into a great plaza flanked by temples, a ballcourt and the strange arrow-shaped Building J, which may have served as an observatory. Early galleries of carved slabs, the so-called Danzantes, show slain or captive enemies, and some of the oldest writing in Mesoamerica.

At its peak in the Classic period the city held perhaps 25,000 people and kept diplomatic ties with Teotihuacan, where an Oaxacan neighbourhood existed. After Teotihuacan's fall, the Zapotec state too weakened. Between about 750 and 850 monumental building stopped and the population scattered to valley towns. The mountain remained sacred: Mixtec lords later reused its tombs, and in 1932 Alfonso Caso found in Tomb 7 a dazzling hoard of Mixtec gold, silver and carved bone.
story.zh:
阿尔班山约在公元前500年建于高出谷底400米的山脊上，是谷地三条支谷的交汇点，易守难攻。一千年间，居民把山顶削平为一座大广场，四周环绕神庙、球场和形状奇特的箭头形J号建筑，后者可能用作观象台。早期的雕刻石板长廊，即所谓“舞者”浮雕，描绘被杀或被俘的敌人，并刻有中美洲最古老的文字之一。

古典期鼎盛时，城中人口或达2.5万，与特奥蒂瓦坎保持外交往来，后者城中还有一个瓦哈卡人街区。特奥蒂瓦坎衰落后，萨波特克国家也随之衰弱。约750至850年间，大型营建停止，人口分散到谷地城镇。这座山依然神圣：米斯特克贵族后来重新利用其墓穴；1932年，阿方索·卡索在7号墓中发现了一批耀眼的米斯特克金银器和骨雕。

name.en: El Tajín and the Pyramid of the Niches
name.zh: 埃尔塔津与壁龛金字塔

summary.en: In the Gulf Coast lowlands of Veracruz, El Tajín flourished between about 800 and 1150, after Teotihuacan's fall. It is known for the Pyramid of the Niches, with 365 recesses, and for at least 17 ballcourts carved with scenes of the ballgame and its sacrificial rites.
summary.zh: 在韦拉克鲁斯的墨西哥湾沿岸低地，埃尔塔津在特奥蒂瓦坎衰落后，于约800至1150年间繁荣。它以拥有365个壁龛的壁龛金字塔闻名，并有至少17座球场，场边浮雕描绘球赛及其献祭仪式。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: El Tajin, Pre-Hispanic City
Michael D. Coe & Rex Koontz, Mexico: From the Olmecs to the Aztecs (7th ed., 2013)
Wikipedia: El Tajín

note: Occupation began earlier; the city's height is placed between about 800 and 1150.

name.zh: 图拉成为托尔特克都城

summary.en: Around 950 Tula (Tollan) in Hidalgo grew into a city of perhaps 40,000–60,000 people, capital of the Toltecs. Its Pyramid B is crowned by 4.6 m basalt warrior columns. Later Aztecs revered the Toltecs as the founders of civilised life and claimed descent from them.
summary.zh: 约950年，伊达尔戈州的图拉（托兰）发展为人口或达4万至6万的城市，成为托尔特克人的都城。其B号金字塔顶立有高4.6米的玄武岩武士像柱。后来的阿兹特克人尊托尔特克人为文明生活的开创者，并自称是其后裔。

sources.title: Richard A. Diehl, Tula: The Toltec Capital of Ancient Mexico (1983)
Michael D. Coe & Rex Koontz, Mexico: From the Olmecs to the Aztecs (7th ed., 2013)
Wikipedia: Tula (Mesoamerican site)

note: Tula Grande's apogee is placed c. 900/950–1150; the city's burning is traditionally dated 1168 or 1179.

story.en:
To the Aztecs, "Toltec" meant artisan, and Tollan was a golden age of feathers, jade and wisdom ruled by the priest-king Ce Acatl Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl. According to the sixteenth-century chronicles, the sorcerer Tezcatlipoca tricked him into drunkenness and shame, and he left Tula for the east, promising to return. Some chroniclers place his departure in 987, the same year Maya sources record the arrival of a lord called K'uk'ulkan (Feathered Serpent) in Yucatán.

Archaeology gives a harder picture. Tula was a militaristic city: its Pyramid B carries basalt "Atlantean" warriors with butterfly breastplates and spear-throwers, and a nearby wall is carved with feathered serpents devouring skeletons. A skull rack stood in the main plaza. The striking similarity between Tula's buildings and those of Chichen Itza, 1,200 km away, is still debated. Tula was burned and abandoned in the twelfth century, and Mexica nobles later carried away its sculpture as relics.
story.zh:
对阿兹特克人来说，“托尔特克”意为能工巧匠，而托兰则是由祭司王“一芦苇”托皮尔琴·克察尔科亚特尔统治的、充满羽毛、玉石与智慧的黄金时代。据16世纪编年史记载，巫师特斯卡特利波卡设计使他醉酒蒙羞，他便离开图拉东去，并许诺将会归来。有的编年史家把他离开的时间定在987年，而玛雅史料恰在同年记载一位名叫库库尔坎（羽蛇）的君主来到尤卡坦。

考古学呈现的图景则更为冷峻。图拉是一座尚武的城市：B号金字塔上立着胸佩蝴蝶甲、手持投矛器的玄武岩“擎天武士”，附近一面墙上刻着吞噬骷髅的羽蛇，主广场上还有头骨架。图拉建筑与远在1200公里外的奇琴伊察惊人相似，其原因至今仍有争论。图拉在12世纪被焚毁并遭遗弃，后来墨西加贵族把它的雕刻当作圣物运走。

name.en: El Castillo (Temple of Kukulcán) at Chichen Itza
name.zh: 奇琴伊察的卡斯蒂略金字塔（库库尔坎神庙）

summary.en: At Chichen Itza, which dominated northern Yucatán from about 850 to 1100, builders raised the nine-tiered pyramid of Kukulcán with four stairways of 91 steps plus a top platform, totalling 365. At the equinoxes the setting sun casts a serpent-like shadow down its northern balustrade.
summary.zh: 奇琴伊察约在850至1100年间称雄尤卡坦北部，那里的工匠建起九层的库库尔坎金字塔，四面各有91级台阶，加上顶层平台共365级。春分和秋分时，落日在北侧栏墙上投下宛如巨蛇蜿蜒的阴影。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Pre-Hispanic City of Chichen-Itza
Michael D. Coe & Rex Koontz, Mexico: From the Olmecs to the Aztecs (7th ed., 2013)
Wikipedia: El Castillo, Chichen Itza

note: The visible pyramid is dated to roughly the 10th–11th century; it encases an earlier pyramid with a red jaguar throne.

story.en:
El Castillo is a calendar in stone. Its four stairways of 91 steps and the top platform make 365, the days of the solar year; its nine terraces, split by the stairs, make 18 sections, the months of the Maya solar calendar. At sunset around the spring and autumn equinoxes, the stepped corners throw a row of triangles of light onto the northern balustrade, which ends in carved serpent heads, so that a body of light seems to slither down to the ground.

Archaeologists tunnelling into it in the 1930s found an older pyramid inside, with a chacmool figure and a throne in the shape of a jaguar painted red and inlaid with jade. Nearby, the round Caracol building has windows aligned to the extreme positions of Venus. Chichen Itza's Great Ballcourt, 168 m long, is the largest in Mesoamerica, and its Sacred Cenote received offerings of gold, jade and human beings for centuries after the city's decline.
story.zh:
卡斯蒂略金字塔是一部石头写成的历法。四面各91级台阶加上顶层平台共365级，对应太阳年的天数；九层台基被阶梯分割为18段，对应玛雅太阳历的18个月。春分、秋分前后日落时，阶梯状的边角在北侧栏墙上投下一串三角形光影，栏墙底端是蛇头雕刻，仿佛一条光之蛇蜿蜒游下地面。

20世纪30年代，考古学家开凿隧道进入塔内，发现其中包着一座更早的金字塔，内有一尊查克穆尔像和一张涂成红色、镶嵌玉石的美洲豹形宝座。附近的圆形“蜗牛”建筑，窗口对准金星运行的极点方位。奇琴伊察的大球场长168米，是中美洲最大的球场；其圣井在城市衰落后数百年间仍不断接纳黄金、玉石和人牲的祭献。

name.en: Eight Deer Jaguar Claw founds the coastal kingdom of Tututepec
name.zh: 八鹿·美洲豹爪建立沿海王国图图特佩克

summary.en: According to Mixtec screenfold books, the young lord Eight Deer Jaguar Claw took power at Tututepec on the Pacific coast of Oaxaca around 1083, then went on to conquer much of the Mixteca. Tututepec remained a major Mixtec kingdom until the Spanish conquest.
summary.zh: 据米斯特克折页手抄本记载，年轻的贵族八鹿·美洲豹爪约于1083年在瓦哈卡太平洋沿岸的图图特佩克掌权，随后征服了米斯特克地区大部。图图特佩克在西班牙征服前一直是重要的米斯特克王国。

sources.title: Codex Zouche-Nuttall (British Museum Am1902,0308.1)
Maarten Jansen & Gabina Aurora Pérez Jiménez, The Mixtec Pictorial Manuscripts (2005)
Wikipedia: Eight Deer Jaguar Claw

note: The date comes from the Mixtec codices' 52-year calendar, correlated with the Christian calendar by Alfonso Caso and later scholars; it is approximate.

name.en: Dresden Codex: Maya astronomy on bark paper
name.zh: 德累斯顿手抄本：树皮纸上的玛雅天文学

summary.en: The Dresden Codex, painted in Yucatán around the 13th century, is the finest of the four surviving Maya books. Its 39 bark-paper leaves contain divination almanacs, a table predicting solar eclipses and a Venus table accurate to about two hours over 481 years.
summary.zh: 德累斯顿手抄本约绘于13世纪的尤卡坦，是现存四部玛雅典籍中最精美的一部。其39页树皮纸上载有占卜历书、预测日食的表格，以及481年间误差仅约两小时的金星表。

sources.title: SLUB Dresden: Codex Dresdensis (Mscr.Dresd.R.310)
Michael D. Coe, Breaking the Maya Code (rev. ed., 1999)
Wikipedia: Dresden Codex

note: Dates proposed range from the 11th to 14th century; it may copy older originals. The marker is placed in northern Yucatán, where it was probably made.

story.en:
Only four Maya books survived the Spanish conquest, and the best of them turned up in Vienna. In 1739 Johann Christian Götze, librarian to the Elector of Saxony, bought it from a private owner and took it to Dresden, where nobody could read it. A century and a half later the Dresden librarian Ernst Förstemann worked out from it how the Maya counted: a place-value system in base 20 with a sign for zero, and the Long Count of days from a starting point in 3114 BCE.

Förstemann also found the Venus pages, which follow the planet's 584-day cycle through five appearances and include corrections that keep the table accurate over centuries, and a table of 405 lunar months that marks the danger points when solar eclipses could occur. The book was soaked with water when Dresden was bombed in February 1945, and some pages were damaged, but it remains a key text for Maya astronomy and the decipherment of the script.
story.zh:
只有四部玛雅典籍躲过了西班牙征服，其中最好的一部出现在维也纳。1739年，萨克森选帝侯的图书馆员约翰·克里斯蒂安·格策从私人手中买下它带回德累斯顿，当时没有人能读懂。一个半世纪后，德累斯顿图书馆员恩斯特·弗斯特曼从中破解了玛雅人的计数方法：以二十为基数、有零的符号的位值制，以及从公元前3114年某一起点开始计日的长纪历。

弗斯特曼还发现了金星篇章，它追踪金星584天的会合周期，历经五次出现，并附有修正值，使历表在数百年内保持精确；另有一份涵盖405个朔望月的表格，标出可能发生日食的危险时点。1945年2月德累斯顿遭轰炸时，手抄本被水浸泡，部分页面受损，但它至今仍是研究玛雅天文学和破译玛雅文字的关键文献。

name.en: Mayapan becomes capital of northern Yucatán
name.zh: 玛雅潘成为尤卡坦北部的都城

summary.en: After Chichen Itza's decline, the walled city of Mayapan rose to dominate northern Yucatán from about 1220, under a confederacy of noble lineages led by the Cocom. Its 9 km wall enclosed about 15,000–17,000 people and a smaller copy of Chichen's Castillo.
summary.zh: 奇琴伊察衰落后，约自1220年起，有城墙环绕的玛雅潘在以科科姆家族为首的贵族联盟统治下崛起，称雄尤卡坦北部。长9公里的城墙内居住着约1.5万至1.7万人，还有一座仿照奇琴伊察卡斯蒂略的小型金字塔。

sources.title: Marilyn A. Masson & Carlos Peraza Lope, Kukulcan's Realm: Urban Life at Ancient Mayapán (2014)
Wikipedia: Mayapan
Robert J. Sharer & Loa P. Traxler, The Ancient Maya (6th ed., 2006)

note: Traditional chronicle dates (from the Books of Chilam Balam) and radiocarbon dates differ; the city grew from c. 1150 and was dominant c. 1220–1441.

summary.en: Around 1441 the Xiu lineage and other nobles rose against the ruling Cocom family, killed them and sacked Mayapan. Northern Yucatán split into about 16 rival provinces, the political landscape the Spanish found when they arrived in the 1520s.
summary.zh: 约1441年，修家族和其他贵族起兵反抗统治的科科姆家族，杀死其成员并洗劫玛雅潘。尤卡坦北部分裂为约16个相互敌对的省份，这正是16世纪20年代西班牙人到来时所见的政治格局。

sources.title: Diego de Landa, Relación de las cosas de Yucatán (c. 1566)
Marilyn A. Masson & Carlos Peraza Lope, Kukulcan's Realm: Urban Life at Ancient Mayapán (2014)
Wikipedia: Mayapan

note: Spanish-era sources place the fall between 1441 and 1461; archaeology shows burning and mass graves in the mid-15th century.

story.en:
Mayapan was a joint capital: the lords of northern Yucatán's provinces were obliged to live inside its walls, where they could be watched. According to Diego de Landa, who heard the story from Maya nobles in the 1560s, the Cocom rulers grew tyrannical, bringing in Mexican mercenaries from Tabasco and selling their subjects as slaves. The Xiu, a lineage that claimed origins in the west, led a conspiracy of the other lords, who killed the Cocom king and his sons, sparing only one who was away trading in Honduras.

Archaeologists have found grim confirmation: burned buildings and a mass grave of dismembered bodies near the main temple, dated to the mid-1400s. The survivors dispersed to found provincial capitals such as Maní (Xiu) and Sotuta (Cocom). Their feud was still alive in 1536, when the Cocom murdered a Xiu pilgrimage party, and it helped the Spanish divide and conquer Yucatán.
story.zh:
玛雅潘是一座共治之都：尤卡坦北部各省领主须居于城墙之内，以便受到监视。据16世纪60年代从玛雅贵族口中听到这段往事的迭戈·德兰达记载，科科姆统治者日益暴虐，从塔巴斯科引来墨西哥雇佣兵，并把臣民卖为奴隶。自称源自西方的修家族联合其他领主密谋起事，杀死科科姆国王及其诸子，只有一个正在洪都拉斯经商的儿子幸免。

考古学家找到了令人心惊的印证：主神庙附近有被焚的建筑和一座埋着肢解尸体的乱葬坑，年代为15世纪中叶。幸存者四散，各自建立省会，如修家族的马尼和科科姆家族的索图塔。他们的世仇延续到1536年，科科姆人杀害了一支修家族的朝圣队伍；这种分裂帮助西班牙人分而治之，征服了尤卡坦。

summary.en: According to Mexica tradition, in 1325 the wandering Mexica settled on a marshy island in Lake Texcoco, where they saw an eagle perched on a prickly pear cactus, the sign promised by their god Huitzilopochtli. Their town of Tenochtitlan grew into the capital of the Aztec empire.
summary.zh: 据墨西加传统，1325年，四处迁徙的墨西加人定居在特斯科科湖中一座沼泽小岛上。他们在那里看到一只雄鹰栖于仙人掌上，正是其神维齐洛波奇特利所许诺的征兆。他们的城镇特诺奇蒂特兰后来发展为阿兹特克帝国的都城。

sources.title: Codex Mendoza, fol. 2r (Bodleian Library MS. Arch. Selden. A. 1)
Michael E. Smith, The Aztecs (3rd ed., 2012)
Britannica: Tenochtitlán
Wikipedia: Tenochtitlan

note: 1325 is the traditional date given by Mexica annals; some sources give 1345, and archaeology shows earlier settlement on the island.

story.en:
The Mexica remembered themselves as latecomers. Leaving a homeland called Aztlan, they wandered for generations, guided by the priests who carried their god Huitzilopochtli. When they reached the Valley of Mexico the best land was taken; they served as mercenaries for the town of Culhuacan, and were driven into the reed marshes after, the chronicles say, sacrificing a Culhua princess they had been given as a bride.

On a rocky islet in the lake they found the sign the god had promised: an eagle on a nopal cactus growing from a rock. The first page of the Codex Mendoza, painted for the Spanish viceroy about 1541, shows the scene with the founder Tenoch seated nearby; today the same image is on Mexico's flag. The settlers built a shrine of reeds and mud, and a twin town, Tlatelolco, was founded on a neighbouring island. Within two centuries Tenochtitlan was a city of perhaps 200,000 people joined to the shore by causeways, one of the largest cities in the world.
story.zh:
墨西加人自认是后来者。他们离开名为阿兹特兰的故乡，在背负其神维齐洛波奇特利的祭司指引下迁徙了好几代人。到达墨西哥谷地时，好地早已被占；他们为库尔瓦坎城充当雇佣兵，编年史称，他们把对方嫁给自己的一位库尔瓦公主献祭之后，便被赶进了芦苇沼泽。

在湖中一座岩石小岛上，他们看到了神所许诺的征兆：一只雄鹰栖在从岩石中长出的仙人掌上。约1541年为西班牙总督绘制的《门多萨手抄本》第一页就描绘了这一场景，创建者特诺奇坐在一旁；如今同样的图案印在墨西哥国旗上。定居者用芦苇和泥土搭起神殿，邻近岛上又建起姊妹城特拉特洛尔科。不到两个世纪，特诺奇蒂特兰已成为一座人口或达20万、以堤道与湖岸相连的城市，跻身当时世界最大城市之列。

name.en: Formation of the Aztec Triple Alliance
name.zh: 阿兹特克三国同盟的建立

summary.en: In 1428 Tenochtitlan under Itzcoatl, Texcoco under Nezahualcoyotl and Tlacopan joined forces to overthrow Maxtla and the Tepanec kingdom of Azcapotzalco. Their alliance, dominated by Tenochtitlan, built the tribute empire known today as the Aztec Empire.
summary.zh: 1428年，伊兹科阿特尔统治的特诺奇蒂特兰、内萨瓦尔科约特尔统治的特斯科科与特拉科潘联合推翻了马斯特拉和阿斯卡波察尔科的特帕内克王国。由特诺奇蒂特兰主导的这一同盟，建立起今天所称的阿兹特克帝国这一纳贡帝国。

sources.title: Michael E. Smith, The Aztecs (3rd ed., 2012)
Ross Hassig, Aztec Warfare: Imperial Expansion and Political Control (1988)
Wikipedia: Aztec Triple Alliance

note: Marker at Azcapotzalco, the defeated Tepanec capital.

story.en:
For a century the Mexica had been junior partners of Azcapotzalco, whose long-lived ruler Tezozomoc built a Tepanec empire across the valley. When he died in 1426 his son Maxtla seized power, and the young Mexica king Chimalpopoca died in mysterious circumstances, probably murdered. Texcoco's heir Nezahualcoyotl had already been driven into exile after Tepanec troops killed his father before his eyes.

The new Mexica ruler Itzcoatl, advised by his nephew Tlacaelel, chose war. With Nezahualcoyotl, the Tepanec town of Tlacopan and rebel cities such as Huexotzinco, the Mexica besieged Azcapotzalco for over 100 days in 1428 and destroyed it. The victors divided tribute by a fixed ratio, two-fifths each to Tenochtitlan and Texcoco and one-fifth to Tlacopan, although Tenochtitlan soon dominated. According to later sources, Itzcoatl then ordered older painted histories burned, so that a new official story could make the Mexica the chosen people of the sun.
story.zh:
一百年来，墨西加人一直是阿斯卡波察尔科的附属伙伴；该城长寿的君主特索索莫克在谷地建立起特帕内克帝国。1426年他死后，其子马斯特拉夺权，年轻的墨西加国王奇马尔波波卡离奇死去，很可能遭到谋杀。特斯科科王位继承人内萨瓦尔科约特尔此前已目睹特帕内克军队杀死其父，被迫流亡。

新任墨西加君主伊兹科阿特尔在侄子特拉卡埃莱尔的辅佐下决定开战。1428年，墨西加人联合内萨瓦尔科约特尔、特帕内克城镇特拉科潘以及韦霍钦戈等反叛城市，围攻阿斯卡波察尔科100多天，将其摧毁。胜利者按固定比例分配贡赋：特诺奇蒂特兰和特斯科科各得五分之二，特拉科潘得五分之一，但特诺奇蒂特兰很快占据主导。据后世史料记载，伊兹科阿特尔随后下令焚毁旧有的图画史书，以便用新的官方叙事把墨西加人塑造为太阳的选民。

summary.en: From about 1450, early frosts, snow and drought destroyed harvests in the Valley of Mexico, culminating in the famine of the year One Rabbit (1454). Moctezuma I opened the state granaries; many people sold themselves into servitude on the Gulf Coast for maize.
summary.zh: 约自1450年起，早霜、降雪和干旱接连毁坏墨西哥谷地的收成，在“一兔年”（1454年）酿成大饥荒。蒙特祖马一世打开国家粮仓；许多人为换取玉米而卖身到墨西哥湾沿岸为奴。

sources.title: Fray Diego Durán, Historia de las Indias de Nueva España (c. 1581), ch. 30
Ross Hassig, Time, History, and Belief in Aztec and Colonial Mexico (2001)
Michael E. Smith, The Aztecs (3rd ed., 2012)

note: Known from colonial-era chronicles; the year One Rabbit corresponds to 1454.

story.en:
One Rabbit (Ce Tochtli) was the first year of the Aztec 52-year cycle, and the chronicles remembered it with dread. According to Fray Diego Durán, a frost killed the maize in the fields, then came years of drought; by 1454 people were dying in the streets, and vultures and wild animals ate the bodies. Moctezuma I distributed the stores of Tenochtitlan until they ran out, then released people to find food where they could. Many went to the Totonac lands on the Gulf Coast, where maize still grew, and sold themselves or their children for a few baskets of grain.

The famine shaped imperial policy. The Triple Alliance pushed its conquests toward the fertile, rain-fed Gulf Coast, built up reserve granaries, and, according to some chronicles, began the ritual "Flower Wars" with Tlaxcala and its neighbours, battles fought to capture sacrificial victims who would feed the gods and keep such disasters away. Ever after, the Aztecs dreaded the coming of a One Rabbit year.
story.zh:
“一兔年”是阿兹特克52年周期的第一年，编年史对它记忆犹新、心存畏惧。据迭戈·杜兰修士记载，一场霜冻冻死了田里的玉米，随后是连年干旱；到1454年，人们倒毙街头，秃鹫和野兽啃食尸体。蒙特祖马一世分发特诺奇蒂特兰的存粮，直到耗尽，随后让百姓自行谋食。许多人前往墨西哥湾沿岸仍有玉米生长的托托纳克人地区，为几篮粮食卖掉自己或子女。

饥荒影响了帝国的政策。三国同盟将征服方向推向肥沃且雨水充沛的墨西哥湾沿岸，扩建储备粮仓；据一些编年史记载，还开始与特拉斯卡拉及其邻邦进行仪式性的“花之战争”，以捕获献祭者供奉众神，防止此类灾祸再临。此后，阿兹特克人始终畏惧“一兔年”的到来。

summary.en: From the mid-15th century the Triple Alliance fought recurring ritual battles, the xochiyaoyotl or "flower wars", with Tlaxcala, Huexotzinco and Cholula. Fought by appointment, they trained warriors and supplied captives for sacrifice, while leaving Tlaxcala independent and bitterly hostile, a fatal weakness in 1519.
summary.zh: 自15世纪中叶起，三国同盟与特拉斯卡拉、韦霍钦戈、乔卢拉反复进行仪式性的“花之战争”。这些约定日期的战斗既训练武士，又为献祭提供俘虏，同时也使特拉斯卡拉保持独立并对阿兹特克人怀有深仇，这在1519年成为致命的弱点。

sources.title: Ross Hassig, Aztec Warfare: Imperial Expansion and Political Control (1988)
Wikipedia: Flower war
Michael E. Smith, The Aztecs (3rd ed., 2012)

note: Whether the wars were truly ritual or a cover for a failed conquest is debated (Hassig argues the latter). Marker at Tlaxcala.

name.en: Tarascans defeat the Aztec army of Axayacatl
name.zh: 塔拉斯坎人击败阿哈雅卡特尔的阿兹特克军队

summary.en: An Aztec army led by the huey tlatoani Axayacatl invaded the Tarascan kingdom of Michoacán and was crushed near Taximaroa by a larger Tarascan force under the cazonci Tzitzipandácuare. It was the worst defeat in Aztec history, and the two empires afterwards faced each other across a fortified frontier.
summary.zh: 阿兹特克大君主阿哈雅卡特尔率军入侵米却肯的塔拉斯坎王国，在塔希马罗阿附近被卡宗西（国王）齐齐潘达夸雷统率的更大兵力击溃。这是阿兹特克历史上最惨重的失败，此后两大帝国隔着设防的边境对峙。

sources.title: Helen Perlstein Pollard, Tariacuri's Legacy: The Prehispanic Tarascan State (1993)
Fray Diego Durán, Historia de las Indias de Nueva España (c. 1581)
Wikipedia: Purépecha Empire

note: Sources give 1478 or 1479; casualty figures (e.g. 20,000 of 24,000 Aztec soldiers lost, per Durán) are probably exaggerated. Marker at Taximaroa (modern Ciudad Hidalgo, Michoacán).

story.en:
West of the Aztec empire lay the one state it never conquered. The Tarascans (P'urhépecha) of Lake Pátzcuaro had been united by the warlord Tariácuri in the 14th century and ruled from Tzintzuntzan, "place of hummingbirds". They spoke a language unrelated to any neighbour and were Mesoamerica's best metalworkers, making copper and bronze tools, bells and weapons.

Around 1479 Axayacatl marched on Michoacán. According to Fray Diego Durán, who wrote from Aztec accounts, scouts reported the Tarascan host at some 40,000, nearly twice the Aztec army; the battle raged for a day and the Aztecs were routed, most of their soldiers killed or captured. Axayacatl limped home and staged a great mourning in Tenochtitlan.

Afterwards both sides built forts along the border, and the Aztecs never attacked again. In 1520, when Moctezuma's envoys asked the Tarascans for help against the Spaniards, the cazonci Zuangua refused, and his successor submitted to Spain in 1522.
story.zh:
阿兹特克帝国以西，有一个它始终未能征服的国家。帕茨夸罗湖畔的塔拉斯坎人（普雷佩查人）在14世纪由军事首领塔里亚库里统一，以“蜂鸟之地”钦聪灿为都。他们的语言与周边民族毫无亲缘关系，也是中美洲最出色的金属工匠，能制作铜质和青铜工具、铃铛与武器。

约1479年，阿哈雅卡特尔进军米却肯。据根据阿兹特克人叙述写作的迭戈·杜兰修士记载，斥候报告塔拉斯坎大军约有4万，几乎是阿兹特克军队的两倍；战斗持续了一整天，阿兹特克人溃败，大部分士兵被杀或被俘。阿哈雅卡特尔狼狈而归，在特诺奇蒂特兰举行了盛大的哀悼。

此后双方都沿边境修筑要塞，阿兹特克人再未进攻。1520年，蒙特祖马的使者请求塔拉斯坎人协助对抗西班牙人，卡宗西苏安瓜予以拒绝；其继任者于1522年归顺西班牙。

summary.en: In 1487 the huey tlatoani Ahuitzotl rededicated the enlarged Great Temple of Tenochtitlan, with twin shrines to Huitzilopochtli and the rain god Tlaloc, in a ceremony that colonial chroniclers said involved the sacrifice of tens of thousands of captives.
summary.zh: 1487年，大君主阿维索特尔为扩建后的特诺奇蒂特兰大神庙重新举行落成典礼。神庙顶上并立维齐洛波奇特利和雨神特拉洛克的双神殿。殖民时期的编年史称，典礼献祭了数以万计的俘虏。

sources.title: Eduardo Matos Moctezuma, The Great Temple of the Aztecs: Treasures of Tenochtitlan (1988)
Fray Diego Durán, Historia de las Indias de Nueva España (c. 1581), ch. 44
Wikipedia: Templo Mayor

note: Durán's figure of 80,400 victims is widely regarded as exaggerated; modern estimates are far lower but uncertain.

story.en:
The Templo Mayor was rebuilt at least seven times, each new pyramid enclosing the last, like nesting boxes. Ahuitzotl's enlargement was completed in the year Eight Reed, 1487. According to Fray Diego Durán, rulers of allied and enemy states were invited to watch as lines of captives from the Huastec and other campaigns climbed the steps for four days; he gives the number as 80,400. Few modern historians accept such a figure, but the ceremony was meant to awe.

The temple was razed after the conquest and lost under colonial Mexico City. On 21 February 1978, electricians digging behind the cathedral struck a huge carved disc: the goddess Coyolxauhqui, dismembered by her brother Huitzilopochtli, exactly as myth told. The excavation that followed, led by Eduardo Matos Moctezuma, uncovered the temple's stages and thousands of offerings, and in 2006 a monolith of the earth goddess Tlaltecuhtli, the largest Aztec sculpture yet found.
story.zh:
大神庙至少重建过七次，每座新金字塔都把前一座包在里面，层层相套。阿维索特尔的扩建于“八芦苇年”即1487年完工。据迭戈·杜兰修士记载，盟邦和敌国的君主都受邀观礼，来自瓦斯特克等战役的俘虏排成长队，四天里不断登上台阶；他给出的数字是80400人。现代史学家很少接受这一数字，但这场典礼的用意正在于震慑。

征服之后，神庙被夷平，湮没在殖民时代的墨西哥城之下。1978年2月21日，电工在大教堂后方挖掘时碰到一块巨大的雕刻圆盘：被其兄长维齐洛波奇特利肢解的女神科约尔沙乌基，与神话所述完全一致。随后由爱德华多·马托斯·蒙特祖马主持的发掘揭露了神庙的各个建造阶段和数千件祭品，2006年又发现了大地女神特拉尔特库特利的巨石雕像，这是迄今发现的最大的阿兹特克雕刻。

name.en: La Isabela, first Spanish town in the Americas
name.zh: 伊莎贝拉城：西班牙人在美洲的第一座城镇

summary.en: On his second voyage, Columbus found the fort of La Navidad destroyed and in January 1494 founded La Isabela on the north coast of Hispaniola with some 1,500 settlers. Disease, hunger and mutiny plagued it, and it was abandoned by about 1498 in favour of Santo Domingo.
summary.zh: 哥伦布第二次航行时发现纳维达德要塞已被毁，遂于1494年1月率约1500名移民在伊斯帕尼奥拉岛北岸建立伊莎贝拉城。疾病、饥饿和哗变不断困扰此地，约1498年它被放弃，人们迁往圣多明各。

sources.title: Kathleen Deagan & José María Cruxent, Columbus's Outpost among the Taínos: Spain and America at La Isabela, 1493–1498 (2002)
Wikipedia: La Isabela
Britannica: Christopher Columbus

note: Columbus's first voyage (1492) is recorded in the europe dataset as ev-columbus-first-voyage.

story.en:
Columbus returned to Hispaniola in November 1493 with 17 ships, about 1,500 men, horses, pigs, seeds and sugar cane. At La Navidad, where he had left 39 sailors from the wrecked Santa María, he found burned houses and bodies; the local cacique Guacanagarí blamed the rival chief Caonabo, whose people the Spaniards had abused.

He chose a new site on a bluff farther east and began building a stone church, a storehouse and a house for himself. Excavations led by Kathleen Deagan and José María Cruxent in the 1990s found the outlines of the town and the remains of its pottery kilns and assaying furnace, built to test gold. The colonists, many of them hidalgos who refused manual labour, fell sick within weeks. Food ran short, gold was scarce, and Columbus began forcing Taíno villages to deliver a quota of gold dust every three months. Within four years the town was all but empty, and the colony moved south to the new port of Santo Domingo.
story.zh:
1493年11月，哥伦布率17艘船、约1500人，带着马匹、猪、种子和甘蔗重返伊斯帕尼奥拉岛。在他曾留下圣玛丽亚号39名水手的纳维达德，他只看到焚毁的房屋和尸体；当地酋长瓜卡纳加里把责任推给敌对酋长卡奥纳沃，后者的族人曾受西班牙人虐待。

他在更东边的一处崖地选了新址，开始修建石砌教堂、仓库和自己的住宅。20世纪90年代，凯瑟琳·迪根和何塞·玛丽亚·克鲁森特主持的发掘找到了城镇轮廓，以及用于烧制陶器的窑和检验黄金的化验炉遗迹。移民中许多是不肯干体力活的小贵族，几周内便病倒了。粮食短缺，黄金稀少，哥伦布开始强迫泰诺村庄每三个月缴纳定额金砂。不到四年，城镇几乎人去楼空，殖民地南迁至新港口圣多明各。

summary.en: Bartholomew Columbus founded a settlement at the mouth of the Ozama River in 1496; after a hurricane in 1502 Governor Nicolás de Ovando rebuilt it on the west bank. Santo Domingo became the first seat of Spanish government in the Americas, with the first cathedral, hospital and royal court (Audiencia, 1511).
summary.zh: 1496年，巴尔托洛梅·哥伦布在奥萨马河口建立定居点；1502年飓风之后，总督尼古拉斯·德奥万多在西岸重建该城。圣多明各成为西班牙在美洲的第一个统治中心，拥有美洲第一座主教座堂、第一所医院和第一个王室检审法院（1511年）。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Colonial City of Santo Domingo
Britannica: Santo Domingo
Wikipedia: Santo Domingo

note: Founding dates of 1496 and 1498 are both found; the 1502 move is undisputed.

name.en: Jaragua massacre and execution of Anacaona
name.zh: 哈拉瓜大屠杀与阿纳卡奥纳之死

summary.en: In 1503 Governor Nicolás de Ovando visited the Taíno chiefdom of Xaragua in western Hispaniola, where the cacica Anacaona received him with a feast. On a signal his men seized the assembled chiefs, burned many alive in a meeting house and later hanged Anacaona, breaking the last independent Taíno chiefdom.
summary.zh: 1503年，总督尼古拉斯·德奥万多来到伊斯帕尼奥拉岛西部的泰诺酋邦哈拉瓜，女酋长阿纳卡奥纳设宴款待。他一声令下，手下抓住与会的众酋长，把许多人关在议事厅里活活烧死，随后绞死阿纳卡奥纳，最后一个独立的泰诺酋邦就此瓦解。

sources.title: Bartolomé de las Casas, Historia de las Indias (written 1527–1561)
Irving Rouse, The Tainos: Rise and Decline of the People Who Greeted Columbus (1992)
Wikipedia: Jaragua massacre

note: Known mainly from Las Casas, who arrived in Hispaniola in 1502; the exact site, near Léogâne in modern Haiti, is approximate.

name.zh: 安东尼奥·德蒙特西诺斯的将临期布道

summary.en: On the fourth Sunday of Advent 1511, the Dominican friar Antonio de Montesinos told the Spanish colonists of Santo Domingo that they were in mortal sin for their cruelty to the Taíno. The outcry led to the Laws of Burgos of 1512, the first Spanish code regulating the treatment of Indigenous people.
summary.zh: 1511年将临期第四主日，多明我会修士安东尼奥·德蒙特西诺斯在圣多明各告诫西班牙殖民者，他们对泰诺人的残暴使自己身陷死罪。此言引起轩然大波，促成1512年的《布尔戈斯法》，这是西班牙第一部规范对待原住民的法典。

sources.title: Bartolomé de las Casas, Historia de las Indias (written 1527–1561)
Lewis Hanke, The Spanish Struggle for Justice in the Conquest of America (1949)
Wikipedia: Antonio de Montesinos
Wikipedia: Laws of Burgos

story.en:
The Dominicans had been in Hispaniola for barely a year when they agreed, as a community, that what they saw could not be ignored. The Taíno population had collapsed under forced labour in mines and fields under the encomienda system. On 21 December 1511, before an audience that included Governor Diego Colón, son of Columbus, Antonio de Montesinos preached on the text "I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness."

According to Las Casas, who recorded the sermon, he demanded to know by what right the settlers held the Indians in such cruel servitude, and asked: "Are they not men?" The colonists demanded a retraction; the next Sunday Montesinos repeated the charge more forcefully.

Both sides sailed to Spain to lobby King Ferdinand. The result, the Laws of Burgos of December 1512, limited working hours and required instruction and food, but kept the encomienda. Among those who heard the friars was a young encomendero, Bartolomé de las Casas, who would make their cause his life's work.
story.zh:
多明我会修士到伊斯帕尼奥拉岛才刚满一年，便集体认定不能对眼前所见视而不见。在委托监护制下，泰诺人在矿山和田地里被强制劳作，人口锐减。1511年12月21日，面对包括哥伦布之子、总督迭戈·哥伦布在内的听众，安东尼奥·德蒙特西诺斯以“我是旷野里呼喊者的声音”为题布道。

据记录这次布道的拉斯卡萨斯所述，他质问殖民者凭什么权利让印第安人处于如此残酷的奴役之中，并问道：“他们难道不是人吗？”殖民者要求他收回言论；下一个主日，蒙特西诺斯更加激烈地重申了指控。

双方都渡海回西班牙游说斐迪南国王。结果是1512年12月的《布尔戈斯法》，它限制劳动时间，规定须提供宗教教导和食物，但保留了委托监护制。听过修士们布道的人中，有一位年轻的委托监护主巴托洛梅·德拉斯·卡萨斯，他后来把修士们的事业当作毕生使命。

name.en: Spanish conquest of Cuba and the death of Hatuey
name.zh: 西班牙征服古巴与阿土伊之死

summary.en: Diego Velázquez de Cuéllar landed near Baracoa in 1511 and conquered Cuba within three years. The Taíno cacique Hatuey, who had fled from Hispaniola to warn the Cubans, led the resistance until he was captured and burned at the stake in 1512.
summary.zh: 1511年，迭戈·贝拉斯克斯·德奎利亚尔在巴拉科阿附近登陆，三年内征服古巴。从伊斯帕尼奥拉岛逃来警告古巴人的泰诺酋长阿土伊领导抵抗，直到1512年被俘并被处以火刑。

sources.title: Bartolomé de las Casas, Historia de las Indias (written 1527–1561)
Bartolomé de las Casas, Brevísima relación de la destrucción de las Indias (1552)
Irene A. Wright, The Early History of Cuba, 1492–1586 (1916)
Wikipedia: Hatuey

note: Marker at Baracoa, the first Spanish town in Cuba (1511).

story.en:
Hatuey was a cacique from the Guahaba region of Hispaniola who crossed to eastern Cuba with a band of followers as the Spaniards tightened their grip on his island. According to Las Casas, who served as a chaplain in the Cuban campaign, Hatuey gathered the Cuban chiefs, showed them a basket of gold and told them that this was the god the Christians worshipped, for which they would kill and enslave. He urged the Cubans to throw it in the river.

For months his warriors harassed Velázquez's men in the hills, but he was betrayed and captured. Tied to the stake, the story goes, a Franciscan urged him to accept baptism so that he would go to heaven. Hatuey asked whether Christians went to heaven; told that good ones did, he replied that he would rather not go there, so as not to meet such cruel people. The anecdote, retold by Las Casas in his Brief Account of 1552, made Hatuey a symbol of resistance; he is remembered in Cuba as its first national hero.
story.zh:
阿土伊是伊斯帕尼奥拉岛瓜阿瓦地区的酋长，当西班牙人加紧控制该岛时，他率众渡海来到古巴东部。据曾随军出征古巴担任随军神父的拉斯卡萨斯记载，阿土伊召集古巴各酋长，向他们展示一篮黄金，说这就是基督徒崇拜的神，他们会为它杀人、奴役他人。他劝古巴人把黄金扔进河里。

他的战士们在山中袭扰贝拉斯克斯的部队达数月之久，但他最终遭人出卖被俘。据说，他被绑上火刑柱时，一位方济各会修士劝他受洗，以便升入天堂。阿土伊问基督徒是否也上天堂；听说好的基督徒会去，他答道，那他宁可不去，免得再遇见如此残忍的人。这段轶事经拉斯卡萨斯写入1552年的《西印度毁灭述略》，使阿土伊成为抵抗的象征；古巴人至今把他纪念为第一位民族英雄。

name.en: Balboa crosses the Isthmus of Panama to the Pacific
name.zh: 巴尔沃亚穿越巴拿马地峡抵达太平洋

summary.en: In September 1513 Vasco Núñez de Balboa led about 190 Spaniards and hundreds of Indigenous guides and porters across the Darién jungle. On 25 September he saw the Pacific from a mountaintop, and on 29 September he waded into the Gulf of San Miguel and claimed the "South Sea" for Castile.
summary.zh: 1513年9月，瓦斯科·努涅斯·德巴尔沃亚率约190名西班牙人和数百名原住民向导、脚夫穿越达连丛林。9月25日他在山顶望见太平洋，9月29日涉入圣米格尔湾，宣布“南海”归卡斯蒂利亚所有。

sources.title: Kathleen Romoli, Balboa of Darién: Discoverer of the Pacific (1953)
Britannica: Vasco Núñez de Balboa
Wikipedia: Vasco Núñez de Balboa

note: Marker at the Gulf of San Miguel, Panama, where Balboa took possession of the sea.

story.en:
Balboa had arrived in Darién in 1510 as a stowaway, hiding in a barrel to escape his creditors on Hispaniola. He rose to lead the struggling colony of Santa María la Antigua, and from local rulers heard of another sea to the south and of a land rich in gold beyond it. The son of the cacique Comagre reportedly told the Spaniards, as they quarrelled over a gift of gold, that if they cared so much for it he could show them a sea where people ate and drank from golden vessels.

In September 1513 Balboa set out with 190 Spaniards, dogs and a large Indigenous force, fighting some chiefs and allying with others. On 25 September, by the traditional account, he climbed ahead alone to a summit and became the first European to see the Pacific from the Americas. Four days later, sword in hand and holding a banner of the Virgin, he walked into the waters of the gulf he named San Miguel.

His rival Pedrarias Dávila, the new governor, had him tried for treason and beheaded at Acla in 1519. The way to Peru that Balboa had opened was followed by Francisco Pizarro, who had been at his side in 1513.
story.zh:
1510年，巴尔沃亚躲在一只木桶里偷渡到达连，以躲避伊斯帕尼奥拉岛上的债主。他后来成为艰难求存的圣玛丽亚-安提瓜殖民地的首领，从当地统治者那里听说南方还有一片海洋，海那边有遍地黄金的国度。据说，当西班牙人为一份黄金礼物争吵时，酋长科马格雷之子对他们说，既然他们如此看重黄金，他可以带他们去一片海边，那里的人用金器吃喝。

1513年9月，巴尔沃亚带着190名西班牙人、猎犬和大批原住民队伍出发，一路上与一些酋长交战，同另一些结盟。按照传统说法，9月25日他独自先行登上一座山顶，成为第一个从美洲望见太平洋的欧洲人。四天后，他手持长剑，举着圣母旗帜，走进他命名为圣米格尔的海湾。

他的对手、新任总督佩德拉里亚斯·达维拉以叛国罪审判他，1519年在阿克拉将其斩首。巴尔沃亚开辟的通往秘鲁之路，后来由1513年曾随他同行的弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗走完。

summary.en: The Taíno cacique Enriquillo, raised by Franciscans, rebelled after a Spaniard abused his wife and courts denied him justice. From the Bahoruco mountains of Hispaniola he held off Spanish forces for 14 years until a 1533 treaty granted his people freedom and land.
summary.zh: 由方济各会修士抚养长大的泰诺酋长恩里基约，因妻子受西班牙人凌辱而诉诸法庭无门，遂起兵反抗。他在伊斯帕尼奥拉岛的巴奥鲁科山区抵御西班牙军队达14年，直到1533年签订和约，其族人获得自由与土地。

sources.title: Bartolomé de las Casas, Historia de las Indias (written 1527–1561)
Irving Rouse, The Tainos: Rise and Decline of the People Who Greeted Columbus (1992)
Wikipedia: Enriquillo

name.en: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire
name.zh: 西班牙征服阿兹特克帝国

summary.en: Hernán Cortés landed on the Gulf Coast in 1519 with about 500 Spaniards. Allied with Totonacs and above all Tlaxcalans, he entered Tenochtitlan, lost it in 1520, and returned with tens of thousands of Indigenous allies and brigantines to besiege and destroy the city in 1521, ending the Aztec Empire.
summary.zh: 1519年，埃尔南·科尔特斯率约500名西班牙人在墨西哥湾沿岸登陆。他与托托纳克人、尤其是特拉斯卡拉人结盟，进入特诺奇蒂特兰，1520年被逐出，随后率数万原住民盟军和双桅帆船卷土重来，于1521年围攻并摧毁该城，阿兹特克帝国由此灭亡。
