sources.title: Hernán Cortés, Cartas de relación (1519–1526)
Bernal Díaz del Castillo, Historia verdadera de la conquista de la Nueva España (written c. 1568)
Hugh Thomas, Conquest: Montezuma, Cortés, and the Fall of Old Mexico (1993)
Matthew Restall, When Montezuma Met Cortés: The True Story of the Meeting That Changed History (2018)
Wikipedia: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire

story.en:
Cortés sailed from Cuba in February 1519 in defiance of the governor who had commissioned him. At Cozumel he recovered Jerónimo de Aguilar, a shipwrecked Spaniard who spoke Yucatec Maya; at Potonchán in Tabasco he was given twenty women, among them Malintzin, who spoke Nahuatl. Through this chain of two interpreters he could talk with Moctezuma's envoys, who arrived with gifts of gold and featherwork that only sharpened Spanish appetites. He founded a town, Villa Rica de la Vera Cruz, so that its council could give him legal authority, and scuttled his ships to stop deserters.

The decisive alliance was with Tlaxcala, the Aztecs' unconquered enemy, which fought the Spaniards for three weeks and then joined them. After the meeting with Moctezuma in November 1519 the Spaniards held him hostage. The massacre at the Toxcatl festival, the Noche Triste and a smallpox epidemic followed. In 1521, with perhaps 1,000 Spaniards and tens of thousands of Tlaxcalan, Texcocan and other allies, Cortés besieged the island city for 93 days with thirteen brigantines on the lake, cutting its water and food. Most historians now stress that the conquest was as much an Indigenous war against Tenochtitlan as a Spanish victory.
story.zh:
1519年2月，科尔特斯违抗委任他的古巴总督之命扬帆出发。在科苏梅尔岛，他救回了会说尤卡坦玛雅语的落难西班牙人赫罗尼莫·德阿吉拉尔；在塔巴斯科的波通昌，他得到二十名女子，其中包括会说纳瓦特尔语的马林钦。借助这两位译员组成的翻译链，他得以与蒙特祖马的使者交谈；使者带来的黄金和羽毛工艺礼物只是更加刺激了西班牙人的贪欲。他建立了富庶的真十字架镇，以便由镇议会授予他合法权力，并凿沉船只以防有人逃跑。

决定性的联盟是与阿兹特克人从未征服的宿敌特拉斯卡拉结成的：特拉斯卡拉与西班牙人激战三周后转而加入他们。1519年11月会见蒙特祖马后，西班牙人将他扣为人质。随后发生了托什卡特尔节大屠杀、悲痛之夜和天花流行。1521年，科尔特斯率约1000名西班牙人和数万特拉斯卡拉、特斯科科等盟军，以湖上的13艘双桅帆船围困这座岛城93天，切断其饮水和粮食。如今多数史学家强调，这场征服既是西班牙人的胜利，也同样是一场原住民对特诺奇蒂特兰的战争。

summary.en: In October 1519, at the sacred city of Cholula, Cortés's men and their Tlaxcalan allies killed several thousand unarmed nobles and townspeople gathered in a temple courtyard, claiming to have uncovered a plot against them. The massacre terrorised the cities of central Mexico before the Spaniards reached Tenochtitlan.
summary.zh: 1519年10月，在圣城乔卢拉，科尔特斯的部下及其特拉斯卡拉盟军声称识破了针对他们的阴谋，在一座神庙庭院里杀害了聚集于此、手无寸铁的数千名贵族和市民。这场屠杀在西班牙人抵达特诺奇蒂特兰之前震慑了墨西哥中部各城。

sources.title: Hernán Cortés, Cartas de relación (1519–1526)
Bernal Díaz del Castillo, Historia verdadera de la conquista de la Nueva España (written c. 1568)
Bernardino de Sahagún, Florentine Codex, Book XII (1577)
Wikipedia: Cholula massacre

note: Spanish accounts say Malintzin learned of the plot from a local noblewoman; Indigenous accounts blame Tlaxcalan instigation. Death toll estimates range from 3,000 to 6,000.

name.zh: 大神庙大屠杀（托什卡特尔节）

summary.en: In May 1520, while Cortés was away fighting Pánfilo de Narváez on the coast, Pedro de Alvarado attacked the Mexica nobility as they danced at the festival of Toxcatl in the Templo Mayor precinct, killing hundreds or thousands. The city rose against the Spaniards, who were besieged in their palace.
summary.zh: 1520年5月，科尔特斯前往海岸与潘菲洛·德纳瓦埃斯作战期间，佩德罗·德阿尔瓦拉多趁墨西加贵族在大神庙区庆祝托什卡特尔节跳舞之机发动袭击，杀死数百乃至数千人。全城奋起反抗，西班牙人被围困在宫殿中。

sources.title: Bernardino de Sahagún, Florentine Codex, Book XII, ch. 19–20 (1577)
Bernal Díaz del Castillo, Historia verdadera de la conquista de la Nueva España (written c. 1568)
Wikipedia: Massacre in the Great Temple of Tenochtitlan

story.en:
Toxcatl was the great spring festival of Huitzilopochtli and Tezcatlipoca. The Mexica had asked permission to hold it while Moctezuma was a captive, and Pedro de Alvarado, left in command of about 120 Spaniards, had agreed. On the day itself, with the young warriors and nobles gathered unarmed in the temple courtyard, singing and dancing to drums, Spanish soldiers closed the gates and attacked.

The Nahua elders who told the story to Sahagún's students a generation later remembered it with terrible precision: the drummer's arms were cut off, then his head; dancers were stabbed from behind, disembowelled, or cut down as they tried to climb the walls. Alvarado later claimed he had struck to forestall a planned uprising, and some historians suspect fear and greed drove him.

The massacre turned the city against the Spaniards. When Cortés returned in June with reinforcements, he found Alvarado besieged; within weeks Moctezuma was dead and the Spaniards had to fight their way out on the Noche Triste.
story.zh:
托什卡特尔节是供奉维齐洛波奇特利和特斯卡特利波卡的春季盛典。蒙特祖马被囚期间，墨西加人请求照常举行，留下指挥约120名西班牙人的佩德罗·德阿尔瓦拉多表示同意。到了节日当天，年轻武士和贵族手无寸铁地聚集在神庙庭院里，随着鼓声歌舞，西班牙士兵却关上大门发动袭击。

一代人之后，向萨阿贡的学生讲述此事的纳瓦长老们记忆犹新、细节惨烈：鼓手先被砍断双臂，随后被斩首；舞者从背后被刺穿、开膛，或在试图翻墙时被砍倒。阿尔瓦拉多后来声称，他是为了先发制人、阻止一场预谋的起义；一些史学家则怀疑他是出于恐惧和贪婪。

这场屠杀使全城与西班牙人反目。6月科尔特斯带着援军返回时，发现阿尔瓦拉多已被围困；几周之内，蒙特祖马死去，西班牙人只得在悲痛之夜杀出重围。

summary.en: On the rainy night of 30 June–1 July 1520 the Spaniards and Tlaxcalans tried to slip out of Tenochtitlan along the Tlacopan causeway. Discovered, they were attacked from canoes; hundreds of Spaniards and thousands of allies died, many drowned under the weight of looted gold.
summary.zh: 1520年6月30日至7月1日的雨夜，西班牙人和特拉斯卡拉人试图沿特拉科潘堤道悄悄撤出特诺奇蒂特兰。他们被发现后遭到独木舟上敌军的袭击，数百名西班牙人和数千名盟军丧生，许多人因身负劫掠的黄金沉入水中溺亡。

sources.title: Bernal Díaz del Castillo, Historia verdadera de la conquista de la Nueva España (written c. 1568)
Hernán Cortés, Cartas de relación (1519–1526)
Hugh Thomas, Conquest: Montezuma, Cortés, and the Fall of Old Mexico (1993)
Wikipedia: La Noche Triste

note: Marker at the "Árbol de la Noche Triste" in Popotla, on the old Tlacopan causeway, where tradition says Cortés wept.

story.en:
By late June 1520 the Spanish position in Tenochtitlan was hopeless. Moctezuma had died, either killed by stones thrown by his own people when he tried to calm them, as Spanish sources claim, or murdered by the Spaniards, as Indigenous sources say. The Mexica had chosen a new ruler, Cuitláhuac, and had lifted the bridges in the causeways.

Cortés decided to break out at midnight, carrying a portable wooden bridge. A woman drawing water raised the alarm, and war drums sounded from the Templo Mayor. Warriors in canoes attacked the column from both sides as it crowded along the causeway. When the portable bridge jammed, the gaps filled with bodies, horses and baggage. Bernal Díaz wrote that men who had stuffed their clothes with gold sank first. Alvarado, according to legend, escaped by vaulting a gap with his lance.

Tradition says Cortés sat under a cypress at Popotla and wept for the dead. He had lost perhaps 600 Spaniards, most of the horses and the treasure, and thousands of Tlaxcalans. A week later, the survivors fought their way through at Otumba and reached Tlaxcala, which stayed loyal.
story.zh:
到1520年6月下旬，西班牙人在特诺奇蒂特兰的处境已毫无希望。蒙特祖马已死：西班牙史料称他在劝说民众时被自己的子民用石块砸死，原住民史料则说他是被西班牙人杀害的。墨西加人已推举新君主奎特拉瓦克，并拆掉了堤道上的桥梁。

科尔特斯决定午夜突围，并携带一座可移动的木桥。一个打水的妇女发出警报，大神庙上响起战鼓。独木舟上的战士从两侧袭击挤在堤道上的队伍。可移动木桥卡住后，缺口被尸体、马匹和辎重填满。贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯写道，把黄金塞满衣服的人最先沉下去。据传说，阿尔瓦拉多用长矛撑地跃过缺口才得以逃生。

相传科尔特斯坐在波波特拉的一棵柏树下为死者哭泣。他损失了约600名西班牙人、大部分马匹和全部财宝，以及数千名特拉斯卡拉人。一周后，幸存者在奥通巴杀出血路，抵达始终忠诚的特拉斯卡拉。

name.zh: 墨西哥中部天花大流行

summary.en: Smallpox, carried to the Gulf Coast in 1520 with Pánfilo de Narváez's expedition, swept through central Mexico in the autumn of that year. It killed a large share of the population of Tenochtitlan, including the new ruler Cuitláhuac, and weakened the Mexica before the final siege.
summary.zh: 1520年，天花随潘菲洛·德纳瓦埃斯的远征队传到墨西哥湾沿岸，当年秋天席卷墨西哥中部。它夺去了特诺奇蒂特兰大量人口的生命，包括新君主奎特拉瓦克，使墨西加人在最后的围城战前元气大伤。

sources.title: Bernardino de Sahagún, Florentine Codex, Book XII, ch. 29 (1577)
Noble David Cook, Born to Die: Disease and New World Conquest, 1492–1650 (1998)
Alfred W. Crosby, The Columbian Exchange (1972)

note: Spanish chroniclers attribute the outbreak to an infected African member of Narváez's party; mortality figures are estimates.

story.en:
Smallpox had reached Hispaniola in late 1518 and wiped out much of what remained of the Taíno. In April 1520 an expedition under Pánfilo de Narváez, sent from Cuba to arrest Cortés, landed near Cempoala; according to the friar Motolinía and others, one of its men, an enslaved African, was sick with the disease.

The Nahua accounts collected by Sahagún describe what came in the month of Tepeilhuitl, autumn 1520: a great sickness of pustules that covered the face, chest and belly, so painful that people could not move or turn over, and many died of hunger because no one was left to cook. It lasted seventy days in Tenochtitlan. Among the dead was Cuitláhuac, who had driven the Spaniards out on the Noche Triste and ruled for only eighty days.

Nobody knows how many died; estimates for central Mexico run from a quarter to nearly half of the population. Cuauhtémoc, a young cousin, defended a city of the sick and grieving when the Spaniards returned in 1521.
story.zh:
天花于1518年底传到伊斯帕尼奥拉岛，几乎消灭了残存的泰诺人。1520年4月，从古巴派来逮捕科尔特斯的潘菲洛·德纳瓦埃斯远征队在森波阿拉附近登陆；据莫托利尼亚修士等人记载，队中一名被奴役的非洲人染有此病。

萨阿贡收集的纳瓦人叙述描述了1520年秋“特佩伊尔维特尔月”到来的灾难：一种大疮病布满脸、胸和腹部，疼得人无法动弹、无法翻身；许多人因无人做饭而饿死。疫情在特诺奇蒂特兰持续了70天。死者中有在悲痛之夜赶走西班牙人、仅在位80天的奎特拉瓦克。

无人知晓死亡人数；对墨西哥中部的估计从四分之一到近一半人口不等。1521年西班牙人卷土重来时，年轻的堂弟夸乌特莫克守卫的是一座满是病人和哀伤者的城市。

summary.en: After a 93-day siege by Spanish troops, brigantines and tens of thousands of Indigenous allies, Tenochtitlan fell on 13 August 1521 when Cuauhtémoc was captured fleeing by canoe from Tlatelolco. The city was razed and Mexico City built on its ruins.
summary.zh: 经过西班牙军队、双桅帆船和数万原住民盟军93天的围攻，1521年8月13日，夸乌特莫克乘独木舟从特拉特洛尔科出逃时被俘，特诺奇蒂特兰陷落。全城被夷平，墨西哥城在其废墟上建起。

sources.title: Hernán Cortés, Cartas de relación (1519–1526)
Bernardino de Sahagún, Florentine Codex, Book XII (1577)
Miguel León-Portilla (ed.), The Broken Spears: The Aztec Account of the Conquest of Mexico (1962)
Wikipedia: Fall of Tenochtitlan

story.en:
The siege began in late May 1521. Cortés's carpenter Martín López had built thirteen brigantines at Texcoco, which were carried in pieces by Tlaxcalan porters and launched on the lake; with them the Spaniards could break the canoe fleets and cover the causeways. Allies from Texcoco, Tlaxcala, Huexotzinco, Chalco and other towns, perhaps 70,000 or more, filled the canals with rubble from demolished houses so that horses and cannon could advance.

The Mexica fought block by block. A Nahua lament recorded after the conquest describes broken spears scattered in the roads and mourners tearing their hair. The people ate lizards, grass and adobe; the water turned brackish after the aqueduct from Chapultepec was cut. On 13 August, the day One Serpent, Cuauhtémoc tried to escape by canoe and was captured. Brought before Cortés, he reportedly touched the Spaniard's dagger and asked to be killed.

A plaque in the present-day Plaza of the Three Cultures describes the fall as neither a triumph nor a defeat, but the painful birth of mestizo Mexico.
story.zh:
围城始于1521年5月下旬。科尔特斯的木匠马丁·洛佩斯在特斯科科造了13艘双桅帆船，由特拉斯卡拉脚夫分拆运抵湖边下水；有了它们，西班牙人便能击溃独木舟船队、掩护堤道。来自特斯科科、特拉斯卡拉、韦霍钦戈、查尔科等城的盟军或达7万人以上，他们用拆毁房屋的碎石填平运河，好让马匹和大炮推进。

墨西加人逐街逐巷地抵抗。征服后记录下来的一首纳瓦哀歌描述了路上散落的断矛和撕扯头发的哀悼者。人们吃蜥蜴、野草和土坯；通往查普尔特佩克的引水渠被切断后，饮水变得咸涩。8月13日，即“一蛇日”，夸乌特莫克试图乘独木舟逃走时被俘。据说，他被带到科尔特斯面前时，摸着这个西班牙人的匕首，请求被处死。

如今三文化广场上的一块铭牌把这场陷落描述为既非胜利也非失败，而是梅斯蒂索人的墨西哥痛苦的诞生。

summary.en: In 1524 Pedro de Alvarado marched from Mexico with Spaniards and thousands of Nahua allies, defeated the K'iche' Maya near Quetzaltenango, burned their capital Q'umarkaj with its kings, and founded Santiago at the Kaqchikel capital Iximché, whose people soon rebelled against him.
summary.zh: 1524年，佩德罗·德阿尔瓦拉多率西班牙人和数千名纳瓦盟军从墨西哥南下，在克萨尔特南戈附近击败基切玛雅人，焚毁其都城库马尔卡赫并烧死其国王，在喀克其奎人的都城伊希姆切建立圣地亚哥城；喀克其奎人不久便起而反抗。

sources.title: Pedro de Alvarado, letters to Cortés (1524)
W. George Lovell, Christopher H. Lutz & Wendy Kramer, Strike Fear in the Land: Pedro de Alvarado and the Conquest of Guatemala, 1520–1541 (2020)
Wikipedia: Spanish conquest of Guatemala

note: Wikidata starts the conquest in 1521 (first contacts) and ends it in 1697 (fall of the Itza kingdom of Nojpetén); this record covers Alvarado's main campaign.

story.en:
Alvarado had been the most ruthless of Cortés's captains, and Guatemala experienced it. In February 1524 his army met the K'iche' on the plain below Xelajú (Quetzaltenango). K'iche' tradition remembers that the war leader Tecún Umán, adorned with quetzal feathers, fought Alvarado in single combat and was killed; a quetzal is said to have landed on his body, its breast stained red ever after. The story is legend, but Tecún Umán is Guatemala's national hero.

The K'iche' kings Oxib Keh and Beleheb Tz'i then invited Alvarado into their capital, Q'umarkaj. Suspecting a trap, he seized and burned them alive and set fire to the city. The rival Kaqchikel Maya had allied with him and hosted the founding of the Spanish town of Santiago at their capital, Iximché, on 25 July 1524. Alvarado's demands for gold drove them to revolt within months, and the war against them lasted until 1530. The capital of the new colony moved twice, to Almolonga and then to the valley of Panchoy, the future Antigua.
story.zh:
阿尔瓦拉多是科尔特斯麾下最冷酷无情的将领，危地马拉对此深有体会。1524年2月，他的军队在谢拉胡（克萨尔特南戈）下方的平原与基切人交战。基切人的传统记得，身饰格查尔鸟羽毛的军事首领特昆·乌曼与阿尔瓦拉多单打独斗而阵亡；据说一只格查尔鸟落在他身上，从此胸羽染成了红色。这是传说，但特昆·乌曼是危地马拉的民族英雄。

随后，基切国王奥希布·克和贝莱赫布·茨伊邀请阿尔瓦拉多进入都城库马尔卡赫。他怀疑是圈套，便抓住两位国王将其活活烧死，并放火焚城。与基切人敌对的喀克其奎玛雅人曾与他结盟，1524年7月25日在其都城伊希姆切见证了西班牙城镇圣地亚哥的建立。阿尔瓦拉多索要黄金，几个月内便逼得他们起兵反抗，这场战争一直持续到1530年。新殖民地的首府两度迁移，先到阿尔莫隆加，后到潘乔伊谷，即日后的安提瓜。

name.en: Apparitions of the Virgin of Guadalupe at Tepeyac
name.zh: 瓜达卢佩圣母在特佩亚克显现

summary.en: According to tradition, in December 1531 the Virgin Mary appeared four times to a Nahua convert, Juan Diego, on the hill of Tepeyac north of Mexico City, leaving her image on his cloak. The image, enshrined at Tepeyac, became the focus of Mexico's greatest devotion and a national symbol.
summary.zh: 据传统说法，1531年12月，圣母马利亚在墨西哥城北的特佩亚克山上四次向纳瓦族皈依者胡安·迭戈显现，并在他的斗篷上留下自己的圣像。供奉于特佩亚克的这幅圣像成为墨西哥最重要的信仰中心和民族象征。

sources.title: Stafford Poole, Our Lady of Guadalupe: The Origins and Sources of a Mexican National Symbol, 1531–1797 (1995)
David A. Brading, Mexican Phoenix: Our Lady of Guadalupe: Image and Tradition across Five Centuries (2001)
Wikipedia: Our Lady of Guadalupe

note: The apparition narrative is first recorded in print in 1648 (Miguel Sánchez) and 1649 (the Nahuatl Nican Mopohua). A chapel at Tepeyac with a venerated image is documented from the 1550s.

story.en:
The story, as told in the Nahuatl text Nican Mopohua published in 1649, is simple. At dawn on 9 December 1531, Juan Diego, a humble convert walking to Mass, heard birdsong on the hill of Tepeyac and saw a young woman who spoke to him in Nahuatl and asked for a church to be built there. Bishop Juan de Zumárraga asked for a sign. On 12 December she told Juan Diego to gather roses, out of season, on the barren hilltop; when he opened his cloak (tilma) before the bishop, the roses fell out and her image was revealed painted on the cloth.

Historians debate how much of this is early tradition. No document from Zumárraga mentions it, and the first written versions come more than a century later. But a shrine at Tepeyac, a hill once associated with the mother goddess Tonantzin, drew Indigenous and Spanish pilgrims by the 1550s. In 1810 Miguel Hidalgo raised a banner of Guadalupe at Dolores, and in 2002 John Paul II canonised Juan Diego. The basilica at Tepeyac receives millions of pilgrims each December.
story.zh:
据1649年出版的纳瓦特尔语文献《尼坎·莫波瓦》记载，故事很简单。1531年12月9日黎明，谦卑的皈依者胡安·迭戈在去望弥撒的路上，于特佩亚克山听到鸟鸣，看见一位少女用纳瓦特尔语对他说话，要求在此地建一座教堂。主教胡安·德苏马拉加要求一个征兆。12月12日，她让胡安·迭戈去荒芜的山顶采摘反季节盛开的玫瑰；当他在主教面前打开斗篷时，玫瑰纷纷落下，布上显出了她的圣像。

史学家对其中多少属于早期传统存有争议。苏马拉加的文献中从未提及此事，最早的书面版本出现在一个多世纪之后。但特佩亚克山曾与母神托南钦相联系，到16世纪50年代，那里的圣所已吸引原住民和西班牙朝圣者。1810年，米格尔·伊达尔戈在多洛雷斯举起瓜达卢佩圣母旗；2002年，教宗若望·保禄二世册封胡安·迭戈为圣人。每年12月，特佩亚克的圣母大殿都会迎来数以百万计的朝圣者。

name.zh: 新西班牙总督辖区建立

summary.en: In 1535 Charles V created the Viceroyalty of New Spain and sent Antonio de Mendoza as its first viceroy, curbing the power of the conquistadors. Governed from Mexico City, it came to stretch from Central America to the present-day US Southwest, the Caribbean and the Philippines.
summary.zh: 1535年，查理五世设立新西班牙总督辖区，派安东尼奥·德门多萨担任首任总督，以削弱征服者的权力。总督辖区以墨西哥城为治所，辖境后来从中美洲延伸到今美国西南部、加勒比地区和菲律宾。

sources.title: Britannica: New Spain
Charles Gibson, Spain in America (1966)
Wikipedia: New Spain

note: Mendoza was appointed on 17 April 1535 and arrived in Mexico City in November.

name.en: First printing press in the Americas

summary.en: In 1539 the Italian printer Juan Pablos, working for the Seville firm of Juan Cromberger at the request of Bishop Zumárraga and Viceroy Mendoza, set up a press in Mexico City. Its first known book was a Christian doctrine in Nahuatl and Spanish; dozens of works in Indigenous languages followed.
summary.zh: 1539年，意大利印刷工胡安·巴勃罗斯受塞维利亚胡安·克罗姆贝格尔印刷坊派遣，应苏马拉加主教和门多萨总督之请，在墨西哥城设立印刷所。已知其印行的第一本书是纳瓦特尔语和西班牙语对照的基督教教义，此后又出版了数十种原住民语言著作。

sources.title: Library of Congress: "Printing in Mexico, 1539–1600"
Hensley C. Woodbridge & Lawrence S. Thompson, Printing in Colonial Spanish America (1976)
Wikipedia: Juan Pablos

note: No copy of the 1539 Breve y más compendiosa doctrina christiana survives; it is known from later references.

summary.en: Caxcan and other peoples of Nueva Galicia, led by Tenamaxtli, rose against Spanish rule and the encomienda, retreating to fortified peaks such as Mixtón. Pedro de Alvarado was killed in the fighting; Viceroy Mendoza crushed the revolt with a large army of Nahua allies.
summary.zh: 新加利西亚的卡斯坎人等民族在特纳马斯特利领导下起来反抗西班牙统治和委托监护制，退守米斯顿等设防山峰。佩德罗·德阿尔瓦拉多在战斗中丧生；门多萨总督率领大批纳瓦盟军镇压了起义。

sources.title: Ida Altman, The War for Mexico's West: Indians and Spaniards in New Galicia, 1524–1550 (2010)
Wikipedia: Mixtón War

note: Marker at Nochistlán, where Alvarado was mortally injured in June 1541.

summary.en: Signed by Charles V at Barcelona in November 1542 after lobbying by Bartolomé de las Casas, the New Laws banned the enslavement of Indigenous people and ordered that encomiendas should lapse on their holders' deaths. Settler revolts forced the crown to revoke the inheritance clause in 1545.
summary.zh: 经巴托洛梅·德拉斯·卡萨斯游说，查理五世于1542年11月在巴塞罗那签署《新法》，禁止奴役原住民，并规定委托监护权在持有人死后收回。殖民者的反抗迫使王室于1545年撤销了关于继承的条款。

sources.title: Lewis Hanke, The Spanish Struggle for Justice in the Conquest of America (1949)
Britannica: Bartolomé de Las Casas
Wikipedia: New Laws

note: Marker at Mexico City, where the visitor Francisco Tello de Sandoval suspended the most contested articles in 1544.

summary.en: A hemorrhagic fever called cocoliztli ("pestilence") swept New Spain from 1545 to 1548, killing perhaps 5 to 15 million people, the majority of the surviving Indigenous population. A 2018 DNA study of victims at Teposcolula-Yucundaa, Oaxaca, identified Salmonella enterica Paratyphi C as a likely cause.
summary.zh: 1545至1548年，一种被称为“科科利兹特利”（意为瘟疫）的出血热席卷新西班牙，或致500万至1500万人死亡，占幸存原住民人口的大多数。2018年对瓦哈卡特波斯科卢拉-尤昆达遇难者的DNA研究认定，C型副伤寒沙门氏菌可能是病原。

sources.title: Åshild J. Vågene et al., "Salmonella enterica genomes from victims of a major sixteenth-century epidemic in Mexico", Nature Ecology & Evolution 2 (2018)
Rodolfo Acuna-Soto et al., "Megadrought and Megadeath in 16th Century Mexico", Emerging Infectious Diseases 8 (2002)
Wikipedia: Cocoliztli epidemics

note: Mortality figures are estimates; the cause is still debated. Marker at Teposcolula-Yucundaa, the excavated epidemic cemetery.

story.en:
The friars who watched it called it something new. Victims burned with fever, bled from the nose, ears and eyes, turned yellow, and died within days. The Franciscan Juan de Torquemada later wrote that in 1545 some 800,000 people died in the Valley of Mexico alone, and that there were not enough living to bury the dead. Spaniards were rarely affected.

Rodolfo Acuña-Soto and colleagues linked the outbreaks of 1545 and 1576 to megadroughts recorded in tree rings, and suggested a native haemorrhagic fever carried by rodents. In 2018 a team from the Max Planck Institute recovered ancient DNA from the teeth of people buried in an epidemic cemetery at Teposcolula-Yucundaa in the Mixteca Alta and found Salmonella enterica Paratyphi C, an enteric fever possibly introduced from Europe.

Combined with the smallpox of 1520 and later outbreaks, cocoliztli helped reduce the Indigenous population of central Mexico from perhaps 15–25 million in 1519 to little more than one million by 1600, one of the worst demographic catastrophes in history.
story.zh:
目睹疫情的修士们称它为一种新病。患者高烧，鼻、耳、眼出血，皮肤发黄，几天内便死去。方济各会修士胡安·德托克马达后来写道，1545年仅墨西哥谷地就死了约80万人，活着的人不够掩埋死者。西班牙人则很少染病。

罗道尔夫·阿库尼亚-索托等学者把1545年和1576年的疫情与树轮记录的特大干旱联系起来，认为病原是由啮齿动物传播的本土出血热。2018年，马克斯·普朗克研究所的团队从米斯特克高地特波斯科卢拉-尤昆达一处疫病墓地中死者的牙齿里提取古DNA，发现了C型副伤寒沙门氏菌，这是一种可能从欧洲传入的肠热病病原。

与1520年的天花和后来的多次疫情一起，科科利兹特利使墨西哥中部的原住民人口从1519年的约1500万至2500万降至1600年的仅一百余万，这是历史上最惨重的人口灾难之一。

summary.en: In September 1546 a party led by Juan de Tolosa found rich silver ores at La Bufa hill in Zacatecas, 600 km north of Mexico City. The mining boom that followed, along with Guanajuato and later mines, made New Spain the world's greatest silver producer and pushed Spanish settlement north along the Camino Real.
summary.zh: 1546年9月，胡安·德托洛萨率领的一行人在墨西哥城以北600公里的萨卡特卡斯拉布法山发现富银矿。随之而来的采矿热潮，连同瓜纳华托及后来的矿山，使新西班牙成为世界最大的白银产地，并推动西班牙人沿皇家大道向北拓殖。

sources.title: P. J. Bakewell, Silver Mining and Society in Colonial Mexico: Zacatecas 1546–1700 (1971)
UNESCO World Heritage: Historic Centre of Zacatecas
Wikipedia: Zacatecas City

story.en:
Juan de Tolosa, a Basque captain, had been sent north into the dry plateau of the Chichimeca peoples. On 8 September 1546, according to the traditional account, local Zacateco people showed him stones from the hill of La Bufa that turned out to be rich in silver. Within two years a mining camp had sprung up, and its four founders (Tolosa, Cristóbal de Oñate, Diego de Ibarra and Baltasar Temiño de Bañuelos) became some of the richest men in the Spanish empire.

The silver had to be refined, and from the 1550s miners used the patio process, mixing crushed ore with mercury, salt and copper sulphate on stone floors, a technique developed by Bartolomé de Medina at Pachuca. Mercury came from Almadén in Spain, silver went back by mule train to Mexico City and Veracruz. The road provoked the long Chichimeca War (1550–1590) with nomadic peoples who raided the caravans. Mexican silver, together with Potosí's, flowed to Seville and across the Pacific on the Manila galleons, becoming the money of global trade.
story.zh:
巴斯克人队长胡安·德托洛萨奉命北上，进入奇奇梅卡诸民族所居的干旱高原。按照传统说法，1546年9月8日，当地的萨卡特科人向他展示了拉布法山的石头，结果发现其中富含白银。不到两年，这里便形成了矿营，四位创建者（托洛萨、克里斯托瓦尔·德奥尼亚特、迭戈·德伊瓦拉和巴尔塔萨尔·特米尼奥·德巴尼乌埃洛斯）跻身西班牙帝国最富有者之列。

白银需要提炼。从16世纪50年代起，矿工采用由巴托洛梅·德梅迪纳在帕丘卡发明的“庭院法”，在石板地上将碎矿石与汞、盐和硫酸铜混合。汞来自西班牙的阿尔马登，白银则由骡队运回墨西哥城和韦拉克鲁斯。这条运银之路引发了与袭击商队的游牧民族之间旷日持久的奇奇梅卡战争（1550—1590年）。墨西哥白银与波托西白银一起流向塞维利亚，又随马尼拉大帆船横渡太平洋，成为全球贸易的通货。

name.en: Royal and Pontifical University of Mexico founded
name.zh: 墨西哥皇家和教宗大学创立

summary.en: A royal decree of September 1551 founded the University of Mexico, modelled on Salamanca; classes began in January 1553. One of the first universities in the Americas, it taught theology, law, medicine and Nahuatl and Otomí, and is the ancestor of today's UNAM.
summary.zh: 1551年9月的一道王室敕令以萨拉曼卡大学为蓝本创立墨西哥大学，1553年1月开课。它是美洲最早的大学之一，讲授神学、法学、医学以及纳瓦特尔语和奥托米语，是今天墨西哥国立自治大学的前身。

sources.title: John Tate Lanning, Academic Culture in the Spanish Colonies (1940)
UNAM: Historia de la Universidad
Wikipedia: Royal and Pontifical University of Mexico

name.en: Popol Vuh written down in K'iche'

summary.en: Between about 1554 and 1558 anonymous K'iche' Maya nobles of Santa Cruz del Quiché wrote down their sacred book, the Popol Vuh, in the Latin alphabet. It tells of the creation of humans from maize and the Hero Twins Hunahpu and Xbalanque, and survives through a copy made by the friar Francisco Ximénez around 1701.
summary.zh: 约1554至1558年间，圣克鲁斯-德尔基切的几位匿名基切玛雅贵族用拉丁字母写下了他们的圣书《波波尔·乌》。书中讲述用玉米造人的创世神话和英雄双子乌纳普与斯巴兰克的故事，现借修士弗朗西斯科·希门尼斯约1701年的抄本流传于世。

sources.title: Dennis Tedlock (trans.), Popol Vuh: The Mayan Book of the Dawn of Life (rev. ed., 1996)
Newberry Library: Popol Vuh manuscript (Ayer MS 1515)
Wikipedia: Popol Vuh

note: Dating is inferred from the text's list of rulers; the original manuscript is lost.

story.en:
The Popol Vuh, the "Book of the Mat" or Council Book, opens by announcing the beginning of the ancient word of the K'iche'. Its authors, writing after the Spanish had burned their capital Q'umarkaj, explained that they were setting down the old book "now that God's word has come", because the original could no longer be seen.

The first part tells of the gods' failed attempts to make people from mud and wood, before they succeed with maize dough. The heart of the book follows the twins Hunahpu and Xbalanque, who descend to Xibalba, the underworld, defeat its lords at the ballgame and through tricks, and rise as the sun and moon. The last part traces K'iche' lineages down to the Spanish conquest.

Around 1701 Francisco Ximénez, a Dominican priest at Chichicastenango, copied the text in two columns, K'iche' and Spanish. His manuscript, now in the Newberry Library in Chicago, is our only source. Scenes on Classic Maya painted vases show the twins and Xibalba's lords, proving that the stories are far older than the colonial text.
story.zh:
《波波尔·乌》（意为“席子之书”或“议事之书”）开篇即宣告基切人古老言辞的开端。作者们是在西班牙人焚毁其都城库马尔卡赫之后写作的，他们解释说，“既然上帝的话语已经到来”，原书已无从得见，所以要把旧书写下来。

第一部分讲述众神先用泥土和木头造人都失败了，最后用玉米面团造人才获成功。全书的核心是双子乌纳普和斯巴兰克的故事：他们下到冥界希巴尔巴，在球赛中并凭借计谋击败冥界诸王，最终升天化为太阳和月亮。最后一部分追溯基切各宗族直到西班牙征服的世系。

约1701年，奇奇卡斯特南戈的多明我会神父弗朗西斯科·希门尼斯以基切语和西班牙语双栏抄录了这部文本。他的手稿现藏芝加哥纽伯里图书馆，是我们唯一的来源。古典期玛雅彩绘陶瓶上描绘着双子和希巴尔巴诸王，证明这些故事远比殖民时期的文本古老。

name.en: Diego de Landa's auto-da-fé at Maní
name.zh: 迭戈·德兰达在马尼的异端审判

summary.en: After discovering that converted Maya in Yucatán still worshipped their old gods, the Franciscan Diego de Landa led an inquisition in which thousands were tortured. At Maní on 12 July 1562 he burned Maya codices and some 5,000 images. His later account of Yucatán nevertheless preserved a key to the Maya script.
summary.zh: 方济各会修士迭戈·德兰达发现尤卡坦已皈依的玛雅人仍在崇拜旧神，遂主持宗教审讯，数千人遭受酷刑。1562年7月12日，他在马尼焚毁玛雅手抄本和约5000尊神像。然而，他后来撰写的尤卡坦记述却保存了破译玛雅文字的一把钥匙。

sources.title: Diego de Landa, Relación de las cosas de Yucatán (c. 1566)
Inga Clendinnen, Ambivalent Conquests: Maya and Spaniard in Yucatan, 1517–1570 (1987)
Michael D. Coe, Breaking the Maya Code (rev. ed., 1999)

story.en:
In May 1562 two Maya boys found idols and human skulls in a cave near Maní. Diego de Landa, the head of the Franciscans in Yucatán, concluded that his converts had been secretly practising the old religion, even, he believed, human sacrifice. Without waiting for the bishop, he began an inquisition: over three months some 4,500 people were questioned under torture, hoisted by the wrists with stones tied to their feet; about 158 died and others killed themselves.

On 12 July, in the square of Maní, Landa held an auto-da-fé. The penitents were paraded and punished, and a great pile of images and books was burned. Landa later wrote that the books contained nothing but superstition and the lies of the devil, so he burned them all, and that the Maya grieved over their loss more than he could have imagined.

Recalled to Spain to answer for his actions, Landa wrote the Relación de las cosas de Yucatán. In it he recorded what he thought was a Maya "alphabet". Four centuries later Yuri Knorozov showed that it was really a list of syllables, and used it to crack the script that Landa had tried to destroy.
story.zh:
1562年5月，两个玛雅男孩在马尼附近的山洞里发现了神像和人的头骨。尤卡坦方济各会首领迭戈·德兰达断定，他的皈依者们一直在暗中信奉旧宗教，他甚至相信还有人祭。他未等主教到来便开始审讯：三个月间约4500人在酷刑下受审，他们被吊起手腕、脚上绑着石头；约158人死亡，还有人自杀。

7月12日，兰达在马尼广场举行异端判决仪式。悔罪者被游街示众并受罚，一大堆神像和书籍被付之一炬。兰达后来写道，这些书里尽是迷信和魔鬼的谎言，所以他把它们全都烧了，而玛雅人为此痛惜之深超出了他的想象。

兰达被召回西班牙为自己的行为辩护，其间写成《尤卡坦风物志》。书中记下了他以为是玛雅“字母表”的东西。四个世纪后，尤里·克诺罗佐夫证明那其实是一份音节表，并借助它破译了兰达曾试图毁灭的文字。

name.zh: 乌达内塔的“回程航线”抵达阿卡普尔科

summary.en: The galleon San Pedro, piloted by the Augustinian friar-navigator Andrés de Urdaneta, left Cebu in June 1565, sailed north to about 38°N to catch westerly winds and the Kuroshio current, and reached Acapulco in October after some 130 days. The route made Acapulco the American terminus of the Manila galleons.
summary.zh: 由奥斯定会修士兼航海家安德烈斯·德乌达内塔领航的“圣佩德罗”号大帆船于1565年6月离开宿务，北上至约北纬38度借助西风和黑潮，历时约130天于10月抵达阿卡普尔科。这条航线使阿卡普尔科成为马尼拉大帆船的美洲终点港。

sources.title: William Lytle Schurz, The Manila Galleon (1939)
Britannica: Manila galleon
Wikipedia: Andrés de Urdaneta

note: The 250-year galleon trade itself is recorded in the southeast-asia dataset as ev-manila-galleon.

story.en:
Spaniards had reached the Philippines from Mexico several times since Magellan, but no ship had ever sailed back: the trade winds that carried them west blew straight against a return. Andrés de Urdaneta, a Basque veteran of the Pacific who had become an Augustinian friar in Mexico, was persuaded by King Philip II to join Miguel López de Legazpi's expedition of 1564 for one purpose: to find the way home.

His idea was to sail far north, as Portuguese experience with the westerlies of the North Atlantic suggested. The San Pedro left Cebu on 1 June 1565, worked up past Japan to around 38 degrees north, and then ran east across the empty North Pacific. Scurvy killed 16 of the crew. In September they sighted the coast of California and turned south, entering Acapulco on 8 October.

From 1571 to 1815 one or two galleons a year made the round trip between Manila and Acapulco. The Acapulco fair, held when the "Nao de China" arrived, brought silks, porcelain and spices to New Spain, carried overland to Mexico City and Veracruz, while Mexican silver went west to China.
story.zh:
自麦哲伦以来，西班牙人曾多次从墨西哥抵达菲律宾，但从未有船只成功返航：把他们送往西方的信风，恰恰挡住了回程。巴斯克人安德烈斯·德乌达内塔是太平洋航海老手，后来在墨西哥成为奥斯定会修士。国王腓力二世说服他加入米格尔·洛佩斯·德黎牙实比1564年的远征，目的只有一个：找到回家的路。

他的设想是远向北航，正如葡萄牙人在北大西洋西风带的经验所示。1565年6月1日，“圣佩德罗”号离开宿务，经日本附近北上至约北纬38度，然后横越空旷的北太平洋向东航行。坏血病夺去了16名船员的生命。9月，他们望见加利福尼亚海岸，转而南下，于10月8日驶入阿卡普尔科。

从1571年到1815年，每年有一两艘大帆船往返于马尼拉和阿卡普尔科之间。“中国船”到港时举办的阿卡普尔科集市，把丝绸、瓷器和香料带到新西班牙，再经陆路运往墨西哥城和韦拉克鲁斯，墨西哥白银则向西流往中国。

name.zh: 萨阿贡完成《佛罗伦萨手抄本》

summary.en: Working for decades with Nahua elders and trilingual students of the Colegio de Santa Cruz de Tlatelolco, the Franciscan Bernardino de Sahagún produced the General History of the Things of New Spain, in Nahuatl and Spanish with some 2,400 illustrations. The 12-book encyclopedia of Aztec religion, society, nature and the conquest is now in Florence.
summary.zh: 方济各会修士贝尔纳迪诺·德萨阿贡与纳瓦长老和特拉特洛尔科圣十字学院精通三种语言的学生合作数十年，以纳瓦特尔语和西班牙语写成《新西班牙诸物通史》，配有约2400幅插图。这部记述阿兹特克宗教、社会、自然和征服史的12卷百科全书现藏佛罗伦萨。

sources.title: World Digital Library / Library of Congress: General History of the Things of New Spain by Fray Bernardino de Sahagún: The Florentine Codex
Kevin Terraciano & Jeanette Favrot Peterson (eds.), The Florentine Codex: An Encyclopedia of the Nahua World in Sixteenth-Century Mexico (2019)
Wikipedia: Florentine Codex

note: Marker at Tlatelolco, where the work was compiled.

name.en: Kalinago genocide at Bloody Point, St Kitts
name.zh: 圣基茨岛血腥角的卡利纳戈人大屠杀

summary.en: English settlers under Thomas Warner and French under Pierre Belain d'Esnambuc, who shared St Kitts, attacked the island's Kalinago (Island Carib) people after a warning of a planned uprising, killing perhaps 2,000 at the place now called Bloody Point. The survivors were driven from the island.
summary.zh: 共同占据圣基茨岛的托马斯·沃纳率领的英国移民与皮埃尔·贝兰·德斯南布克率领的法国移民，在得到卡利纳戈人（岛加勒比人）将要起事的警告后，对岛上的卡利纳戈人发动袭击，在今称血腥角的地方杀死约2000人，幸存者被逐出该岛。

sources.title: Philip P. Boucher, Cannibal Encounters: Europeans and Island Caribs, 1492–1763 (1992)
Jean-Baptiste du Tertre, Histoire générale des Antilles habitées par les François (1667)
Wikipedia: Kalinago genocide of 1626

note: Death tolls in the sources vary widely (from about 100 to 4,000); the date is given as 1626 or 1625.

story.en:
St Kitts, which the Kalinago called Liamuiga, was the first Caribbean island colonised by both England and France. Thomas Warner landed in 1624 and was joined the next year by Pierre Belain d'Esnambuc. The Kalinago chief Tegremond (Ouboutou Tegremante) at first tolerated them. According to the French chronicler du Tertre, a Kalinago woman named Barbe, the companion of one of the settlers, warned that the Kalinago planned to attack with allies from other islands.

The English and French struck first, killing men in their sleep, and then met a war party at a ravine near the island's west coast. Accounts claim that 2,000 or more Kalinago died, and that the stream ran red for days; the place is still called Bloody Point. The survivors fled to Dominica and St Vincent, which remained Kalinago strongholds for over a century. The Europeans divided St Kitts between them and planted tobacco and then sugar. Today about 3,000 Kalinago live in a territory on Dominica, the last Indigenous community of the eastern Caribbean.
story.zh:
圣基茨岛，卡利纳戈人称之为“利亚穆伊加”，是英国和法国共同殖民的第一个加勒比岛屿。托马斯·沃纳于1624年登陆，次年皮埃尔·贝兰·德斯南布克也来到这里。卡利纳戈酋长特格雷蒙起初容忍了他们。据法国编年史家迪特尔特记载，一位名叫巴贝的卡利纳戈女子（某位移民的伴侣）警告说，卡利纳戈人正计划联合其他岛屿的盟友发动袭击。

英法两方先下手为强，在睡梦中杀死男子，随后在岛西岸附近的一条峡谷与一支战队遭遇。记载称有2000名以上的卡利纳戈人死亡，溪水连日殷红；此地至今仍名为“血腥角”。幸存者逃往多米尼克和圣文森特，这两个岛在此后一个多世纪里仍是卡利纳戈人的据点。欧洲人瓜分了圣基茨岛，先种烟草，后种甘蔗。如今约有3000名卡利纳戈人生活在多米尼克的一块领地上，他们是东加勒比地区最后的原住民社群。

summary.en: From the 1640s English planters in Barbados, learning techniques from Dutch traders who had worked in Brazil, switched from tobacco and cotton to sugar. Large plantations worked by enslaved Africans replaced small farms, making Barbados England's richest colony and the model for slave societies across the Caribbean.
summary.zh: 从17世纪40年代起，巴巴多斯的英国种植园主向曾在巴西经营的荷兰商人学习技术，由种植烟草和棉花转向种植甘蔗。由被奴役的非洲人劳作的大种植园取代了小农场，使巴巴多斯成为英国最富有的殖民地，也成为整个加勒比奴隶社会的样板。

sources.title: Richard S. Dunn, Sugar and Slaves: The Rise of the Planter Class in the English West Indies, 1624–1713 (1972)
Richard Ligon, A True and Exact History of the Island of Barbados (1657)
Britannica: Barbados

note: "Sugar revolution" is a historians' term; the transformation was largely complete by about 1680.

story.en:
When Richard Ligon arrived in Barbados in 1647 he found an island in the middle of a gold rush, except that the gold was sugar. Planters such as James Drax had learned from Dutch merchants how to build the mills, boiling houses and curing sheds that turned cane juice into crystals, and the Dutch supplied credit and enslaved Africans. Land prices soared; small farmers and indentured servants from Britain were squeezed out.

By 1680 Barbados had some 38,000 enslaved Africans and 20,000 whites, and a handful of great planters controlled most of the land. Work in the cane fields and boiling houses was brutal and the death rate so high that the population could only be sustained by constant imports from Africa. The Barbados Slave Code of 1661 defined enslaved people as chattel property and was copied in Jamaica, South Carolina and Antigua. The plantation complex pioneered here, sugar, slavery and absentee wealth, spread to Jamaica, Saint-Domingue and Cuba, and shaped the Caribbean for two centuries.
story.zh:
1647年理查德·利贡来到巴巴多斯时，发现这座岛正处在一场淘金热中，只不过这里的“金子”是蔗糖。詹姆斯·德拉克斯等种植园主从荷兰商人那里学会了建造磨坊、熬糖房和晾糖棚，把蔗汁变成结晶；荷兰人还提供贷款和被奴役的非洲人。地价飞涨，来自不列颠的小农和契约仆役被挤了出去。

到1680年，巴巴多斯约有3.8万名被奴役的非洲人和2万名白人，少数大种植园主控制了大部分土地。甘蔗田和熬糖房里的劳作极其残酷，死亡率之高，只能靠不断从非洲输入人口来维持。1661年的《巴巴多斯奴隶法典》把被奴役者界定为动产，后来被牙买加、南卡罗来纳和安提瓜照搬。这里首创的种植园体系——蔗糖、奴隶制和不在地主的财富——扩散到牙买加、圣多明各和古巴，塑造了此后两个世纪的加勒比。

name.en: English conquest of Jamaica (the Western Design)
name.zh: 英国征服牙买加（“西方计划”）

summary.en: Oliver Cromwell's "Western Design" sent a fleet under William Penn and an army under Robert Venables to seize Spanish territory in the Caribbean. Repulsed at Santo Domingo in April 1655, they took lightly defended Jamaica in May. Enslaved Africans freed by the Spanish fled to the mountains, forming the first Maroon communities.
summary.zh: 奥利弗·克伦威尔的“西方计划”派遣威廉·佩恩率领的舰队和罗伯特·维纳布尔斯统率的陆军夺取西班牙在加勒比的领土。1655年4月他们在圣多明各被击退，5月转而攻占防守薄弱的牙买加。被西班牙人释放的非洲奴隶逃入山区，形成了最早的马龙人社群。

sources.title: Carla Gardina Pestana, The English Conquest of Jamaica: Oliver Cromwell's Bid for Empire (2017)
Britannica: Jamaica: History
Wikipedia: Invasion of Jamaica

note: Spain recognised English possession in the Treaty of Madrid (1670). Marker at Spanish Town (Santiago de la Vega), the Spanish capital.

name.zh: 亨利·摩根洗劫巴拿马城

summary.en: In January 1671 the Welsh privateer Henry Morgan led about 1,400 buccaneers up the Chagres River and across the isthmus, routed the Spanish defenders outside Panama City and occupied it for a month. The city burned; the Spanish rebuilt it on a new, more defensible site in 1673.
summary.zh: 1671年1月，威尔士私掠船长亨利·摩根率约1400名海盗溯查格雷斯河而上，横穿地峡，在巴拿马城外击溃西班牙守军，占领该城一个月。城市被焚毁；1673年西班牙人在一处更易防守的新址重建了它。

sources.title: Alexandre Exquemelin, De Americaensche Zee-Roovers (The Buccaneers of America) (1678)
Peter Earle, The Sack of Panamá: Sir Henry Morgan's Adventures on the Spanish Main (1981)
UNESCO World Heritage: Archaeological Site of Panamá Viejo and Historic District of Panamá

note: Marker at Panamá Viejo, the ruins of the old city.

story.en:
Panama was the hinge of Spain's silver empire: Peruvian silver came up the Pacific to the city, then crossed the isthmus by mule to Portobelo for the treasure fleets. Henry Morgan had already sacked Portobelo in 1668. In December 1670, with a commission from the governor of Jamaica and the largest buccaneer force ever assembled in the Caribbean, he took the fort of San Lorenzo at the mouth of the Chagres and started inland by canoe and on foot.

The nine-day march through the jungle nearly broke the army; Exquemelin, a surgeon who was there, says men ate their leather satchels. On 28 January 1671 they met the Spanish militia on the plain outside the city. The Spanish governor tried to stampede herds of cattle into the buccaneers' ranks, but the animals turned back on his own men. Panama fell, and fire, set by the Spanish or the raiders, destroyed most of it.

Much of the treasure had been shipped away in time, and Morgan's men grumbled at their small shares. Worse, England and Spain had just signed a peace treaty. Morgan was arrested and sent to London, only to be knighted and returned to Jamaica as lieutenant governor.
story.zh:
巴拿马是西班牙白银帝国的枢纽：秘鲁白银经太平洋运到该城，再由骡队穿过地峡运往波托韦洛装上运宝船队。亨利·摩根已于1668年洗劫过波托韦洛。1670年12月，他持牙买加总督颁发的委任状，率领加勒比史上规模最大的海盗队伍，攻取查格雷斯河口的圣洛伦索要塞，随后乘独木舟和步行深入内陆。

穿越丛林的九天行军几乎拖垮了这支队伍；亲历其事的外科医生埃克斯奎梅林说，人们饿得啃食皮革背包。1671年1月28日，他们在城外平原与西班牙民兵遭遇。西班牙总督想驱赶牛群冲散海盗的阵列，牛群却掉头冲向了他自己的部下。巴拿马陷落，一场大火（不知是西班牙人还是袭击者所放）烧毁了城市的大部分。

大量财宝早已及时运走，摩根的手下抱怨分得太少。更糟的是，英西两国刚刚签订和约。摩根被捕并押往伦敦，结果却被封为爵士，以副总督身份回到牙买加。

summary.en: On 7 June 1692 an earthquake and the liquefaction of the sand spit on which it stood sank about two-thirds of Port Royal, Jamaica, the booming harbour of buccaneers and merchants. Some 2,000 people died at once and perhaps 3,000 more of injuries and disease; Kingston was founded across the harbour to replace it.
summary.zh: 1692年6月7日，一场地震以及城市所在沙嘴的液化，使牙买加的罗亚尔港约三分之二沉入海中。这座海盗与商人云集的繁华港口当即约有2000人罹难，此后或又有3000人死于伤病；人们在港湾对岸建立金斯敦取而代之。

sources.title: Michael Pawson & David Buisseret, Port Royal, Jamaica (1974)
Texas A&M Nautical Archaeology Program: Port Royal Project
Wikipedia: 1692 Jamaica earthquake

story.en:
Port Royal stood at the tip of the Palisadoes, a long sand spit closing Kingston Harbour. In thirty years it had grown into the largest English town in the Americas after Boston, with perhaps 6,500 people, brick houses up to four storeys high, goldsmiths, taverns and a notorious reputation. Buccaneers spent their plunder there, and merchants traded slaves and Spanish silver.

Just before noon on 7 June 1692 three shocks struck. The waterlogged sand beneath the town liquefied, and whole streets slid into the harbour. Survivors described the ground opening and closing on people, and a wave that carried a ship over the rooftops. The graveyard where Henry Morgan had been buried four years earlier disappeared under the sea. Preachers called it God's judgement on "the wickedest city on earth".

The survivors moved across the harbour to found Kingston. Underwater excavations from the 1960s, and by Texas A&M University in the 1980s, found buildings and their contents almost intact, including a pocket watch whose hands stopped at 11:43.
story.zh:
罗亚尔港坐落在帕利萨多斯沙嘴的末端，这道长长的沙嘴围住了金斯敦港。三十年间，它发展成为美洲仅次于波士顿的第二大英国城镇，人口或达6500，有高达四层的砖房、金匠铺和酒馆，名声狼藉。海盗在这里挥霍掠获，商人在这里买卖奴隶和西班牙白银。

1692年6月7日临近正午，三次震动接连袭来。城下饱含水分的沙土液化，整条街道滑入港中。幸存者描述地面开合吞噬行人，一道巨浪把一艘船冲过屋顶。四年前安葬亨利·摩根的墓地也沉入海底。传教士称这是上帝对“世上最邪恶之城”的审判。

幸存者迁到港湾对岸，建立了金斯敦。从20世纪60年代起，以及80年代得克萨斯农工大学进行的水下发掘，发现建筑及其中的物品几乎完好无损，其中有一块指针停在11点43分的怀表。

name.en: Sor Juana's Reply to Sor Filotea
name.zh: 胡安娜修女《致菲洛特亚修女的答复》

summary.en: Rebuked in print by the Bishop of Puebla, writing as "Sor Filotea", for her theological criticism, the Hieronymite nun Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz wrote a long autobiographical letter defending women's right to study and learn. It is one of the founding texts of feminist thought in the Americas.
summary.zh: 普埃布拉主教化名“菲洛特亚修女”在出版物中责备圣哲罗姆会修女胡安娜·伊内斯·德拉克鲁斯的神学批评，胡安娜随后写下一封长篇自传性书信，捍卫女性求学求知的权利。它是美洲女性主义思想的奠基文献之一。

sources.title: Octavio Paz, Sor Juana, or, The Traps of Faith (1982; Eng. trans. 1988)
Britannica: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
Wikipedia: Respuesta a Sor Filotea de la Cruz

note: Dated 1 March 1691 at the convent of San Jerónimo, Mexico City; first printed in 1700.

name.zh: 牙买加第一次马龙战争

summary.en: For a decade the Maroons of Jamaica, communities of escaped enslaved Africans in the Cockpit Country and the Blue Mountains, fought British troops to a standstill. Treaties in 1739 with the Leeward leader Cudjoe and the Windward Maroons granted them land and autonomy in return for returning future runaways.
summary.zh: 牙买加的马龙人是聚居在“驾驶舱地区”和蓝山中的逃亡非洲奴隶社群，他们与英军周旋十年，使其无法取胜。1739年，英国与背风区首领库乔和迎风区马龙人订立条约，授予他们土地和自治权，条件是交还日后的逃亡者。

sources.title: Mavis C. Campbell, The Maroons of Jamaica 1655–1796: A History of Resistance, Collaboration and Betrayal (1988)
Britannica: Maroon
Wikipedia: First Maroon War

note: Marker at Accompong, the Leeward Maroon town that survives today.

summary.en: At Easter 1760 enslaved Akan ("Coromantee") men led by Tacky rose on plantations in St Mary Parish, Jamaica; risings followed in Westmoreland and elsewhere. It took British troops and Maroon allies over a year to suppress the largest slave revolt in the 18th-century British Caribbean; about 60 whites and over 500 enslaved people died.
summary.zh: 1760年复活节，以塔基为首的被奴役阿坎人（“科罗曼蒂人”）在牙买加圣玛丽区的种植园起义，西摩兰等地随即响应。英军在马龙人协助下用了一年多才镇压这场18世纪英属加勒比规模最大的奴隶起义，约60名白人和500多名被奴役者丧生。

sources.title: Vincent Brown, Tacky's Revolt: The Story of an Atlantic Slave War (2020)
Edward Long, The History of Jamaica (1774)
Wikipedia: Tacky's Revolt

note: Marker at Port Maria, St Mary Parish, where the revolt began.

story.en:
Tacky was said to have been a chief or war leader in the Gold Coast before he was enslaved. Before dawn on Easter Monday, 7 April 1760, he and his followers broke into the fort at Port Maria, seized muskets and gunpowder, and moved from estate to estate, killing planters and recruiting the enslaved. Obeah practitioners promised the fighters protection from bullets.

British soldiers and Maroons, bound by their 1739 treaty to fight rebels, tracked them through the hills. A Maroon marksman shot Tacky, and his head was displayed on a pole in Spanish Town. But the war was not over: in May a larger rising began in Westmoreland, and fighting dragged on into 1761. Historian Vincent Brown calls it an "Atlantic slave war", part of a chain of conflicts linked to wars in West Africa and the Seven Years' War.

The colonial government responded with savage executions, some rebels burned alive or hung in iron cages until they starved, and a new law banning obeah. Tacky became a hero of Jamaican independence.
story.zh:
据说塔基被奴役前曾是黄金海岸的一位酋长或军事首领。1760年4月7日复活节星期一黎明前，他和追随者闯入玛丽亚港的要塞，夺取火枪和火药，随后一个庄园接一个庄园地推进，杀死种植园主，招募被奴役者。奥比巫师向战士们许诺刀枪不入。

英国士兵和受1739年条约约束、须协助镇压叛乱的马龙人在山中追踪他们。一名马龙神枪手射杀了塔基，他的头颅被插在西班牙镇的木杆上示众。但战争并未结束：5月，西摩兰爆发了规模更大的起义，战斗一直拖到1761年。历史学家文森特·布朗称之为一场“大西洋奴隶战争”，是与西非战争和七年战争相关联的一连串冲突的一部分。

殖民政府以残酷的处决作为回应，一些起义者被活活烧死，或被吊在铁笼里直到饿死，还颁布了禁止奥比巫术的新法。塔基后来成为牙买加独立的英雄。

summary.en: In the Seven Years' War a British expedition under the Earl of Albemarle besieged Havana from June 1762, stormed the Morro Castle on 30 July and took the city on 13 August. During eleven months of occupation Havana opened to British trade; it was returned to Spain in 1763 in exchange for Florida.
summary.zh: 七年战争期间，阿尔伯马尔伯爵统率的英国远征军自1762年6月起围攻哈瓦那，7月30日攻克莫罗城堡，8月13日占领该城。在长达十一个月的占领期间，哈瓦那向英国贸易开放；1763年，英国以哈瓦那交还西班牙，换取佛罗里达。

sources.title: David F. Marley, Wars of the Americas: A Chronology of Armed Conflict in the Western Hemisphere (2nd ed., 2008)
Elena A. Schneider, The Occupation of Havana: War, Trade, and Slavery in the Atlantic World (2018)
Wikipedia: Battle of Havana (1762)

story.en:
Havana was the key of the Spanish Caribbean, the harbour where the treasure fleets gathered, guarded by the Morro Castle on its rocky headland. When Spain entered the Seven Years' War in 1762, Britain sent more than 50 warships and about 12,000 soldiers. They landed east of the city in June, dragged guns up the hill behind the Morro and battered it for weeks under a blazing sun, while yellow fever and dysentery killed far more men than Spanish fire.

Defenders included Black militia and enslaved men promised their freedom; the Morro's commander, Luis Vicente de Velasco, was mortally wounded when British sappers blew a mine under the walls and stormed in on 30 July. The city surrendered on 13 August. In eleven months British merchants brought in goods and, according to Elena Schneider, several thousand enslaved Africans.

The Peace of Paris returned Havana to Spain in exchange for Florida. Shaken, Spain built the vast La Cabaña fortress and opened Cuba to freer trade, laying foundations for the sugar boom that followed.
story.zh:
哈瓦那是西属加勒比的锁钥，是运宝船队集结的港口，由岩岬上的莫罗城堡守护。1762年西班牙加入七年战争后，英国派出50多艘战舰和约1.2万名士兵。他们于6月在城东登陆，把大炮拖上莫罗城堡后方的山坡，在烈日下轰击数周；而黄热病和痢疾夺去的士兵远多于西班牙的炮火。

守军中有黑人民兵和被许诺获得自由的奴隶。7月30日，英国工兵在城墙下引爆地雷后冲入城堡，莫罗守将路易斯·比森特·德贝拉斯科身受致命伤。8月13日全城投降。据伊莱娜·施奈德研究，在十一个月里，英国商人运来了大批货物和数千名被奴役的非洲人。

《巴黎和约》将哈瓦那归还西班牙，换取佛罗里达。受到震动的西班牙修建了庞大的拉卡瓦尼亚要塞，并开放古巴实行较自由的贸易，为随后的蔗糖繁荣奠定了基础。

name.en: Santa Marta earthquakes destroy Santiago de Guatemala
name.zh: 圣玛尔塔地震摧毁危地马拉圣地亚哥城

summary.en: On 29 July 1773, the feast of St Martha, a series of earthquakes wrecked Santiago de los Caballeros de Guatemala, capital of the Kingdom of Guatemala. Against the clergy's resistance the crown moved the capital to a new site, Nueva Guatemala de la Asunción (today's Guatemala City), in 1776; the old city became "La Antigua".
summary.zh: 1773年7月29日圣玛尔塔节，一连串地震摧毁了危地马拉王国首府危地马拉圣地亚哥骑士城。王室不顾教会的反对，于1776年把首府迁到新址“新危地马拉-德拉亚松森”（今危地马拉城）；旧城从此被称为“安提瓜”（意为“旧城”）。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Antigua Guatemala
Christopher H. Lutz, Santiago de Guatemala, 1541–1773: City, Caste, and the Colonial Experience (1994)
Wikipedia: 1773 Guatemala earthquake

summary.en: According to tradition, on the night of 14 August 1791 enslaved leaders from the plantations of northern Saint-Domingue met in a wood called Bois Caïman, where the houngan Dutty Boukman and the priestess Cécile Fatiman led a Vodou ceremony and oath. A week later the great uprising that began the Haitian Revolution broke out.
summary.zh: 据传统说法，1791年8月14日夜，圣多明各北部各种植园被奴役者的首领在一片名为“鳄鱼林”的树林中聚会，由伏都教祭司达蒂·布克曼和女祭司塞西尔·法蒂曼主持仪式并盟誓。一周后，揭开海地革命序幕的大起义爆发。

sources.title: David Patrick Geggus, Haitian Revolutionary Studies (2002)
Laurent Dubois, Avengers of the New World: The Story of the Haitian Revolution (2004)
Wikipedia: Bois Caïman

note: The earliest accounts (Dalmas, 1793) are hostile and second-hand; historians accept that a meeting took place at the Lenormand de Mézy estate around 14 August, but the details of the ceremony are partly legend.

story.en:
The French colonist Antoine Dalmas, writing in 1793, described the scene: a storm-lashed forest clearing, a black pig sacrificed, its blood drunk by the conspirators, who swore to kill the whites. Later Haitian tradition added a prayer attributed to Boukman, calling on the "good god" of the oppressed to help them throw away the image of the whites' god, "who thirsts for our tears".

Historian David Geggus has shown that a political meeting of slave drivers and coachmen from about a hundred plantations really took place at the Lenormand de Mézy estate on 14 August, planning a coordinated rising. Whether the religious ceremony happened that night, or at another meeting, is debated. What is certain is that on the night of 22–23 August the enslaved of the Northern Plain rose, burning cane fields and great houses; within weeks over a thousand plantations were in flames. Boukman was killed in November and his head displayed in Cap-Français. Bois Caïman became Haiti's founding myth, and is still contested by some evangelical churches who read it as a pact with evil spirits.
story.zh:
法国殖民者安托万·达尔马斯在1793年描述了这一场景：暴风雨中的林间空地，一头黑猪被献祭，密谋者喝下猪血，发誓要杀死白人。后来的海地传统又加上了一段据说出自布克曼的祷词，呼求被压迫者的“善神”帮助他们抛弃“渴饮我们泪水”的白人之神的形象。

历史学家戴维·格格斯证明，8月14日确实有来自约一百个种植园的奴隶监工和马车夫在勒诺尔芒·德梅齐庄园举行政治集会，策划一场协同起义。宗教仪式是否就在那天夜里举行，抑或是在另一次集会上，尚有争论。可以确定的是，8月22日至23日夜间，北部平原的被奴役者揭竿而起，焚烧甘蔗田和庄园主宅；几周内，一千多个种植园陷入火海。布克曼于11月被杀，首级被悬挂在法兰西角示众。鳄鱼林成了海地的建国神话，至今仍有一些福音派教会将其视为与邪灵的契约而加以非议。

summary.en: The enslaved people of Saint-Domingue, France's richest colony, rose in 1791, won the abolition of slavery in 1793–94, defeated Spanish, British and finally Napoleonic armies, and declared the independent state of Haiti in 1804. It was the only slave revolt in history to found a state.
summary.zh: 法国最富庶的殖民地圣多明各的被奴役者于1791年起义，1793至1794年间争得废除奴隶制，先后击败西班牙、英国以及拿破仑的军队，于1804年宣告独立的海地国家诞生。这是历史上唯一一次建立了国家的奴隶起义。

sources.title: Laurent Dubois, Avengers of the New World: The Story of the Haitian Revolution (2004)
C. L. R. James, The Black Jacobins: Toussaint L'Ouverture and the San Domingo Revolution (1938)
David Patrick Geggus, Haitian Revolutionary Studies (2002)
Carolyn E. Fick, The Making of Haiti: The Saint Domingue Revolution from Below (1990)
Wikipedia: Haitian Revolution

story.en:
In 1789 Saint-Domingue produced about a third of the world's sugar and much of its coffee, worked by nearly half a million enslaved people, most born in Africa, under some 30,000 whites and a similar number of free people of colour. The French Revolution split the colony's elites, and in August 1791 the enslaved of the north rose.

The war became a contest of empires. Spain, from Santo Domingo, and Britain, which occupied the coast in 1793, armed Black generals against revolutionary France. To win them back the French commissioner Léger-Félicité Sonthonax freed the slaves of the north in August 1793, and the National Convention abolished slavery throughout the empire on 4 February 1794. Toussaint Louverture then changed sides, expelled the British in 1798, defeated the mixed-race general André Rigaud in a civil war and in 1801 issued a constitution making himself governor for life.

Napoleon sent his brother-in-law Leclerc with over 20,000 troops to restore French rule, and, it soon became clear, slavery. Toussaint was tricked, arrested and deported. Yellow fever destroyed the French army, and Dessalines led the final war. After the defeat at Vertières in November 1803 the French evacuated, and on 1 January 1804 Haiti declared independence.
story.zh:
1789年，圣多明各生产了世界约三分之一的蔗糖和大量咖啡，劳作者是近50万被奴役者，其中大多数生于非洲；统治他们的是约3万白人和人数相当的自由有色人。法国大革命使殖民地精英分裂，1791年8月北部的被奴役者揭竿而起。

战争演变为帝国之间的角逐。从圣多明各城出兵的西班牙和1793年占领海岸的英国，都武装黑人将领对抗革命的法国。为了把他们争取回来，法国专员莱热-费利西泰·松托纳克斯于1793年8月宣布解放北部奴隶，国民公会于1794年2月4日在整个帝国废除奴隶制。杜桑·卢维杜尔随即改换阵营，1798年赶走英军，在内战中击败混血将领安德烈·里戈，并于1801年颁布宪法，自任终身总督。

拿破仑派妹夫勒克莱尔率两万多大军前来恢复法国统治，人们很快就明白，还要恢复奴隶制。杜桑中计被捕并被押往法国。黄热病摧毁了法军，德萨林领导了最后的战争。1803年11月法军在韦蒂埃战败撤离，1804年1月1日海地宣告独立。

summary.en: On 18 November 1803 Dessalines's army stormed the French forts at Vertières outside Cap-Français. The bravery of the officer François Capois ("Capois-La-Mort") under fire became legendary. The French commander Rochambeau surrendered the next day and evacuated the colony, the last great battle of the Haitian Revolution.
summary.zh: 1803年11月18日，德萨林的军队猛攻法兰西角城外韦蒂埃的法军堡垒。军官弗朗索瓦·卡波瓦（“不怕死的卡波瓦”）冒着炮火冲锋的英勇事迹成为传奇。次日，法军司令罗尚博投降并撤出殖民地。这是海地革命的最后一场大战。

sources.title: Laurent Dubois, Avengers of the New World: The Story of the Haitian Revolution (2004)
Philippe R. Girard, The Slaves Who Defeated Napoleon: Toussaint Louverture and the Haitian War of Independence, 1801–1804 (2011)
Wikipedia: Battle of Vertières

summary.en: At Gonaïves on 1 January 1804 Jean-Jacques Dessalines proclaimed the independence of Haiti, reviving the Taíno name of the island. The second independent republic in the Americas and the first Black republic, it abolished slavery permanently, though it was shunned diplomatically for decades.
summary.zh: 1804年1月1日，让-雅克·德萨林在戈纳伊夫宣布海地独立，恢复了该岛的泰诺语旧名。这是美洲第二个独立国家、世界上第一个黑人共和国，它永久废除了奴隶制，但此后数十年在外交上备受孤立。

sources.title: Julia Gaffield (ed.), The Haitian Declaration of Independence: Creation, Context, and Legacy (2016)
The National Archives (UK): Haitian Declaration of Independence, CO 137/111
Laurent Dubois, Avengers of the New World: The Story of the Haitian Revolution (2004)
Wikipedia: Haitian Declaration of Independence

story.en:
On the night of 31 December 1803 Dessalines's secretary, Louis Boisrond-Tonnerre, is said to have declared that the act of independence should be written on the skin of a white man, with his blood for ink and a bayonet for a pen. The text he produced the next morning was read to the army and people at Gonaïves. It renounced France forever and swore to die rather than live again under its rule.

The generals chose the name Haïti, from the Taíno word for the mountainous island, as a deliberate rejection of the colonial name and a claim to the Americas' Indigenous past. Dessalines was named governor-general for life, and in September proclaimed himself emperor.

For centuries no original printed copy was known. In 2010 the Canadian graduate student Julia Gaffield found one in the British National Archives at Kew, filed among Jamaica's colonial correspondence, and a second copy surfaced later. No major power recognised Haiti until France did so in 1825, at a price.
story.zh:
据说1803年12月31日夜里，德萨林的秘书路易·布瓦龙-托内尔宣称，独立文告应当写在白人的皮上，以其血为墨、以刺刀为笔。他次日清晨写成的文告在戈纳伊夫向军队和民众宣读。文告宣布永远与法国决裂，誓言宁死也不再受其统治。

将领们选择了“海地”这个名字，它来自泰诺语，意为“多山之岛”，以此有意拒绝殖民地旧名，并宣示与美洲原住民过往的联系。德萨林被推举为终身总督，同年9月自立为皇帝。

数百年间，人们一直没有找到原始印本。2010年，加拿大研究生朱莉娅·加菲尔德在邱园的英国国家档案馆中发现了一份，它被归档在牙买加殖民地往来公文之中；后来又发现了第二份。在1825年法国以索取巨额代价予以承认之前，没有一个大国承认海地。

name.zh: 拉费里埃尔城堡的修建

summary.en: To guard independent Haiti against a French return, Henri Christophe, later King Henry I of northern Haiti, built a huge mountaintop fortress 900 m above Milot, with 365 cannon, alongside his Sans-Souci palace. Tens of thousands of labourers worked on it; it is the largest fortress in the Americas.
summary.zh: 为防范法国卷土重来，亨利·克里斯托夫（后来的北海地国王亨利一世）在米洛上方900米的山顶修建了一座巨型要塞，配置365门大炮，并在山下建造无忧宫。数以万计的劳工参与修建，它是美洲最大的要塞。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: National History Park – Citadel, Sans Souci, Ramiers
Hubert Cole, Christophe: King of Haiti (1967)
Wikipedia: Citadelle Laferrière

note: Begun under Dessalines's orders in 1805 and largely completed by Christophe's death in 1820; Wikidata's 1820 date refers to completion.

summary.en: In the early hours of 16 September 1810 the parish priest Miguel Hidalgo rang the church bell of Dolores and called his parishioners to rise against the colonial government. The "Cry of Dolores" began the Mexican War of Independence and is celebrated as Mexico's Independence Day.
summary.zh: 1810年9月16日凌晨，教区神父米格尔·伊达尔戈敲响多洛雷斯教堂的钟，号召教民起来反抗殖民政府。这声“多洛雷斯呼声”拉开了墨西哥独立战争的序幕，这一天被定为墨西哥独立日。

sources.title: Hugh M. Hamill Jr., The Hidalgo Revolt: Prelude to Mexican Independence (1966)
Britannica: Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla
Brian R. Hamnett, A Concise History of Mexico (3rd ed., 2019)
Wikipedia: Grito de Dolores

note: No verbatim record of Hidalgo's words survives; versions were reconstructed later.

story.en:
The conspiracy had been meeting for months in the houses of Querétaro, disguised as a literary club, under the protection of Josefa Ortiz de Domínguez, wife of the town's magistrate. When it was betrayed in September 1810 she managed to send word to Ignacio Allende and Hidalgo in Dolores. Rather than flee, Hidalgo acted. Before dawn on Sunday 16 September he freed the prisoners from the town jail, rang the church bell and addressed the crowd that gathered for Mass.

Nobody wrote down his words. Later accounts have him shouting "Long live the Virgin of Guadalupe! Long live Ferdinand VII! Death to bad government!", a call that combined religion, loyalty to the captive Spanish king and hatred of the peninsular Spaniards who monopolised office. Taking a banner of Guadalupe from the sanctuary at Atotonilco, Hidalgo marched with a growing army of Indigenous and mestizo peasants and miners. Each year on the night of 15 September the president of Mexico repeats the grito from the balcony of the National Palace, ringing the very bell of Dolores.
story.zh:
密谋者们以文学社为掩护，在克雷塔罗城的宅邸中聚会了好几个月，受到该城地方官之妻何塞法·奥尔蒂斯·德多明格斯的庇护。1810年9月密谋泄露时，她设法把消息送到多洛雷斯的伊格纳西奥·阿连德和伊达尔戈手中。伊达尔戈没有逃走，而是立即行动。9月16日星期日黎明前，他释放了镇监狱的囚犯，敲响教堂钟声，向前来望弥撒的人群发表讲话。

没有人记下他说了什么。后来的记述称他高呼：“瓜达卢佩圣母万岁！斐迪南七世万岁！打倒坏政府！”这一口号融合了宗教、对被囚西班牙国王的效忠，以及对垄断官职的半岛西班牙人的憎恨。伊达尔戈从阿托托尼尔科圣所取来瓜达卢佩圣母旗，率领由原住民、梅斯蒂索农民和矿工组成、不断壮大的队伍出征。每年9月15日夜，墨西哥总统都会在国家宫阳台上敲响多洛雷斯的那口钟，重现这声呼喊。

summary.en: Begun by Miguel Hidalgo's peasant army in 1810 and continued by José María Morelos and guerrilla leaders such as Vicente Guerrero, the insurgency against Spanish rule ended in 1821 when the royalist officer Agustín de Iturbide joined the rebels under the Plan of Iguala, and New Spain became the independent Mexican Empire.
summary.zh: 1810年由米格尔·伊达尔戈的农民军发起，此后由何塞·玛丽亚·莫雷洛斯以及比森特·格雷罗等游击领袖继续进行的反西班牙统治起义，到1821年保王派军官阿古斯丁·德伊图尔比德根据《伊瓜拉计划》投向起义者时宣告结束，新西班牙成为独立的墨西哥帝国。

summary.en: Convened by José María Morelos in September 1813, the Congress of Anáhuac at Chilpancingo heard his "Sentiments of the Nation", calling for sovereignty of the people, the abolition of slavery and caste distinctions, and on 6 November 1813 declared North America independent of Spain.

summary.en: On 24 February 1821 Agustín de Iturbide and the insurgent Vicente Guerrero proclaimed the Plan of Iguala: independence under a constitutional monarchy, Catholicism and equality for all inhabitants (the "Three Guarantees"). The Treaty of Córdoba followed in August, and the Army of the Three Guarantees entered Mexico City on 27 September.
summary.zh: 1821年2月24日，阿古斯丁·德伊图尔比德与起义领袖比森特·格雷罗宣布《伊瓜拉计划》：在君主立宪制下独立、尊奉天主教、全体居民一律平等（即“三项保证”）。8月签订《科尔多瓦条约》，9月27日三保证军进入墨西哥城。
