name.en: Act of Independence of Central America

summary.en: On 15 September 1821 notables meeting in Guatemala City declared the Kingdom of Guatemala independent of Spain. The region was annexed to Iturbide's Mexican Empire in 1822, then formed the Federal Republic of Central America in 1823. 15 September is the independence day of Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica.
summary.zh: 1821年9月15日，聚集在危地马拉城的名流宣布危地马拉王国脱离西班牙独立。1822年该地区被并入伊图尔比德的墨西哥帝国，1823年组成中美洲联邦共和国。9月15日是危地马拉、萨尔瓦多、洪都拉斯、尼加拉瓜和哥斯达黎加的独立日。

sources.title: Ralph Lee Woodward Jr., Central America: A Nation Divided (3rd ed., 1999)
Jordana Dym, From Sovereign Villages to National States: City, State, and Federation in Central America, 1759–1839 (2006)
Wikipedia: Act of Independence of Central America

story.en:
Independence came to Central America almost by default. Once the news of Iturbide's Plan of Iguala reached Guatemala, the captain general Gabino Gaínza called a meeting of officials, clergy and leading citizens in the National Palace on 15 September 1821. Outside, a crowd gathered by liberal activists, among them María Dolores Bedoya, whose fireworks and music urged the delegates on, cheered for independence.

The act, drafted by the Honduran lawyer José Cecilio del Valle, declared independence "to prevent the dreadful consequences that would follow if the people themselves proclaimed it". Gaínza stayed in charge. Within months the conservative elite, fearing radicals, voted to join Mexico; only El Salvador resisted and was invaded. When Iturbide fell in 1823 the provinces declared themselves the United Provinces of Central America (except Chiapas, which stayed Mexican). Soon the quarrels of liberals and conservatives and the rivalry of the provinces tore the federation apart, and by 1841 five separate republics had emerged.
story.zh:
中美洲的独立几乎是顺势而来。伊图尔比德《伊瓜拉计划》的消息传到危地马拉后，都督加维诺·盖因萨于1821年9月15日在国家宫召集官员、教士和名流开会。宫外，由自由派活动人士聚集的人群为独立欢呼，其中包括玛丽亚·多洛雷斯·贝多亚，她以烟花和音乐催促代表们作出决定。

独立法案由洪都拉斯律师何塞·塞西略·德尔巴列起草，声称宣布独立是“为了防止人民自行宣布独立将带来的可怕后果”。盖因萨继续掌权。几个月内，惧怕激进派的保守精英投票决定并入墨西哥，只有萨尔瓦多反对并因此遭到入侵。1823年伊图尔比德倒台后，各省宣布成立中美洲联合省（恰帕斯除外，它留在墨西哥）。不久，自由派与保守派之争以及各省之间的竞争使联邦四分五裂，到1841年已形成五个独立的共和国。

name.en: France imposes the "independence debt" on Haiti
name.zh: 法国向海地强加“独立债务”

summary.en: In 1825, with warships off Port-au-Prince, King Charles X of France agreed to recognise Haiti's independence in return for an indemnity of 150 million francs to former colonists. President Jean-Pierre Boyer accepted. Reduced to 90 million in 1838, the debt and the loans taken to pay it burdened Haiti until the mid-20th century.
summary.zh: 1825年，在法国战舰兵临太子港之际，法王查理十世同意承认海地独立，条件是向前殖民者支付1.5亿法郎赔款。让-皮埃尔·布瓦耶总统接受了这一条件。这笔债务在1838年减为9000万法郎，它连同为偿债而举借的贷款，使海地背负沉重负担直到20世纪中叶。

sources.title: François Blancpain, Un siècle de relations financières entre Haïti et la France (1825–1922) (2001)
The New York Times, "The Ransom" (series, 20 May 2022)
Wikipedia: Haiti indemnity controversy

story.en:
For two decades after 1804 Haiti lived under the threat of a French invasion and without diplomatic recognition from any major power. In July 1825 a French squadron of fourteen warships anchored off Port-au-Prince. The envoy, Baron de Mackau, brought a royal ordinance: France would "concede" independence to the French part of Saint-Domingue if Haiti paid 150 million francs in five annual instalments to compensate former colonists, and halved customs duties on French goods.

President Boyer accepted. The sum was about ten times Haiti's annual revenue. To pay the first instalment Haiti borrowed from French banks, creating a "double debt". The indemnity was cut to 90 million francs in 1838, and the last payments on the related loans were made only in the 1940s and 1950s. A 2022 investigation by The New York Times estimated that the payments cost Haiti between 21 and 115 billion dollars in lost economic growth. In 2003 President Jean-Bertrand Aristide demanded restitution from France; the question remains open.
story.zh:
1804年后的二十年间，海地一直生活在法国入侵的阴影下，也得不到任何大国的外交承认。1825年7月，由14艘战舰组成的法国舰队在太子港外下锚。特使马考男爵带来一道王室敕令：只要海地分五年向前殖民者支付1.5亿法郎赔款，并将法国商品关税减半，法国便“准予”圣多明各法属部分独立。

布瓦耶总统接受了。这笔钱约相当于海地年财政收入的十倍。为支付第一期款项，海地向法国银行借贷，形成“双重债务”。1838年赔款减为9000万法郎，而相关贷款的最后一笔直到20世纪四五十年代才还清。《纽约时报》2022年的调查估计，这些支付使海地损失了210亿至1150亿美元的经济增长。2003年，让-贝特朗·阿里斯蒂德总统要求法国归还赔款；这一问题至今悬而未决。

summary.en: On 27 February 1844 members of Juan Pablo Duarte's secret society La Trinitaria seized the Puerta del Conde in Santo Domingo and proclaimed the Dominican Republic independent of Haiti, which had ruled the whole island since 1822. Haitian invasions were repelled in a war that lasted until 1856.
summary.zh: 1844年2月27日，胡安·巴勃罗·杜阿尔特创立的秘密社团“三位一体会”成员夺取圣多明各的伯爵门，宣布多米尼加共和国脱离自1822年起统治全岛的海地而独立。此后海地多次入侵均被击退，战争一直持续到1856年。

sources.title: Frank Moya Pons, The Dominican Republic: A National History (3rd ed., 2010)
Britannica: Dominican Republic: History
Wikipedia: Dominican War of Independence

summary.en: In 1847 Maya peasants of eastern Yucatán, burdened by taxes, debt and land loss, rose against the white and mestizo elite and nearly took Mérida in 1848. The rebels retreated to the forests of the east, where the cult of the Talking Cross at Chan Santa Cruz sustained a de facto Maya state until Mexican troops occupied it in 1901.
summary.zh: 1847年，不堪赋税、债务和失地之苦的尤卡坦东部玛雅农民起来反抗白人和梅斯蒂索精英，1848年几乎攻下梅里达。起义者退入东部森林，以禅圣克鲁斯“会说话的十字架”信仰为核心，维持了一个事实上的玛雅国家，直到1901年墨西哥军队占领该地。

sources.title: Nelson A. Reed, The Caste War of Yucatán (rev. ed., 2001)
Terry Rugeley, Rebellion Now and Forever: Mayas, Hispanics, and Caste War Violence in Yucatán, 1800–1880 (2009)
Wikipedia: Caste War of Yucatán

note: Marker at Chan Santa Cruz (today Felipe Carrillo Puerto, Quintana Roo).

story.en:
In July 1847 the authorities in Valladolid, Yucatán, executed Manuel Antonio Ay, a Maya batab (local leader) accused of plotting rebellion. His comrades Cecilio Chi and Jacinto Pat struck first, attacking the town of Tepich. The revolt spread with astonishing speed. By May 1848 Maya armies had taken Valladolid and Izamal and stood within reach of Mérida and Campeche, whose terrified residents prepared to flee by sea. Then, according to a much-retold story, the rebel soldiers saw the winged ants that signal the first rains and went home to plant their maize.

Whatever the reason, the offensive collapsed, and Yucatán's government, which had declared independence from Mexico, rejoined the country to get help. The rebels fell back to the southeast. In 1850 at a cenote in the forest a cross began to "speak", through a ventriloquist, urging continued war. Around it grew Chan Santa Cruz, a theocratic Maya polity that traded guns with British Belize and resisted for half a century. Mexican troops under General Ignacio Bravo occupied it only in 1901, and some villages never formally surrendered.
story.zh:
1847年7月，尤卡坦巴利亚多利德当局处决了被控密谋叛乱的玛雅地方首领曼努埃尔·安东尼奥·艾。他的同伴塞西利奥·奇和哈辛托·帕特抢先动手，进攻特皮奇镇。起义以惊人的速度蔓延。到1848年5月，玛雅大军已攻占巴利亚多利德和伊萨马尔，兵临梅里达和坎佩切，惊恐的居民准备从海上逃走。随后，据一个流传甚广的故事所说，起义士兵看到了预示雨季来临的飞蚁，便回家种玉米去了。

不论原因为何，攻势瓦解了；此前宣布脱离墨西哥独立的尤卡坦政府为求援助，重新加入墨西哥。起义者退往东南。1850年，森林中一处天然井边的十字架开始借腹语者之口“说话”，号召继续战斗。围绕它兴起了禅圣克鲁斯，一个与英属伯利兹交易枪支、抵抗了半个世纪的玛雅神权政体。直到1901年，伊格纳西奥·布拉沃将军率领的墨西哥军队才占领该地，一些村庄始终没有正式投降。

name.en: National War against William Walker (Filibuster War)
name.zh: 反对威廉·沃克的国民战争（海盗战争）

summary.en: The American adventurer William Walker, invited by Nicaraguan Liberals, seized Granada in 1855, made himself president of Nicaragua in 1856 and re-legalised slavery. Costa Rica, Honduras, El Salvador and Guatemala united against him; he surrendered in 1857 and was executed in Honduras in 1860 after a later attempt.
summary.zh: 美国冒险家威廉·沃克应尼加拉瓜自由派之邀，于1855年夺取格拉纳达，1856年自任尼加拉瓜总统并恢复奴隶制合法地位。哥斯达黎加、洪都拉斯、萨尔瓦多和危地马拉联合起来反抗他；他于1857年投降，后因再次图谋，于1860年在洪都拉斯被处决。

sources.title: Michel Gobat, Confronting the American Dream: Nicaragua under U.S. Imperial Rule (2005)
Ralph Lee Woodward Jr., Central America: A Nation Divided (3rd ed., 1999)
Wikipedia: Filibuster War

note: Marker at Rivas, where the Costa Rican drummer Juan Santamaría set fire to Walker's stronghold on 11 April 1856.

story.en:
William Walker, a Tennessee-born doctor, lawyer and journalist, had already tried to carve a republic out of Mexican Baja California. In 1855 Nicaragua's Liberals, losing a civil war, hired him; he landed with 58 men, "the Immortals", took the Conservative capital Granada by surprise and soon controlled the country through a puppet president. The transit route across Nicaragua, used by gold-seekers bound for California, made the country valuable, and Walker hoped to win Southern support by reintroducing slavery and making English an official language. In July 1856 he had himself inaugurated president.

Central America's republics, for once, united. At Rivas on 11 April 1856 Costa Rican troops attacked Walker's men in a fortified inn; the young drummer Juan Santamaría volunteered to set it on fire and was shot dead, becoming Costa Rica's national hero. In Nicaragua, Andrés Castro is remembered for killing a filibuster with a stone at San Jacinto in September. Besieged at Rivas, Walker surrendered to a US Navy officer in May 1857. After a third expedition he was captured by the British and handed to Honduras, which shot him at Trujillo in 1860.
story.zh:
威廉·沃克生于田纳西，当过医生、律师和记者，此前曾试图在墨西哥下加利福尼亚建立一个共和国。1855年，内战失利的尼加拉瓜自由派雇用了他；他带着58人（号称“不死者”）登陆，出其不意地攻下保守派首府格拉纳达，很快通过一位傀儡总统控制了全国。横贯尼加拉瓜、供前往加利福尼亚淘金者使用的过境通道使这个国家价值倍增；沃克希望通过恢复奴隶制、把英语定为官方语言来赢得美国南方的支持。1856年7月，他自己就任总统。

中美洲各共和国难得地团结起来。1856年4月11日在里瓦斯，哥斯达黎加军队进攻沃克部下据守的一座设防客栈；年轻的鼓手胡安·圣玛丽亚自告奋勇前去纵火，中弹身亡，成为哥斯达黎加的民族英雄。在尼加拉瓜，人们纪念安德烈斯·卡斯特罗，他于9月在圣哈辛托用石头砸死了一名海盗。被围困在里瓦斯的沃克于1857年5月向一名美国海军军官投降。第三次远征时他被英国人俘获并移交洪都拉斯，1860年在特鲁希略被枪决。

summary.en: The Liberal constitution of 1857 and laws stripping the Church and corporations of property provoked a Conservative revolt. For three years two governments fought a civil war, the Liberals under Benito Juárez based at Veracruz; the Liberals won, entering Mexico City in January 1861.
summary.zh: 1857年自由派宪法以及剥夺教会和团体财产的法律激起保守派叛乱。三年间两个政府展开内战，以贝尼托·华雷斯为首、以韦拉克鲁斯为基地的自由派最终获胜，于1861年1月进入墨西哥城。

sources.title: Brian Hamnett, Juárez (1994)
Brian R. Hamnett, A Concise History of Mexico (3rd ed., 2019)
Wikipedia: Reform War

note: Marker at Veracruz, seat of Juárez's government 1858–1860.

summary.en: On 5 May 1862 a Mexican army under General Ignacio Zaragoza repulsed the attack of a larger, better-armed French force on the forts of Loreto and Guadalupe above Puebla. The victory delayed the French intervention for a year and is celebrated as Cinco de Mayo.
summary.zh: 1862年5月5日，伊格纳西奥·萨拉戈萨将军率领的墨西哥军队，在普埃布拉城上方的洛雷托和瓜达卢佩堡垒击退了兵力更多、装备更精良的法军进攻。这场胜利使法国的干涉推迟了一年，人们以“五月五日节”纪念它。

sources.title: Britannica: Battle of Puebla
Jack Autrey Dabbs, The French Army in Mexico, 1861–1867 (1963)
Wikipedia: Battle of Puebla

story.en:
In July 1861 the Juárez government, bankrupt after the Reform War, suspended payments on its foreign debts. Britain, Spain and France sent troops to Veracruz. The British and Spanish soon negotiated and left, but Napoleon III had larger plans: a Catholic, Latin monarchy in Mexico that would check the United States, then absorbed in its civil war.

The French commander, the Count of Lorencez, marched inland with about 6,000 men, confident that Mexicans would welcome him. On 5 May he attacked the hilltop forts above Puebla head-on. General Ignacio Zaragoza, a 33-year-old born in Texas, had some 4,000 to 5,000 men, many poorly armed. Rain turned the slopes to mud; the French assaults were cut down, and a cavalry charge, with a brigade led by the young Porfirio Díaz holding the flank, drove them back. Lorencez lost around 460 dead.

Zaragoza reported to Juárez that "the national arms have covered themselves with glory". The French returned with 30,000 troops and took Puebla in 1863 after a two-month siege. But Cinco de Mayo became a symbol of resistance, celebrated more widely today among Mexican Americans in the United States than in Mexico itself.
story.zh:
1861年7月，因改革战争而财政破产的华雷斯政府宣布暂停偿还外债。英国、西班牙和法国派兵前往韦拉克鲁斯。英西两国很快通过谈判撤军，而拿破仑三世却另有图谋：在墨西哥建立一个天主教的拉丁君主国，以遏制当时深陷内战的美国。

法军司令洛朗塞伯爵率约6000人向内陆进军，自信墨西哥人会欢迎他。5月5日，他从正面进攻普埃布拉城上方的山顶堡垒。时年33岁、生于得克萨斯的伊格纳西奥·萨拉戈萨将军手下有四五千人，许多人装备简陋。大雨使山坡变成泥沼，法军的冲锋一次次被击退；一次骑兵冲锋（由年轻的波菲里奥·迪亚斯率一个旅守住侧翼）把他们赶了回去。洛朗塞阵亡约460人。

萨拉戈萨向华雷斯报告：“国家的军队赢得了荣耀。”法军调来3万大军，在两个月围城后于1863年攻下普埃布拉。但五月五日节成为抵抗的象征，如今在美国的墨西哥裔中比在墨西哥本土庆祝得更为广泛。

name.en: Execution of Emperor Maximilian at Querétaro
name.zh: 马克西米连皇帝在克雷塔罗被处决

summary.en: After French troops withdrew, the Republican armies of Benito Juárez besieged Emperor Maximilian at Querétaro. Captured in May 1867, he was tried by court-martial and shot on the Cerro de las Campanas on 19 June with Generals Miguel Miramón and Tomás Mejía, ending the Second Mexican Empire.
summary.zh: 法军撤走后，贝尼托·华雷斯的共和派军队把马克西米连皇帝围困在克雷塔罗。他于1867年5月被俘，经军事法庭审判，6月19日与米格尔·米拉蒙、托马斯·梅希亚两位将军一起在钟山被枪决，第二墨西哥帝国随之终结。

sources.title: Jasper Ridley, Maximilian and Juárez (1992)
Britannica: Maximilian
Wikipedia: Maximilian I of Mexico

story.en:
Ferdinand Maximilian, younger brother of the Austrian emperor Franz Joseph, accepted the crown of Mexico in 1864 from a deputation of Mexican conservatives and with the backing of French bayonets. He and his wife Carlota arrived at Veracruz in May. Earnest and liberal by instinct, he disappointed his conservative backers by confirming the sale of Church property, while Juárez's republic fought on from the north.

When the American Civil War ended, the United States pressed France to leave, and Napoleon III, facing Prussia in Europe, withdrew his army in 1866–67. Carlota sailed to Europe to plead for help, suffered a mental breakdown in Rome and never returned. Maximilian refused to abdicate and joined his last troops at Querétaro, where after a 70-day siege he was betrayed and captured in May 1867.

Victor Hugo and Giuseppe Garibaldi appealed for mercy, but Juárez refused, wanting to show Europe that Mexico could not be conquered. Maximilian gave each of the firing squad a gold coin and asked them to aim at his heart. Édouard Manet painted the execution in several versions, in the style of Goya's Third of May.
story.zh:
费迪南德·马克西米连是奥地利皇帝弗朗茨·约瑟夫的弟弟，1864年他从墨西哥保守派代表团手中接受了墨西哥皇冠，背后是法国的刺刀。同年5月，他与妻子卡洛塔抵达韦拉克鲁斯。他为人诚恳，天性偏于自由主义，确认了教会财产的出售，令保守派支持者大失所望；华雷斯的共和国则在北方坚持作战。

美国内战结束后，美国施压要求法国撤离；在欧洲面临普鲁士威胁的拿破仑三世于1866至1867年间撤回军队。卡洛塔前往欧洲求援，在罗马精神崩溃，再未归来。马克西米连拒绝退位，前往克雷塔罗与最后的部队会合，经过70天围城，于1867年5月遭人出卖被俘。

维克多·雨果和朱塞佩·加里波第呼吁宽恕，但华雷斯拒绝了，他要向欧洲表明墨西哥不可征服。马克西米连给每一名行刑士兵一枚金币，请他们瞄准他的心脏。爱德华·马奈仿照戈雅《1808年5月3日》的风格，把这次处决画成了好几个版本。

summary.en: On 10 October 1868 the planter Carlos Manuel de Céspedes freed his slaves at his La Demajagua estate and proclaimed Cuban independence (the Grito de Yara). The rebels held much of eastern Cuba for a decade before the Pact of Zanjón of 1878; General Antonio Maceo rejected it in the Protest of Baraguá.
summary.zh: 1868年10月10日，种植园主卡洛斯·曼努埃尔·德塞斯佩德斯在其拉德马哈瓜庄园解放奴隶，宣布古巴独立（“亚拉呼声”）。起义者控制古巴东部大部地区长达十年，直到1878年签订《桑洪条约》；安东尼奥·马塞奥将军以“巴拉瓜抗议”拒绝接受该条约。

sources.title: Louis A. Pérez Jr., Cuba: Between Reform and Revolution (5th ed., 2015)
Ada Ferrer, Insurgent Cuba: Race, Nation, and Revolution, 1868–1898 (1999)
Wikipedia: Ten Years' War

note: Marker near La Demajagua, outside Manzanillo.

summary.en: A royal decree of 7 October 1886 ended the "patronato", the system of apprenticeship that had replaced slavery in Cuba in 1880, freeing the last 25,000 or so people held in bondage. Cuba was the last Spanish colony, and with Brazil (1888) one of the last places in the Americas, to abolish slavery.
summary.zh: 1886年10月7日的一道王室敕令废除了古巴1880年用以取代奴隶制的“庇护制”学徒制度，解放了最后约2.5万名受奴役者。古巴是最后一个废除奴隶制的西班牙殖民地，与巴西（1888年）同为美洲最后废奴的地区之一。

sources.title: Rebecca J. Scott, Slave Emancipation in Cuba: The Transition to Free Labor, 1860–1899 (1985)
Louis A. Pérez Jr., Cuba: Between Reform and Revolution (5th ed., 2015)
Britannica: Cuba: History

summary.en: Organised from exile by José Martí's Cuban Revolutionary Party, a new war began in February 1895; Martí was killed at Dos Ríos in May. Under Máximo Gómez and Antonio Maceo the insurgents invaded the west, and Spain's general Weyler herded peasants into deadly reconcentration camps. US intervention in 1898 ended Spanish rule.
summary.zh: 1895年2月，由何塞·马蒂在流亡中组建的古巴革命党筹划的新战争爆发；马蒂于5月在多斯里奥斯阵亡。在马克西莫·戈麦斯和安东尼奥·马塞奥率领下，起义者向西部挺进，西班牙将军韦勒则把农民强行集中到死亡率极高的“集中营”。1898年美国的干预结束了西班牙的统治。

sources.title: Louis A. Pérez Jr., Cuba: Between Reform and Revolution (5th ed., 2015)
Ada Ferrer, Insurgent Cuba: Race, Nation, and Revolution, 1868–1898 (1999)
John Lawrence Tone, War and Genocide in Cuba, 1895–1898 (2006)
Wikipedia: Cuban War of Independence

note: Marker at Dos Ríos, where Martí fell on 19 May 1895.

story.en:
José Martí spent fifteen years in New York building a movement: raising funds from cigar workers in Tampa and Key West, reconciling the old generals of the Ten Years' War, and writing that the new Cuba must be "with all and for the good of all", without racial divisions. On 24 February 1895 risings began in eastern Cuba. Martí, with General Máximo Gómez, landed at Playitas in April. On 19 May, near the confluence of the Cauto and Contramaestre rivers at Dos Ríos, he rode forward against a Spanish column and was shot dead, his body carried off by the Spaniards.

The war he started was fought with fire. Gómez and Maceo burned cane fields to wreck the colonial economy and marched the length of the island. In 1896 the Spanish commander Valeriano Weyler ordered rural people into fortified towns; perhaps 150,000 to 170,000 died of hunger and disease in this "reconcentration". American newspapers, led by Hearst and Pulitzer, made the suffering a cause. When the battleship USS Maine exploded in Havana harbour in February 1898, the United States declared war, and within months Spain's 400-year rule over Cuba was over.
story.zh:
何塞·马蒂在纽约用了十五年时间组织运动：向坦帕和基韦斯特的雪茄工人募款，调解十年战争的老将领们，并写道新古巴必须“与所有人一起，为了所有人的福祉”，不分种族。1895年2月24日，古巴东部爆发起义。4月，马蒂与马克西莫·戈麦斯将军在普拉伊塔斯登陆。5月19日，在考托河与孔特拉马埃斯特雷河交汇处的多斯里奥斯附近，他策马冲向一支西班牙纵队，中弹身亡，遗体被西班牙人带走。

他发动的这场战争以火为武器。戈麦斯和马塞奥焚烧甘蔗田以摧毁殖民经济，并纵贯全岛进军。1896年，西班牙司令瓦莱里亚诺·韦勒下令把农村居民赶进设防城镇；在这场“集中”中，约15万至17万人死于饥饿和疾病。以赫斯特和普利策为首的美国报纸大力渲染这一苦难。1898年2月美国战舰“缅因”号在哈瓦那港爆炸后，美国宣战，几个月内西班牙对古巴400年的统治便告结束。

name.en: Naval Battle of Santiago de Cuba

summary.en: On 3 July 1898 Admiral Pascual Cervera's Spanish squadron tried to break out of Santiago de Cuba harbour and was destroyed by the US fleet in about four hours. With Santiago besieged by US and Cuban forces, the city surrendered on 17 July, ending Spanish power in Cuba.
summary.zh: 1898年7月3日，帕斯夸尔·塞韦拉海军上将的西班牙舰队试图冲出圣地亚哥-德古巴港，约四小时内被美国舰队全歼。在美军和古巴起义军的围困下，该城于7月17日投降，西班牙在古巴的势力就此终结。

sources.title: David F. Trask, The War with Spain in 1898 (1981)
Louis A. Pérez Jr., Cuba: Between Reform and Revolution (5th ed., 2015)
Wikipedia: Battle of Santiago de Cuba

note: The wider Spanish–American War (1898) is left to the north-america dataset; this record covers its decisive Cuban battle. Cuban insurgents were excluded from the surrender ceremony, a grievance that shaped later Cuban nationalism.

summary.en: After Colombia's Senate rejected a canal treaty, Panamanian separatists backed by the French engineer Philippe Bunau-Varilla declared independence on 3 November 1903; US warships prevented Colombian troops from landing. Two weeks later the Hay–Bunau-Varilla Treaty gave the United States a canal zone in perpetuity.
summary.zh: 哥伦比亚参议院否决运河条约后，得到法国工程师菲利普·比诺-瓦里亚支持的巴拿马分离主义者于1903年11月3日宣布独立；美国军舰阻止哥伦比亚军队登陆。两周后，《海-比诺-瓦里亚条约》把一片运河区永久交给美国。

sources.title: David McCullough, The Path Between the Seas: The Creation of the Panama Canal, 1870–1914 (1977)
Michael L. Conniff, Panama and the United States: The End of the Alliance (3rd ed., 2012)
Wikipedia: Separation of Panama from Colombia

summary.en: Commissioned by the education minister José Vasconcelos, Diego Rivera, José Clemente Orozco, David Alfaro Siqueiros and others began in 1922 to paint the walls of public buildings in Mexico City with scenes of Mexican history, labour and Indigenous life, creating an art for the people of the Revolution that influenced artists worldwide.
summary.zh: 受教育部长何塞·巴斯孔塞洛斯委托，迭戈·里维拉、何塞·克莱门特·奥罗斯科、大卫·阿尔法罗·西凯罗斯等人自1922年起在墨西哥城公共建筑的墙壁上描绘墨西哥历史、劳动和原住民生活，创造了一种属于革命人民的艺术，影响遍及世界。

sources.title: Desmond Rochfort, Mexican Muralists: Orozco, Rivera, Siqueiros (1993)
Britannica: Mexican muralism
Wikipedia: Mexican muralism

note: Marker at the Antiguo Colegio de San Ildefonso, where the first murals were painted.

story.en:
After ten years of revolution, José Vasconcelos, rector of the university and then minister of education, wanted a culture that every Mexican could share, including the millions who could not read. Walls were the answer. In 1922 he gave painters the courtyards of the old Jesuit college of San Ildefonso and the new ministry building, paying them by the day like labourers. They formed a union and issued a manifesto denouncing easel painting as aristocratic.

Diego Rivera, just back from fourteen years in Europe, covered the ministry's two courtyards with 235 panels: Indigenous festivals, miners, a teacher in a village, and capitalists dining on gold. Orozco painted savage, grieving scenes of the Revolution at San Ildefonso; Siqueiros experimented with industrial paints and spray guns. Rivera's epic history of Mexico on the stairway of the National Palace (1929–1935) runs from Quetzalcoatl to Marx.

The muralists took their art abroad: Rivera to Detroit and to the Rockefeller Center in New York, where his mural was destroyed in 1934 because it showed Lenin. Their example inspired the US New Deal mural programme and public art from Chile to Los Angeles.
story.zh:
经过十年革命，先任大学校长后任教育部长的何塞·巴斯孔塞洛斯希望创造一种全体墨西哥人、包括数百万不识字者都能共享的文化。墙壁就是答案。1922年，他把旧耶稣会圣伊尔德丰索学院的庭院和新教育部大楼交给画家们，像对待工人一样按日付酬。画家们组织了工会，发表宣言，斥架上绘画为贵族艺术。

刚在欧洲度过十四年的迭戈·里维拉，在教育部的两座庭院画满了235幅壁画：原住民节庆、矿工、乡村教师，以及用黄金进餐的资本家。奥罗斯科在圣伊尔德丰索画下了革命中暴烈而哀恸的场景；西凯罗斯则尝试使用工业涂料和喷枪。里维拉在国家宫楼梯上绘制的墨西哥史诗（1929—1935年）从克察尔科亚特尔一直画到马克思。

壁画家们把艺术带到国外：里维拉去了底特律和纽约洛克菲勒中心，后者的壁画因画有列宁而于1934年被毁。他们的榜样启发了美国新政时期的壁画计划，以及从智利到洛杉矶的公共艺术。

summary.en: After a failed French attempt (1881–1889) and ten years of US construction, the 82 km Panama Canal opened on 15 August 1914 with the passage of the SS Ancon. Its locks lift ships 26 m to the artificial Gatún Lake; some 25,000 workers, most from the Caribbean, died building the French and American canals.
summary.zh: 经过法国的失败尝试（1881—1889年）和美国十年施工，长82公里的巴拿马运河于1914年8月15日随“安孔”号的通过而正式通航。运河船闸把船只提升26米进入人工开凿的加通湖。法美两国修建运河期间约有2.5万名工人死亡，其中大多数来自加勒比地区。

sources.title: David McCullough, The Path Between the Seas: The Creation of the Panama Canal, 1870–1914 (1977)
Julie Greene, The Canal Builders: Making America's Empire at the Panama Canal (2009)
Britannica: Panama Canal
Wikipedia: Panama Canal

note: Death toll estimates: about 22,000 in the French period and 5,600 in the US period.

story.en:
Ferdinand de Lesseps, builder of the Suez Canal, began digging in 1881, determined to cut a sea-level channel through the mountains of the isthmus. Landslides in the Culebra Cut, floods of the Chagres River, yellow fever and malaria defeated him; perhaps 22,000 workers died, and the company collapsed in 1889 in a financial scandal that shook France.

The United States, having secured the Canal Zone in 1903, started work in 1904. The army doctor William Gorgas, acting on the new understanding that mosquitoes spread yellow fever and malaria, fumigated houses, drained pools and screened windows, and yellow fever vanished from Panama by 1906. Chief engineer John Stevens and then Colonel George Goethals abandoned the sea-level plan for a lock canal: a dam on the Chagres created Gatún Lake, at the time the largest artificial lake in the world, and three sets of locks raised and lowered ships.

The heaviest labour fell to about 150,000 workers from Barbados, Jamaica and other islands, paid in silver under a segregated system while white Americans were paid in gold. The canal opened quietly on 15 August 1914, eleven days after the First World War began, cutting the voyage from New York to San Francisco by about 13,000 km.
story.zh:
苏伊士运河的建造者斐迪南·德莱塞普于1881年开工，决心在地峡群山中开凿一条海平面运河。库莱布拉切口的山体滑坡、查格雷斯河的洪水、黄热病和疟疾击败了他；约2.2万名工人丧生，公司于1889年在一场震动法国的金融丑闻中破产。

美国在1903年获得运河区后，于1904年开工。陆军军医威廉·戈加斯依据蚊子传播黄热病和疟疾的新认识，熏蒸房屋、排干积水、给窗户装纱网；到1906年，黄热病在巴拿马绝迹。总工程师约翰·史蒂文斯和后任的乔治·戈瑟尔斯上校放弃了海平面方案，改建船闸式运河：查格雷斯河上的一座水坝造出加通湖，这是当时世界上最大的人工湖，三组船闸让船只升降通行。

最繁重的劳动落在约15万名来自巴巴多斯、牙买加等岛屿的工人身上，他们在种族隔离制度下领取银币工资，而美国白人领取的是金币工资。运河于1914年8月15日悄然通航，距第一次世界大战爆发仅11天，使纽约至旧金山的航程缩短约1.3万公里。

summary.en: Francisco Madero's call to revolt against the 34-year rule of Porfirio Díaz in November 1910 began a decade of civil war among shifting factions, Zapata's agrarians in the south, Villa's Division of the North, and Carranza and Obregón's Constitutionalists. Perhaps a million people died; the Constitution of 1917 promised land reform, labour rights and secular education.
summary.zh: 1910年11月，弗朗西斯科·马德罗号召起义反抗波菲里奥·迪亚斯长达34年的统治，由此开始了十年内战，参战各派分合不定：南方萨帕塔的土地派、比利亚的北方师，以及卡兰萨和奥夫雷贡的立宪派。死亡人数或达百万；1917年宪法许诺土地改革、劳工权利和世俗教育。

sources.title: Alan Knight, The Mexican Revolution (2 vols., 1986)
John Womack Jr., Zapata and the Mexican Revolution (1968)
Friedrich Katz, The Life and Times of Pancho Villa (1998)
Britannica: Mexican Revolution
Wikipedia: Mexican Revolution

note: Death toll estimates range from about 1 to 2 million, including deaths from disease and famine; some historians end the Revolution in 1917, 1920 or 1940.

story.en:
By 1910 Porfirio Díaz had ruled Mexico for a generation. Railways, mines and oil fields had been built with foreign capital, but most rural people had lost their land to haciendas, and elections were a sham. When the wealthy northerner Francisco Madero challenged Díaz in the 1910 election, he was jailed; from exile in Texas he called for revolt on 20 November. Pascual Orozco and Pancho Villa took Ciudad Juárez in May 1911, and the old dictator sailed for Paris.

Madero proved too cautious for Emiliano Zapata, whose Plan of Ayala demanded the return of village lands, and too liberal for the old army. In February 1913 General Victoriano Huerta overthrew and murdered him. The revolt against Huerta united Villa, Zapata and the Constitutionalists of Venustiano Carranza, then split into a war between the victors. In December 1914 Villa and Zapata occupied Mexico City and were photographed side by side in the presidential palace, Villa laughing in the presidential chair. In 1915 Álvaro Obregón's trenches and machine guns broke Villa's cavalry at Celaya.

The Constitution of 1917, still in force, nationalised subsoil resources, promised land reform and an eight-hour day, and curbed the Church. Zapata was ambushed in 1919, Carranza killed in 1920, and Villa assassinated in 1923.
story.zh:
到1910年，波菲里奥·迪亚斯已统治墨西哥整整一代人。铁路、矿山和油田借助外资建成，但多数农村人口的土地落入大庄园之手，选举形同虚设。北方富豪弗朗西斯科·马德罗在1910年大选中挑战迪亚斯，结果被投入监狱；他流亡得克萨斯，号召人民于11月20日起义。1911年5月，帕斯夸尔·奥罗斯科和潘乔·比利亚攻占华雷斯城，老独裁者乘船前往巴黎。

对埃米利亚诺·萨帕塔来说，马德罗过于谨慎；萨帕塔的《阿亚拉计划》要求归还村社土地。而对旧军队来说，马德罗又过于自由。1913年2月，维多里亚诺·韦尔塔将军推翻并杀害了他。反对韦尔塔的斗争把比利亚、萨帕塔和贝努斯蒂亚诺·卡兰萨的立宪派联合在一起，胜利后又分裂为胜利者之间的战争。1914年12月，比利亚和萨帕塔占领墨西哥城，两人在总统府并肩合影，比利亚坐在总统椅上大笑。1915年，阿尔瓦罗·奥夫雷贡的堑壕和机枪在塞拉亚击溃了比利亚的骑兵。

至今仍有效的1917年宪法把地下资源收归国有，许诺土地改革和八小时工作制，并限制教会。萨帕塔于1919年遭伏击身亡，卡兰萨于1920年被杀，比利亚于1923年遇刺。

summary.en: From 9 to 19 February 1913 rebel troops and the federal army fought in central Mexico City, shelling neighbourhoods and killing hundreds of civilians. General Victoriano Huerta, nominally defending the government, betrayed President Madero in a pact brokered at the US embassy; Madero and Vice-President Pino Suárez were murdered on 22 February.
summary.zh: 1913年2月9日至19日，叛军与联邦军队在墨西哥城中心激战，炮击街区，数百名平民丧生。名义上保卫政府的维多里亚诺·韦尔塔将军在美国大使馆斡旋下达成密约，背叛了马德罗总统；2月22日，马德罗和副总统皮诺·苏亚雷斯遇害。

sources.title: Alan Knight, The Mexican Revolution (2 vols., 1986)
Michael C. Meyer, Huerta: A Political Portrait (1972)
Wikipedia: Ten Tragic Days

summary.en: In April 1915 Álvaro Obregón's Constitutionalist army, dug into trenches with barbed wire and machine guns, repelled repeated cavalry charges by Pancho Villa's Division of the North at Celaya, Guanajuato. The defeat broke Villa's power and decided the civil war in Carranza's favour.
summary.zh: 1915年4月，阿尔瓦罗·奥夫雷贡的立宪派军队在瓜纳华托州塞拉亚依托堑壕、铁丝网和机枪，击退了潘乔·比利亚北方师的多次骑兵冲锋。这场失败摧毁了比利亚的力量，使内战局势转向有利于卡兰萨的一方。

sources.title: Friedrich Katz, The Life and Times of Pancho Villa (1998)
Alan Knight, The Mexican Revolution (2 vols., 1986)
Wikipedia: Battle of Celaya

summary.en: After the lynching of President Vilbrun Guillaume Sam in July 1915, US Marines landed at Port-au-Prince and stayed for 19 years. The occupation rewrote Haiti's constitution to allow foreign landownership, revived forced road labour (corvée) and crushed the Caco revolt of Charlemagne Péralte, killing thousands.
summary.zh: 1915年7月总统维尔布伦·纪尧姆·萨姆被私刑处死后，美国海军陆战队在太子港登陆，一驻就是19年。占领当局改写海地宪法，允许外国人拥有土地，恢复强迫修路的徭役制，并镇压了夏尔马涅·佩拉尔特领导的卡科起义，杀死数千人。

sources.title: Hans Schmidt, The United States Occupation of Haiti, 1915–1934 (1971)
Mary A. Renda, Taking Haiti: Military Occupation and the Culture of U.S. Imperialism, 1915–1940 (2001)
Wikipedia: United States occupation of Haiti

story.en:
Haiti had six presidents between 1911 and 1915, each overthrown by armed bands of peasants called cacos. In July 1915 President Vilbrun Guillaume Sam ordered the execution of 167 political prisoners; a mob dragged him from the French legation and tore him apart. The same day US Marines landed, officially to restore order and protect foreigners, and in practice also to secure US banks' control of Haiti's finances and keep Germany out of the Caribbean.

The Americans installed a client president and in 1918 imposed a constitution, reportedly drafted in part by the young Franklin D. Roosevelt, that allowed foreigners to own land for the first time since Dessalines had banned it. To build roads, the Marines revived a colonial-era law of forced labour; peasants were roped together and worked under guard. Charlemagne Péralte led a revolt until he was betrayed and killed in 1919; the Marines photographed his body tied to a door and distributed the image, which made him a martyr.

By the time the Marines left in 1934 they had built roads, hospitals and a new National Guard, but also deepened colour and class divisions, and left an army that would dominate Haitian politics for decades.
story.zh:
1911至1915年间，海地换了六位总统，每一位都被称为“卡科”的农民武装推翻。1915年7月，维尔布伦·纪尧姆·萨姆总统下令处决167名政治犯；愤怒的人群把他从法国公使馆拖出来撕成碎片。同一天，美国海军陆战队登陆，名义上是恢复秩序、保护外国人，实际上也是为了确保美国银行控制海地财政，并把德国挡在加勒比之外。

美国人扶植了一位傀儡总统，并于1918年强行推出一部宪法，据说部分由年轻的富兰克林·罗斯福起草；这部宪法使外国人自德萨林颁布禁令以来首次可以拥有海地土地。为了修路，海军陆战队恢复了一条殖民时期的强迫劳役法，农民被绳子拴成一串，在看守下劳作。夏尔马涅·佩拉尔特领导起义，直到1919年遭人出卖被杀；海军陆战队把他绑在门板上的遗体拍成照片四处散发，反倒使他成为烈士。

1934年海军陆战队撤离时，他们修建了道路、医院和一支新的国民警卫队，但也加深了肤色和阶级的分裂，并留下一支此后数十年主宰海地政治的军队。

summary.en: Drafted by a congress at Querétaro and promulgated on 5 February 1917, Mexico's constitution declared national ownership of land, water and subsoil (Article 27), guaranteed workers' rights including the eight-hour day (Article 123) and imposed strict secular education. It was among the first constitutions to enshrine social rights and remains in force.
summary.zh: 1917年2月5日，由克雷塔罗制宪会议起草的墨西哥宪法颁布。它宣布土地、水和地下资源归国家所有（第27条），保障包括八小时工作制在内的劳工权利（第123条），并推行严格的世俗教育。它是最早载入社会权利的宪法之一，至今仍然有效。

sources.title: Alan Knight, The Mexican Revolution (2 vols., 1986)
Britannica: Constitution of 1917
Wikipedia: Constitution of Mexico

summary.en: When President Plutarco Elías Calles strictly enforced the constitution's anti-clerical articles, Mexico's bishops suspended public worship in 1926 and Catholic peasants of the centre-west rose under the cry "¡Viva Cristo Rey!". About 90,000 combatants died before a settlement brokered by the US ambassador in 1929.
summary.zh: 普卢塔科·埃利亚斯·卡列斯总统严格执行宪法中的反教权条款后，墨西哥主教们于1926年暂停公开礼拜，中西部的天主教农民高呼“基督君王万岁！”起义。至1929年美国大使斡旋达成和解时，双方已有约9万名战斗人员死亡。

sources.title: Jean Meyer, The Cristero Rebellion: The Mexican People between Church and State, 1926–1929 (1976)
Brian R. Hamnett, A Concise History of Mexico (3rd ed., 2019)
Wikipedia: Cristero War

note: Marker at Guadalajara, centre of the Cristero heartland in Jalisco.

name.en: Sandino's war against the US Marines in Nicaragua
name.zh: 桑地诺抗击美国海军陆战队的战争

summary.en: Refusing the 1927 US-brokered peace, the Liberal general Augusto César Sandino led a guerrilla army from the mountains of Nueva Segovia against the Nicaraguan National Guard and the US Marines occupying the country. The Marines withdrew in January 1933; in 1934 Sandino was murdered on the orders of the Guard's commander, Anastasio Somoza García.
summary.zh: 自由派将领奥古斯托·塞萨尔·桑地诺拒绝接受1927年美国斡旋的和约，率领游击队从新塞哥维亚山区出发，对抗尼加拉瓜国民警卫队和占领该国的美国海军陆战队。海军陆战队于1933年1月撤离；1934年，桑地诺遭国民警卫队司令阿纳斯塔西奥·索摩查·加西亚下令杀害。

sources.title: Michael J. Schroeder, The Sandino Rebellion Archive
Neill Macaulay, The Sandino Affair (1967)
Wikipedia: Augusto César Sandino

note: Marker at Ocotal, where the Battle of Ocotal (16 July 1927) saw one of the first coordinated dive-bombing attacks in history.

summary.en: In October 1937 the Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo ordered soldiers and civilian auxiliaries to kill Haitians living in the Dominican borderlands. Over about five days, mostly with machetes, they killed an estimated 12,000 to 20,000 people, reportedly identifying victims by how they pronounced perejil, "parsley".
summary.zh: 1937年10月，多米尼加独裁者拉斐尔·特鲁希略命令士兵和民间帮手杀害居住在多米尼加边境地区的海地人。约五天之内，他们主要用砍刀杀死了约1.2万至2万人；据说他们根据人们如何发“perejil”（香芹）一词的音来辨认受害者。

sources.title: Richard Lee Turits, "A World Destroyed, A Nation Imposed: The 1937 Haitian Massacre in the Dominican Republic", Hispanic American Historical Review 82 (2002)
Edwidge Danticat, The Farming of Bones (1998), a novel based on survivor testimony
Wikipedia: Parsley massacre

note: Death toll estimates vary from under 1,000 (Dominican government) to over 20,000; marker at Dajabón on the Massacre River.

story.en:
The border between the Dominican Republic and Haiti had long been porous. In the northern valleys Haitian and Dominican peasants farmed side by side, married each other and spoke both Spanish and Kreyòl. Rafael Trujillo, dictator since 1930, wanted to "Dominicanise" the frontier. On 2 October 1937, at a dance in Dajabón, he declared that the Haitian "occupation" would be ended.

Over the following days soldiers, many in plain clothes so that the army could deny involvement, went from house to house. They used machetes and clubs rather than guns, to make the killings look like the work of farmers. Survivors later told the story that victims were made to say perejil; those who could not roll the Spanish r were killed. Historians such as Richard Turits note that the soldiers also simply targeted anyone known to be Haitian. Thousands fled across the river, whose name, Massacre River, dated from an earlier colonial killing.

Under international pressure Trujillo agreed in 1938 to pay Haiti 750,000 dollars, of which only a fraction was paid. The massacre became the foundation of a state-sponsored anti-Haitian ideology that still marks relations on the island.
story.zh:
多米尼加共和国与海地之间的边界长期以来来往自由。在北部河谷，海地和多米尼加农民比邻而耕、相互通婚，既讲西班牙语也讲海地克里奥尔语。1930年起实行独裁的拉斐尔·特鲁希略想要使边境“多米尼加化”。1937年10月2日，他在达哈博恩的一场舞会上宣布，要结束海地人的“占领”。

此后数日，士兵们挨家挨户搜杀，许多人身着便装，以便军队推卸责任。他们用砍刀和棍棒而不用枪，好让杀戮看起来像农民所为。幸存者后来讲述，受害者被要求说出“perejil”，发不好西班牙语颤音r的人便被杀死。理查德·图里茨等史学家指出，士兵们也直接针对任何已知是海地人的人。数千人渡河逃亡；这条河叫“屠杀河”，其名源于更早的一次殖民时期杀戮。

在国际压力下，特鲁希略于1938年同意向海地赔偿75万美元，实际只付了一小部分。这次屠杀奠定了一种由国家推动的反海地意识形态，至今仍影响着岛上两国的关系。

summary.en: On 18 March 1938, after British and American oil companies defied a Supreme Court ruling in a labour dispute, President Lázaro Cárdenas nationalised the oil industry under Article 27 of the constitution. Mexicans of all classes donated money, jewellery and even chickens toward compensation, and the state company Pemex was founded in June.
summary.zh: 1938年3月18日，英美石油公司拒不执行最高法院在一场劳资纠纷中的裁决，拉萨罗·卡德纳斯总统随即依据宪法第27条将石油工业收归国有。各阶层墨西哥人纷纷捐出钱款、首饰甚至鸡只以凑集赔偿金，国营墨西哥石油公司于同年6月成立。

sources.title: Lorenzo Meyer, Mexico and the United States in the Oil Controversy, 1917–1942 (1977)
Britannica: Lázaro Cárdenas
Wikipedia: Mexican oil expropriation

story.en:
Mexico had been one of the world's great oil producers since the 1910s, but the wells around Tampico and the Gulf Coast belonged to foreign companies such as Royal Dutch Shell's Mexican Eagle and Standard Oil. In 1937 the oil workers' union struck for higher pay; an arbitration board and then the Supreme Court ruled in its favour, and the companies refused to comply.

On the night of 18 March 1938 Lázaro Cárdenas went on national radio and announced that the properties of seventeen companies were expropriated. The reaction was a patriotic outpouring. Crowds of perhaps 200,000 marched in Mexico City; women queued at the Palace of Fine Arts to hand in wedding rings, peasants brought livestock, and the Church supported the government, a rare moment of unity after the Cristero War.

Britain broke off relations and the companies organised a boycott, but with the Second World War approaching, the Roosevelt administration chose to negotiate, and compensation was agreed in 1942. 18 March is celebrated as a national day, and Pemex became a symbol of Mexican sovereignty.
story.zh:
自1910年代起，墨西哥就是世界主要产油国之一，但坦皮科和墨西哥湾沿岸的油井属于外国公司，如荷兰皇家壳牌旗下的墨西哥之鹰公司和标准石油公司。1937年，石油工人工会罢工要求加薪；仲裁委员会和最高法院先后作出有利于工会的裁决，石油公司拒不执行。

1938年3月18日夜，拉萨罗·卡德纳斯通过全国广播宣布征收十七家公司的财产。随之而来的是爱国热潮。墨西哥城或有20万人上街游行；妇女在美术宫前排队捐出结婚戒指，农民送来牲畜，教会也支持政府，这是基督战争之后难得的团结时刻。

英国与墨西哥断交，石油公司组织抵制，但随着第二次世界大战临近，罗斯福政府选择谈判，双方于1942年就赔偿达成协议。3月18日被定为全国纪念日，墨西哥石油公司成为墨西哥主权的象征。

summary.en: A CIA operation (PBSuccess) backed an invasion from Honduras by Carlos Castillo Armas and a campaign of radio propaganda and air raids that forced the elected president Jacobo Árbenz, whose land reform had expropriated uncultivated lands of the United Fruit Company, to resign on 27 June 1954. Decades of military rule followed.
summary.zh: 美国中央情报局的“成功行动”支持卡洛斯·卡斯蒂略·阿马斯从洪都拉斯入侵，并辅以电台宣传和空袭，迫使民选总统哈科沃·阿本斯于1954年6月27日辞职；阿本斯的土地改革曾征收联合果品公司闲置的土地。此后危地马拉经历了数十年军人统治。

sources.title: Piero Gleijeses, Shattered Hope: The Guatemalan Revolution and the United States, 1944–1954 (1991)
Nick Cullather, Secret History: The CIA's Classified Account of Its Operations in Guatemala, 1952–1954 (1999)
US Department of State, Foreign Relations of the United States, 1952–1954, Guatemala (2003)
Wikipedia: 1954 Guatemalan coup d'état

story.en:
Guatemala's "ten years of spring" began with a revolution in 1944 that ended the dictatorship of Jorge Ubico. In 1950 Colonel Jacobo Árbenz was elected president. His Decree 900 of 1952 expropriated uncultivated land on large estates, with compensation based on declared tax values, and gave it to some 100,000 peasant families. The largest landowner was the US-based United Fruit Company, which held vast reserves of idle land and had close ties to the Eisenhower administration.

Washington, already alarmed by communists in Árbenz's coalition, approved a covert operation. In June 1954 Castillo Armas crossed from Honduras with a few hundred men, while CIA pilots bombed Guatemala City and a clandestine radio station broadcast reports of a huge invading army. The rebel force was militarily weak, but the army refused to fight. Árbenz resigned on 27 June and went into exile, searched at the airport in his underwear before departure.

The new regime reversed the land reform and outlawed opposition. Among those who witnessed the coup was a young Argentine doctor, Ernesto Guevara, who concluded that revolutions must destroy the old army, a lesson he carried to Cuba.
story.zh:
危地马拉“十年之春”始于1944年终结豪尔赫·乌维科独裁的革命。1950年，哈科沃·阿本斯上校当选总统。他在1952年颁布的第900号法令征收大庄园中的闲置土地，按申报的纳税价值给予补偿，并分给约10万户农民家庭。最大的土地所有者是总部在美国的联合果品公司，它拥有大片闲置土地，与艾森豪威尔政府关系密切。

早已对阿本斯执政联盟中的共产党人心怀警惕的华盛顿批准了一项秘密行动。1954年6月，卡斯蒂略·阿马斯率数百人从洪都拉斯越境，中情局飞行员轰炸危地马拉城，一个秘密电台则不断播报一支庞大入侵军正在逼近的消息。叛军在军事上不堪一击，但危地马拉军队拒绝作战。阿本斯于6月27日辞职流亡，离境前在机场被搜身，仅剩内衣。

新政权废除了土地改革，取缔反对派。目睹这场政变的人中有一位年轻的阿根廷医生埃内斯托·格瓦拉，他由此得出结论：革命必须摧毁旧军队。他把这一教训带到了古巴。

summary.en: Beginning with Fidel Castro's failed attack on the Moncada barracks in 1953, the 26th of July Movement waged guerrilla war from the Sierra Maestra after landing from the yacht Granma in 1956. Dictator Fulgencio Batista fled on 1 January 1959, and the revolutionary government soon aligned Cuba with the Soviet Union.
summary.zh: 古巴革命始于1953年菲德尔·卡斯特罗攻打蒙卡达兵营的失败之举。1956年“格拉玛”号游艇登陆后，“七·二六运动”以马埃斯特腊山为根据地开展游击战。1959年1月1日独裁者富尔亨西奥·巴蒂斯塔出逃，革命政府随后使古巴倒向苏联。

sources.title: Hugh Thomas, Cuba: The Pursuit of Freedom (1971; updated 1998)
Louis A. Pérez Jr., Cuba: Between Reform and Revolution (5th ed., 2015)
Samuel Farber, The Origins of the Cuban Revolution Reconsidered (2006)
Wikipedia: Cuban Revolution

story.en:
On 26 July 1953 Fidel Castro, a 26-year-old lawyer, led about 160 young men in an attack on the Moncada barracks in Santiago de Cuba, hoping to spark a rising against Fulgencio Batista, who had seized power in a coup the year before. It failed disastrously; many captured rebels were tortured and killed. At his trial Castro ended his defence with the words "Condemn me, it does not matter. History will absolve me."

Amnestied in 1955, he went to Mexico, where he met Ernesto "Che" Guevara. In late November 1956, 82 men crammed onto the leaky yacht Granma and sailed for Cuba. They landed two days late, in a mangrove swamp, on 2 December, and were scattered by the army within days; perhaps twenty survivors regrouped in the Sierra Maestra. With peasant support, urban underground networks and a press that made them famous, the guerrillas grew, and in summer 1958 they defeated Batista's offensive.

In late December Guevara's column derailed an armoured train and took Santa Clara. On New Year's Eve Batista fled to the Dominican Republic. Castro's week-long "caravan of liberty" across the island ended in Havana on 8 January 1959, when, as he spoke, a white dove landed on his shoulder.
story.zh:
1953年7月26日，26岁的律师菲德尔·卡斯特罗率领约160名青年进攻圣地亚哥-德古巴的蒙卡达兵营，希望由此点燃反抗富尔亨西奥·巴蒂斯塔的起义；巴蒂斯塔在前一年通过政变夺取了政权。行动惨败，许多被俘的起义者遭酷刑折磨致死。卡斯特罗在受审时以这样一句话结束辩护：“判我的罪吧，这没有关系。历史将宣判我无罪。”

1955年获大赦后，他前往墨西哥，在那里结识了埃内斯托·“切”·格瓦拉。1956年11月底，82人挤上漏水的“格拉玛”号游艇驶向古巴。他们晚了两天才于12月2日在一片红树林沼泽登陆，几天之内就被政府军打散，大约二十名幸存者在马埃斯特腊山重新集结。依靠农民的支持、城市地下网络，以及使他们声名远扬的报刊，游击队不断壮大，并在1958年夏天粉碎了巴蒂斯塔的攻势。

12月下旬，格瓦拉的纵队使一列装甲列车出轨，攻克圣克拉拉。除夕夜，巴蒂斯塔逃往多米尼加共和国。卡斯特罗横贯全岛、历时一周的“自由大篷车”于1959年1月8日抵达哈瓦那；他演讲时，一只白鸽落在了他的肩上。

summary.en: On 17 April 1961 about 1,400 CIA-trained Cuban exiles of Brigade 2506 landed at the Bay of Pigs (Playa Girón). Without the expected uprising or US air cover, they were defeated within three days; some 1,100 were captured and later ransomed for food and medicine. The fiasco strengthened Castro, who had declared the revolution socialist the day before.
summary.zh: 1961年4月17日，约1400名由美国中央情报局训练的古巴流亡者组成的2506旅在猪湾（吉隆滩）登陆。由于预期中的起义和美国空中掩护都没有出现，他们在三天内被击败，约1100人被俘，后以食品和药品赎回。这场惨败巩固了卡斯特罗的地位，他在前一天宣布了革命的社会主义性质。

sources.title: Peter Kornbluh (ed.), Bay of Pigs Declassified: The Secret CIA Report on the Invasion of Cuba (1998)
Hugh Thomas, Cuba: The Pursuit of Freedom (1971; updated 1998)
Wikipedia: Bay of Pigs Invasion

summary.en: In October 1962 US reconnaissance flights revealed Soviet nuclear missile sites being built in western Cuba. For thirteen days President Kennedy imposed a naval "quarantine" and the world faced the threat of nuclear war, until Khrushchev agreed on 28 October to withdraw the missiles in exchange for a US pledge not to invade Cuba and a secret removal of US missiles from Turkey.
summary.zh: 1962年10月，美国侦察机发现苏联正在古巴西部修建核导弹发射场。在十三天里，肯尼迪总统实施海上“隔离”，世界面临核战争的威胁，直到10月28日赫鲁晓夫同意撤走导弹，换取美国不入侵古巴的保证，以及秘密撤除部署在土耳其的美国导弹。

sources.title: Aleksandr Fursenko & Timothy Naftali, "One Hell of a Gamble": Khrushchev, Castro, and Kennedy, 1958–1964 (1997)
Sergo Mikoyan, The Soviet Cuban Missile Crisis (2012)
Britannica: Cuban missile crisis
Wikipedia: Cuban Missile Crisis

note: Marker at the San Cristóbal missile sites in Pinar del Río province, photographed by a U-2 on 14 October 1962.

story.en:
Nikita Khrushchev decided in the spring of 1962 to send to Cuba some 40,000 Soviet troops and medium- and intermediate-range nuclear missiles, to protect his new ally after the Bay of Pigs and to offset America's lead in long-range weapons. On 14 October a U-2 spy plane photographed launch sites near San Cristóbal. Kennedy and his advisers debated an air strike and invasion, and on 22 October he announced a naval quarantine of Cuba.

The most dangerous day was 27 October. A Soviet surface-to-air missile shot down a U-2 over eastern Cuba, killing its pilot, Major Rudolf Anderson. In the Sargasso Sea, US destroyers dropped practice depth charges on a Soviet submarine whose officers, out of contact with Moscow, reportedly considered firing a nuclear torpedo. In Havana, Castro wrote to Khrushchev urging him to strike first if the Americans invaded.

That night Robert Kennedy met the Soviet ambassador and offered a deal. On the morning of 28 October Radio Moscow announced that the missiles would be removed. Castro, who learned of the agreement from the radio, was furious at not being consulted. The crisis led to the Moscow–Washington hotline and the Partial Test Ban Treaty of 1963.
story.zh:
1962年春，尼基塔·赫鲁晓夫决定向古巴派遣约4万名苏军和中程、中远程核导弹，以便在猪湾事件后保护这个新盟友，并抵消美国在远程武器上的优势。10月14日，一架U-2侦察机在圣克里斯托瓦尔附近拍到了发射场。肯尼迪和顾问们讨论了空袭和入侵方案，10月22日他宣布对古巴实施海上隔离。

最危险的一天是10月27日。一枚苏联地对空导弹在古巴东部上空击落一架U-2，飞行员鲁道夫·安德森少校身亡。在马尾藻海，美国驱逐舰向一艘苏联潜艇投下练习深水炸弹；据称，与莫斯科失去联系的艇上军官曾考虑发射一枚核鱼雷。在哈瓦那，卡斯特罗写信给赫鲁晓夫，敦促他在美国入侵时先发制人。

当晚，罗伯特·肯尼迪会见苏联大使，提出了一项交易。10月28日上午，莫斯科广播电台宣布将撤走导弹。卡斯特罗是从广播中得知这项协议的，他因未被征求意见而怒不可遏。这场危机促成了莫斯科与华盛顿之间的热线，以及1963年的《部分禁止核试验条约》。

summary.en: A 36-year conflict between leftist guerrillas and US-backed military governments killed or "disappeared" some 200,000 people. The UN-sponsored truth commission found that state forces committed 93% of the violations and, in the early 1980s, acts of genocide against Maya communities such as the Ixil. Peace accords were signed in December 1996.
summary.zh: 左翼游击队与美国支持的军政府之间长达36年的冲突，造成约20万人被杀害或“失踪”。联合国支持的真相委员会认定，93%的侵权行为由国家力量所为，并且在20世纪80年代初对伊希尔等玛雅社群犯下了种族灭绝行为。和平协定于1996年12月签署。

sources.title: Commission for Historical Clarification (CEH), Guatemala: Memory of Silence (1999)
Greg Grandin, The Last Colonial Massacre: Latin America in the Cold War (2004)
Wikipedia: Guatemalan Civil War

note: Marker at Nebaj in the Ixil region, the area worst affected by the scorched-earth campaigns of 1981–1983. Wikidata dates the war from 1965; it is conventionally counted from the officers' revolt of 13 November 1960.

story.en:
The war grew out of the 1954 coup. In November 1960 young army officers revolted against the government; some fled to the hills and founded guerrilla movements. Through the 1960s and 1970s death squads killed students, union leaders and priests, while guerrillas increasingly recruited among the Maya peasants of the western highlands.

The worst came in 1981–1983, under Generals Romeo Lucas García and Efraín Ríos Montt. The army destroyed some 440 villages in "scorched earth" campaigns, massacring men, women and children it accused of supporting the guerrillas, and forced survivors into "model villages" and civil patrols. In 1980 security forces stormed the Spanish embassy, which peasant activists had occupied, and 37 people died in the fire, among them Vicente Menchú, father of the future Nobel laureate.

The peace accords of 29 December 1996 ended the fighting. The truth commission's 1999 report, "Memory of Silence", concluded that the state had committed genocide against Maya groups. In 2013 Ríos Montt was convicted of genocide by a Guatemalan court, the first former head of state tried for genocide in his own country, though the verdict was annulled on procedural grounds.
story.zh:
这场战争源于1954年政变。1960年11月，年轻军官发动兵变反对政府，部分人逃入山区，建立了游击运动。整个20世纪六七十年代，暗杀队杀害学生、工会领袖和神父，游击队则越来越多地在西部高地的玛雅农民中招募人员。

最惨烈的时期是1981至1983年间罗密欧·卢卡斯·加西亚和埃弗拉因·里奥斯·蒙特两位将军执政时。军队在“焦土”行动中摧毁约440个村庄，屠杀被指控支持游击队的男女老少，并把幸存者赶进“模范村”、编入民防巡逻队。1980年，安全部队强攻被农民活动人士占领的西班牙大使馆，37人在大火中丧生，其中包括后来的诺贝尔奖得主之父维森特·门楚。

1996年12月29日签署的和平协定结束了战火。真相委员会1999年发表的报告《沉默的记忆》断定，国家对玛雅族群犯下了种族灭绝罪。2013年，危地马拉法院以种族灭绝罪判处里奥斯·蒙特有罪，他是第一位在本国因种族灭绝罪受审的前国家元首，但判决后来因程序问题被撤销。

summary.en: On 2 October 1968, ten days before the Mexico City Olympics opened, army and secret police units opened fire on a student rally in the Plaza of the Three Cultures at Tlatelolco. The government admitted to a few dozen deaths; later investigations suggest at least 44 and possibly several hundred were killed.
summary.zh: 1968年10月2日，墨西哥城奥运会开幕前十天，军队和秘密警察部队向在特拉特洛尔科三文化广场集会的学生开枪。政府只承认数十人死亡；后来的调查表明，至少44人、可能数百人遇难。

sources.title: Elena Poniatowska, La noche de Tlatelolco (1971; Eng. Massacre in Mexico, 1975)
National Security Archive: The Tlatelolco Massacre: U.S. Documents on Mexico and the Events of 1968
Wikipedia: Tlatelolco massacre

note: The death toll is still disputed.

story.en:
Through the summer of 1968 Mexico's student movement grew from a street brawl into the largest challenge in decades to the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which had ruled since 1929. Hundreds of thousands marched for the release of political prisoners and an end to police brutality. President Gustavo Díaz Ordaz, determined that nothing would spoil the first Olympic Games held in Latin America, sent the army into the National University in September.

On the evening of 2 October some 10,000 people gathered in the Plaza of the Three Cultures, among Aztec ruins, a colonial church and modern apartment blocks. Flares fell from a helicopter; snipers of the Olympia Battalion, wearing a white glove on the left hand to recognise each other, fired from the buildings, and the soldiers surrounding the square fired into the crowd. Hundreds were arrested and the bodies removed overnight.

The Games opened on 12 October as planned and are remembered for Bob Beamon's long jump and the raised fists of Tommie Smith and John Carlos. Elena Poniatowska's oral history La noche de Tlatelolco kept the memory alive, and "2 de octubre no se olvida" (2 October is not forgotten) is still chanted each year.
story.zh:
1968年整个夏天，墨西哥学生运动从一场街头斗殴发展为数十年来对自1929年起执政的革命制度党最大的挑战。数十万人游行，要求释放政治犯、停止警察暴行。古斯塔沃·迪亚斯·奥尔达斯总统决意不让任何事情破坏在拉丁美洲举办的首届奥运会，9月派军队进驻国立大学。

10月2日傍晚，约1万人聚集在三文化广场，四周是阿兹特克遗址、殖民时期的教堂和现代公寓楼。直升机投下照明弹；左手戴白手套以便相互识别的“奥林匹亚营”狙击手从楼上开枪，包围广场的士兵也向人群射击。数百人被捕，尸体在夜里被运走。

奥运会于10月12日如期开幕，人们记住的是鲍勃·比蒙的跳远和汤米·史密斯、约翰·卡洛斯高举的拳头。埃莱娜·波尼亚托夫斯卡的口述史《特拉特洛尔科之夜》延续了人们的记忆，“10月2日不会被遗忘”的口号至今每年都会响起。

summary.en: The XIX Olympiad, held from 12 to 27 October 1968, was the first Olympics in Latin America and the first held at high altitude (2,240 m), which helped Bob Beamon's 8.90 m long jump. Tommie Smith and John Carlos raised black-gloved fists on the podium; Enriqueta Basilio became the first woman to light an Olympic cauldron.
summary.zh: 第十九届奥运会于1968年10月12日至27日举行，是首次在拉丁美洲、也是首次在高海拔地区（2240米）举办的奥运会，高海拔帮助鲍勃·比蒙跳出8.90米的跳远成绩。汤米·史密斯和约翰·卡洛斯在领奖台上高举戴黑手套的拳头；恩里克塔·巴西利奥成为首位点燃奥运圣火的女性。

sources.title: International Olympic Committee: Mexico City 1968
Kevin B. Witherspoon, Before the Eyes of the World: Mexico and the 1968 Olympic Games (2008)
Wikipedia: 1968 Summer Olympics

summary.en: Shortly after midnight on 23 December 1972 a magnitude 6.2 earthquake directly beneath Managua destroyed much of the Nicaraguan capital and killed some 10,000 people. The dictator Anastasio Somoza Debayle's family and the National Guard diverted much of the international aid, turning business elites as well as the poor against the regime.
summary.zh: 1972年12月23日午夜刚过，马那瓜城正下方发生6.2级地震，尼加拉瓜首都大部被毁，约1万人丧生。独裁者阿纳斯塔西奥·索摩查·德瓦伊莱的家族和国民警卫队侵吞了大量国际援助，使工商精英和穷人一样转而反对这个政权。

sources.title: US Geological Survey: Managua, Nicaragua earthquake of December 23, 1972
Thomas W. Walker, Nicaragua: Living in the Shadow of the Eagle (5th ed., 2011)
Wikipedia: 1972 Nicaragua earthquake

note: Death toll estimates range from about 4,000 to 11,000.

name.en: Torrijos–Carter Treaties and the handover of the Panama Canal
name.zh: 《托里霍斯-卡特条约》与巴拿马运河的移交

summary.en: Signed on 7 September 1977 by US President Jimmy Carter and Panama's leader Omar Torrijos, the treaties abolished the Canal Zone and provided for the canal's transfer to Panama, which took place at noon on 31 December 1999, while guaranteeing its permanent neutrality.
summary.zh: 1977年9月7日，美国总统吉米·卡特与巴拿马领导人奥马尔·托里霍斯签署条约，废除运河区，规定把运河移交巴拿马，同时保证运河永久中立。移交于1999年12月31日正午完成。

sources.title: Michael L. Conniff, Panama and the United States: The End of the Alliance (3rd ed., 2012)
Office of the Historian, US State Department: The Panama Canal and the Torrijos–Carter Treaties
Wikipedia: Torrijos–Carter Treaties

summary.en: After the 1978 murder of the opposition editor Pedro Joaquín Chamorro, a national uprising led by the Sandinista National Liberation Front (FSLN) overthrew Anastasio Somoza Debayle on 19 July 1979, ending 43 years of Somoza rule. The Sandinista government then fought the US-backed Contras until elections in 1990 brought Violeta Chamorro to power.
summary.zh: 1978年反对派报人佩德罗·华金·查莫罗遇害后，以桑地诺民族解放阵线为首的全国起义于1979年7月19日推翻阿纳斯塔西奥·索摩查·德瓦伊莱，结束了索摩查家族43年的统治。此后桑地诺政府与美国支持的反政府武装作战，直到1990年大选使比奥莱塔·查莫罗上台。

sources.title: Thomas W. Walker, Nicaragua: Living in the Shadow of the Eagle (5th ed., 2011)
Matilde Zimmermann, Sandinista: Carlos Fonseca and the Nicaraguan Revolution (2000)
Wikipedia: Nicaraguan Revolution

story.en:
The Sandinista National Liberation Front, founded in 1961 by Carlos Fonseca and others, named itself after Augusto Sandino, the guerrilla murdered by the first Somoza in 1934. For years it was a small band in the mountains. The Managua earthquake of 1972, and the regime's theft of relief aid, changed the mood. On 10 January 1978 gunmen killed Pedro Joaquín Chamorro, editor of La Prensa and the country's best-known opposition voice; tens of thousands marched at his funeral and businesses went on strike.

In August 1978 a Sandinista commando led by Edén Pastora, "Commander Zero", seized the National Palace with the Congress inside and won the release of political prisoners. Spontaneous risings broke out in Masaya, León and Estelí, and the Guard bombed its own cities. The final offensive began in June 1979; after the National Guard killed the American TV journalist Bill Stewart on camera, the United States withdrew support. Somoza fled to Miami on 17 July, and on 19 July the guerrillas entered Managua.

The revolution's literacy crusade and land reform drew wide admiration, but the Reagan administration funded the Contra rebels, and a war costing some 30,000 lives followed. In 1990 the Sandinistas lost the election and handed over power peacefully; their leader Daniel Ortega returned to the presidency in 2007.
story.zh:
桑地诺民族解放阵线由卡洛斯·丰塞卡等人创建于1961年，以1934年被第一代索摩查杀害的游击队领袖奥古斯托·桑地诺命名。多年来它只是山中的一支小队伍。1972年的马那瓜地震以及政权对救灾援助的侵吞改变了民心。1978年1月10日，枪手杀死了《新闻报》主编、全国最著名的反对派人士佩德罗·华金·查莫罗；数万人为他送葬游行，商界举行罢工。

1978年8月，由“零号司令”埃登·帕斯托拉率领的桑地诺突击队占领了正在开会的国会所在的国家宫，迫使当局释放政治犯。马萨亚、莱昂和埃斯特利相继爆发自发起义，国民警卫队竟轰炸本国城市。1979年6月发动最后攻势；国民警卫队在镜头前杀害美国电视记者比尔·斯图尔特之后，美国撤回了支持。7月17日索摩查逃往迈阿密，7月19日游击队进入马那瓜。

革命的扫盲运动和土地改革赢得了广泛赞誉，但里根政府资助反政府武装，随之而来的战争夺去约3万人的生命。1990年桑地诺阵线在大选中落败，和平交出政权；其领导人丹尼尔·奥尔特加于2007年重新出任总统。

summary.en: The war between El Salvador's US-backed military government and the guerrillas of the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front (FMLN) killed about 75,000 people, most of them civilians killed by state forces and death squads, including about 800 people in the El Mozote massacre of 1981. The Chapultepec Peace Accords of January 1992 ended it.
summary.zh: 萨尔瓦多由美国支持的军政府与法拉本多·马蒂民族解放阵线游击队之间的战争造成约7.5万人死亡，其中大多数是被国家力量和暗杀队杀害的平民，包括1981年莫索特大屠杀中的约800人。1992年1月的《查普尔特佩克和平协定》结束了这场战争。

sources.title: UN Commission on the Truth for El Salvador, From Madness to Hope: The 12-Year War in El Salvador (1993)
Mark Danner, The Massacre at El Mozote (1994)
Wikipedia: Salvadoran Civil War

summary.en: On 24 March 1980 Archbishop Óscar Romero of San Salvador, who had used his Sunday sermons to denounce killings by the army and death squads, was shot dead by a sniper while celebrating Mass in the chapel of the Divine Providence cancer hospital. He was canonised by Pope Francis in 2018.
summary.zh: 1980年3月24日，圣萨尔瓦多大主教奥斯卡·罗梅罗在神圣天意癌症医院的小教堂主持弥撒时被狙击手射杀。他曾利用主日讲道谴责军队和暗杀队的杀戮。2018年，教宗方济各册封他为圣人。

sources.title: UN Commission on the Truth for El Salvador, From Madness to Hope (1993), section on the Romero case
James R. Brockman, Romero: A Life (1989)
Wikipedia: Óscar Romero

story.en:
Óscar Arnulfo Romero was chosen archbishop in February 1977 partly because he was thought cautious and conservative. Three weeks later his friend, the Jesuit Rutilio Grande, was machine-gunned on a country road for organising peasants. Romero refused to attend state ceremonies until the killing was investigated, and over the next three years his Sunday homilies, broadcast on the archdiocese's radio station, became the country's most listened-to programme: he read out each week the names of the murdered and disappeared.

On 23 March 1980 he addressed the soldiers directly, telling them that no one was bound to obey an order against the law of God, and in the name of the suffering people he begged, then ordered them to stop the repression. The next evening, as he finished his homily in the small hospital chapel where he lived, a single shot from a car outside struck him in the heart.

At his funeral a bomb and gunfire caused panic in which dozens died. The UN Truth Commission found that the death-squad leader Roberto D'Aubuisson had ordered the killing. Pope Francis declared Romero a martyr and in October 2018 a saint.
story.zh:
奥斯卡·阿努尔福·罗梅罗于1977年2月被选为大主教，部分原因是人们认为他谨慎保守。三周后，他的朋友、耶稣会士鲁蒂利奥·格兰德因组织农民而在乡间公路上被机枪射杀。罗梅罗在案件查明前拒绝出席国家典礼。此后三年，他通过总教区电台播出的主日讲道成为全国收听人数最多的节目：他每周都宣读被杀害者和失踪者的名字。

1980年3月23日，他直接向士兵们喊话，告诉他们没有人必须服从违背上帝律法的命令，并以受苦人民的名义恳求、继而命令他们停止镇压。第二天傍晚，他在自己居住的医院小教堂里结束讲道时，门外一辆汽车里射出的一颗子弹击中了他的心脏。

他的葬礼上发生爆炸和枪击，引发的混乱造成数十人死亡。联合国真相委员会认定，暗杀队头目罗伯托·多布伊松下令实施了这次暗杀。教宗方济各宣布罗梅罗为殉道者，并于2018年10月封他为圣人。

summary.en: At 7:17 a.m. on 19 September 1985 a magnitude 8.0 earthquake off the Pacific coast of Michoacán shook Mexico City, 350 km away, where the soft clay of the old lake bed amplified the waves. Hundreds of buildings collapsed and at least 5,000, perhaps 10,000 or more, people died. Citizen rescue brigades outpaced the government.
summary.zh: 1985年9月19日上午7时17分，米却肯州太平洋沿岸外海发生8.0级地震，震动了350公里外的墨西哥城；古湖床的软黏土放大了地震波。数百栋建筑倒塌，至少5000人、或许1万人以上丧生。市民自发组织的救援队比政府行动得更快。

sources.title: US Geological Survey: The Mexico Earthquake of September 19, 1985 (Earthquake Spectra 4:3, 1988)
Elena Poniatowska, Nada, nadie: las voces del temblor (1988)
Wikipedia: 1985 Mexico City earthquake

note: The official death toll is about 5,000; other estimates reach 10,000–40,000. Marker at Mexico City, where nearly all deaths occurred; the epicentre was off the Michoacán coast.

story.en:
The quake struck as Mexico City was starting its working day. Its epicentre lay off the coast, but the capital is built on the drained bed of Lake Texcoco, and the waterlogged clay shook like jelly at the very frequency that made mid-rise buildings of six to fifteen storeys resonate. Within two minutes the Nuevo León tower in Tlatelolco, the Juárez hospital, the Televisa building and garment factories in San Antonio Abad, where seamstresses were trapped inside, had collapsed.

The government of Miguel de la Madrid at first refused foreign aid and seemed paralysed. Ordinary people moved first: neighbours dug with their hands, and volunteers who tunnelled into the ruins became known as los topos, "the moles", now a famous rescue brigade. Newborn babies were pulled alive from the ruins of the Juárez hospital up to a week later.

The disaster exposed shoddy construction and corruption and gave birth to new civic organisations, from the seamstresses' union to neighbourhood associations, that helped erode the PRI's one-party rule. Mexico City built a seismic early-warning system. On 19 September 2017, the anniversary, another earthquake struck, hours after a national drill.
story.zh:
地震发生时，墨西哥城刚刚开始一天的工作。震中在外海，但首都建在排干的特斯科科湖床之上，饱含水分的黏土像果冻一样晃动，其频率恰好使六至十五层的中高层建筑发生共振。两分钟内，特拉特洛尔科的新莱昂大楼、华雷斯医院、特莱维萨电视台大楼以及圣安东尼奥·阿瓦德的制衣厂相继倒塌，制衣女工被困其中。

米格尔·德拉马德里政府起初拒绝外国援助，显得手足无措。普通人率先行动：邻居们徒手挖掘，钻进废墟的志愿者被称为“鼹鼠”，后来成为著名的救援队。直到一周之后，仍有新生婴儿从华雷斯医院的废墟中被救出。

这场灾难暴露了建筑质量低劣和腐败问题，催生了从制衣女工工会到街区协会的新公民组织，它们推动削弱了革命制度党的一党统治。墨西哥城建立了地震预警系统。2017年9月19日，在地震纪念日当天，全国演习结束几小时后，又一场地震袭来。

summary.en: On 20 December 1989 about 27,000 US troops invaded Panama (Operation Just Cause) to remove General Manuel Noriega, a former CIA asset indicted in the US for drug trafficking. Noriega took refuge in the Vatican embassy and surrendered on 3 January 1990. Hundreds of Panamanians, many civilians in the El Chorrillo district, were killed.
summary.zh: 1989年12月20日，约2.7万名美军入侵巴拿马（“正义事业行动”），以推翻曾为中情局线人、在美国被控贩毒的曼努埃尔·诺列加将军。诺列加躲进梵蒂冈使馆，于1990年1月3日投降。数百名巴拿马人丧生，其中许多是埃尔乔里约区的平民。

sources.title: Lawrence A. Yates, The U.S. Military Intervention in Panama: Operation Just Cause (2014)
Michael L. Conniff, Panama and the United States: The End of the Alliance (3rd ed., 2012)
Wikipedia: United States invasion of Panama

note: Panamanian death toll estimates range from about 300 to several thousand.

summary.en: In 1952 the Soviet scholar Yuri Knorozov argued that Maya hieroglyphs were partly phonetic, reading Landa's "alphabet" as a syllabary. In 1960 Tatiana Proskouriakoff showed that the inscriptions recorded the lives of real kings. At the first Palenque Round Table in 1973 scholars reconstructed Palenque's dynasty, opening the way to reading Maya history.
summary.zh: 1952年，苏联学者尤里·克诺罗佐夫提出玛雅象形文字部分为表音文字，并把兰达的“字母表”解读为音节表。1960年，塔季扬娜·普罗斯库里亚科夫证明铭文记载的是真实国王的生平。1973年在首届帕伦克圆桌会议上，学者们复原了帕伦克的王朝世系，由此开启了阅读玛雅历史之路。

sources.title: Michael D. Coe, Breaking the Maya Code (rev. ed., 1999)
Tatiana Proskouriakoff, "Historical Implications of a Pattern of Dates at Piedras Negras, Guatemala", American Antiquity 25 (1960)
Stephen Houston, Oswaldo Chinchilla Mazariegos & David Stuart (eds.), The Decipherment of Ancient Maya Writing (2001)

note: Marker at Palenque, site of the 1973 Mesa Redonda.

story.en:
For a century after Förstemann cracked the Maya numbers, the leading Mayanist, Eric Thompson, insisted that the glyphs were symbols of calendar and ritual that could never be "read" as language. The breakthrough came from an unlikely place. Yuri Knorozov, a young Soviet linguist who, legend has it, had picked up a book on Maya codices in the burning Berlin library in 1945, published a paper in 1952 arguing that Landa's 16th-century "alphabet" was a list of syllables: Landa's informant had written the sounds of the Spanish letter names. Cold War politics and Thompson's scorn kept his ideas marginal for years.

In 1960 Tatiana Proskouriakoff, an architect by training working in Washington, noticed that the stelae of Piedras Negras fell into groups each spanning a human lifetime, with a birth date, an accession date and death. The monuments were histories of kings.

In December 1973 a small group, including the artist Linda Schele, the linguist Floyd Lounsbury and the student Peter Mathews, met at Palenque. In one afternoon they worked out the dynasty of Pakal and his successors, two centuries of kings with names and dates. Today about 90 per cent of Classic Maya texts can be read.
story.zh:
在弗斯特曼破解玛雅数字之后的一百年里，首屈一指的玛雅学家埃里克·汤普森坚持认为，这些字符是历法和仪式的符号，永远无法作为语言来“阅读”。突破来自一个意想不到的地方。尤里·克诺罗佐夫是一位年轻的苏联语言学家，传说他于1945年在燃烧的柏林图书馆里捡到一本关于玛雅手抄本的书。1952年他发表论文，认为兰达在16世纪记录的“字母表”其实是一份音节表：兰达的报告人写下的是西班牙语字母名称的读音。冷战政治和汤普森的轻蔑使他的观点多年处于边缘。

1960年，受过建筑学训练、在华盛顿工作的塔季扬娜·普罗斯库里亚科夫注意到，彼德拉斯内格拉斯的石碑可以分成若干组，每组恰好跨越一个人的一生，有出生日期、即位日期和死亡日期。这些石碑原来是国王们的历史。

1973年12月，包括画家琳达·谢勒、语言学家弗洛伊德·朗斯伯里和学生彼得·马修斯在内的一小群人在帕伦克聚会。他们在一个下午就理出了巴加尔及其继承者的王朝世系，两个世纪的国王都有了名字和年代。如今，约90%的古典期玛雅文献已能够释读。

summary.en: On 1 January 1994, the day the North American Free Trade Agreement took effect, the Zapatista Army of National Liberation (EZLN), mostly Tzotzil and Tzeltal Maya, seized San Cristóbal de las Casas and other towns in Chiapas. After twelve days of fighting a ceasefire began a long negotiation over Indigenous rights and autonomy.
summary.zh: 1994年1月1日，即《北美自由贸易协定》生效当天，以佐齐尔和泽套玛雅人为主的萨帕塔民族解放军占领了恰帕斯州的圣克里斯托瓦尔-德拉斯卡萨斯等城镇。经过十二天战斗后实现停火，随后围绕原住民权利与自治展开了长期谈判。

sources.title: Neil Harvey, The Chiapas Rebellion: The Struggle for Land and Democracy (1998)
George A. Collier, Basta! Land and the Zapatista Rebellion in Chiapas (3rd ed., 2005)
Wikipedia: Zapatista uprising

story.en:
As Mexico's elite celebrated the New Year and entry into NAFTA, some 3,000 masked rebels, many armed only with sticks or old rifles, walked into San Cristóbal de las Casas and occupied the town hall. From its balcony they read the First Declaration of the Lacandon Jungle, declaring war on the "illegitimate" government of Carlos Salinas and demanding "work, land, housing, food, health, education, independence, freedom, democracy, justice and peace". They called NAFTA "a death sentence for Indigenous peoples" because it accompanied the end of land redistribution under Article 27.

The army counter-attacked and about 150 people died, many in the market town of Ocosingo. But the rebels' spokesman, a pipe-smoking, balaclava-wearing mestizo called Subcomandante Marcos, wrote witty communiqués that made the movement famous around the world, and huge protests in Mexico City forced a ceasefire on 12 January.

The San Andrés Accords on Indigenous rights were signed in 1996 but never fully enacted. The Zapatistas withdrew into autonomous communities, the caracoles, with their own schools, clinics and "good government councils", which continue today.
story.zh:
当墨西哥精英们庆祝新年和加入北美自由贸易区时，约3000名蒙面起义者（许多人只拿着木棍或旧步枪）走进圣克里斯托瓦尔-德拉斯卡萨斯，占领了市政厅。他们在市政厅阳台上宣读了《拉坎冬丛林第一宣言》，向卡洛斯·萨利纳斯的“非法”政府宣战，要求“工作、土地、住房、食物、医疗、教育、独立、自由、民主、正义与和平”。他们称北美自由贸易协定是“对原住民的死刑判决”，因为与之相伴的是宪法第27条下土地再分配的终结。

军队发动反击，约150人死亡，许多人死在集镇奥科辛戈。但起义军的发言人、叼着烟斗、戴着面罩的梅斯蒂索人“副司令马科斯”撰写的妙趣横生的公报使这场运动闻名世界，墨西哥城的大规模抗议迫使政府于1月12日停火。

关于原住民权利的《圣安德烈斯协议》于1996年签署，但从未得到全面实施。萨帕塔人退回自治社区“蜗牛”，建立了自己的学校、诊所和“善治委员会”，延续至今。

summary.en: In late October 1998 Hurricane Mitch stalled over Honduras and Nicaragua, dropping up to 1,900 mm of rain. Floods and landslides, including the collapse of the Casita volcano's flank that buried villages near Posoltega, killed about 11,000 people and left thousands missing, the deadliest Atlantic hurricane in two centuries.
summary.zh: 1998年10月下旬，米奇飓风在洪都拉斯和尼加拉瓜上空停滞，降雨量高达1900毫米。洪水和山体滑坡（包括卡西塔火山侧翼崩塌，掩埋了波索尔特加附近的村庄）造成约1.1万人死亡、数千人失踪，是两个世纪以来死亡人数最多的大西洋飓风。

sources.title: US National Hurricane Center: Preliminary Report, Hurricane Mitch (1999)
Wikipedia: Hurricane Mitch

note: Marker at Tegucigalpa, where much of the city was destroyed by the flooding of the Choluteca River.

summary.en: On 12 January 2010 a magnitude 7.0 earthquake with its epicentre near Léogâne, 25 km west of Port-au-Prince, destroyed much of the capital, including the National Palace and cathedral. Estimates of the dead range from about 100,000 to the Haitian government's 316,000. A cholera epidemic introduced by UN peacekeepers followed in October.
summary.zh: 2010年1月12日，震中位于太子港以西25公里莱奥甘附近的7.0级地震摧毁了首都大部分地区，包括国家宫和大教堂。死亡人数估计从约10万到海地政府公布的31.6万不等。同年10月，联合国维和人员带入的霍乱又引发了一场疫情。

sources.title: US Geological Survey: M 7.0 – Haiti Region, 2010-01-12
Jonathan M. Katz, The Big Truck That Went By: How the World Came to Save Haiti and Left Behind a Disaster (2013)
Wikipedia: 2010 Haiti earthquake

note: The death toll is uncertain and politically disputed.

story.en:
The shaking began at 4:53 in the afternoon and lasted about 35 seconds. Port-au-Prince, a city of nearly three million crowded into ravines and hillsides, had grown without building codes; concrete-block houses pancaked by the tens of thousands. The National Palace's white domes folded, the cathedral and the main prison collapsed, and the headquarters of the UN mission fell, killing its chief, Hédi Annabi. About 1.5 million people ended up in tent camps.

The world responded with pledges of more than 10 billion dollars, but much of the money went to foreign contractors and NGOs rather than the Haitian state, and reconstruction stalled. In October 2010 cholera, unknown in Haiti for at least a century, broke out downstream of a base where Nepalese peacekeepers' sewage leaked into the Artibonite River; it killed nearly 10,000 people. The UN apologised in 2016.

The journalist Jonathan Katz, who was in Port-au-Prince that day, described how aid workers and journalists overestimated looting and violence, while Haitians themselves did most of the rescuing in the first hours.
story.zh:
震动始于下午4时53分，持续约35秒。近300万人口挤在沟壑和山坡上的太子港，在没有建筑规范的情况下发展起来；成千上万的混凝土砌块房屋层层坍塌。国家宫的白色穹顶折叠下来，大教堂和中央监狱倒塌，联合国特派团总部也坍塌了，团长赫迪·安纳比遇难。约150万人最终住进帐篷营地。

世界各国认捐了100多亿美元，但大部分资金流向外国承包商和非政府组织，而非海地政府，重建陷入停滞。2010年10月，至少一个世纪未在海地出现的霍乱在一处基地下游暴发，那里尼泊尔维和人员的污水渗入了阿蒂博尼特河；疫情夺去近1万人的生命。联合国于2016年道歉。

当天身在太子港的记者乔纳森·卡茨描述说，援助人员和记者高估了抢劫和暴力，而在最初几个小时里，大部分救援工作其实是海地人自己完成的。

name.zh: 第13个“巴克顿”周期结束（2012年）

summary.en: On 21 December 2012 the Maya Long Count reached 13.0.0.0.0, completing 13 b'ak'tuns (about 5,125 years) since its mythical starting point in 3114 BCE. Popular culture spun it into an apocalypse; Maya scholars and communities pointed out that inscriptions such as Tortuguero Monument 6 saw it only as a calendar milestone.
summary.zh: 2012年12月21日，玛雅长纪历到达13.0.0.0.0，自公元前3114年那个神话起点以来走完了13个巴克顿（约5125年）。流行文化把它渲染为世界末日；玛雅学者和玛雅社群则指出，托尔图格罗6号碑等铭文只把它视为历法上的一个里程碑。

sources.title: David Stuart, The Order of Days: The Maya World and the Truth about 2012 (2011)
NASA: Why the World Didn't End Yesterday (2012)
Wikipedia: 2012 phenomenon

note: Marker near Tortuguero, Tabasco, whose 7th-century monument mentions the 2012 date.

summary.en: On 17 December 2014 Presidents Barack Obama and Raúl Castro announced the restoration of diplomatic relations after 54 years, following secret talks brokered by Canada and Pope Francis. Embassies reopened in 2015 and Obama visited Havana in March 2016, but the US embargo remained and many measures were reversed from 2017.
summary.zh: 2014年12月17日，在加拿大和教宗方济各斡旋的秘密谈判之后，巴拉克·奥巴马总统和劳尔·卡斯特罗宣布在中断54年后恢复外交关系。两国于2015年重开使馆，奥巴马于2016年3月访问哈瓦那，但美国的禁运依然存在，许多措施自2017年起被撤销。

sources.title: William M. LeoGrande & Peter Kornbluh, Back Channel to Cuba: The Hidden History of Negotiations between Washington and Havana (updated ed., 2015)
Wikipedia: Cuban thaw

summary.en: Hurricane Maria devastated Dominica as a Category 5 storm on 18 September 2017 and struck Puerto Rico two days later, destroying its electrical grid; much of the island was without power for months. A later study estimated about 2,975 excess deaths in Puerto Rico, far above the initial official count of 64.
summary.zh: 2017年9月18日，玛丽亚飓风以5级强度重创多米尼克，两天后袭击波多黎各，摧毁其电网，岛上大部分地区停电长达数月。后来的一项研究估计，波多黎各的超额死亡人数约为2975人，远高于最初官方公布的64人。

sources.title: George Washington University Milken Institute School of Public Health, Ascertainment of the Estimated Excess Mortality from Hurricane María in Puerto Rico (2018)
US National Hurricane Center: Tropical Cyclone Report, Hurricane Maria (2018)
Wikipedia: Hurricane Maria

name.en: Claudia Sheinbaum elected Mexico's first woman president
name.zh: 克劳迪娅·辛鲍姆当选墨西哥首位女总统

summary.en: In the election of 2 June 2024, Claudia Sheinbaum, a climate scientist and former head of government of Mexico City, won with about 60% of the vote, becoming the first woman president of Mexico when she took office on 1 October 2024.
summary.zh: 在2024年6月2日的大选中，气候科学家、前墨西哥城政府首脑克劳迪娅·辛鲍姆以约60%的得票率获胜，并于2024年10月1日就职，成为墨西哥首位女总统。

Reuters, "Claudia Sheinbaum wins Mexico presidency in landslide" (3 June 2024)
